### 系统要求
- Windows 11 版本 22000(21H2)或更高版本
- Mica 表面相关选项需要 Windows 11 版本 22621(22H2)或更高版本

### 已知限制
- 部分 Win32 控件在浅色/深色模式多次切换后可能残留旧颜色。这是 Windows 自身的限制(uxtheme/comctl32 内部缓存)，重启资源管理器即可解决。

### 常见问题

**这个模组会占用很多资源吗？**
日常使用中应当无感。所用的钩子(主题、颜色、文本)轻量且带缓存，避免重复调用开销较大的 shell/COM 接口，大多数功能仅在元素确实需要现代化时才执行额外代码。由于模组注入所有进程，始终存在少量拦截开销，但动画(指示条、图标、展开箭头)运行在各自的线程中，屏幕无变化时处于空闲状态(不消耗 CPU)。更复杂的功能(自定义字形图标、动画指示条)仅在你明确启用后才会产生开销。

**这个模组与其他模组兼容吗？例如 Translucent Windows：**
目前，本模组不保证与 Translucent Windows 等第三方透明度模组兼容，仅保证与本模组自身的透明度功能兼容。1.0.4 已移除外部透明度兼容选项。进程排除列表仍然可用，但仅排除深色模式，不会停用其他现代样式。

**某个程序在深色模式下颜色不对：**
使用深色模式排除列表，添加该程序的可执行文件名。

**我可以按需组合所有设置吗？**
可以。所有功能禁用时本模组几乎不做任何事，你可以自由组合其中的绝大多数。冲突组合没有自动警告——部分选项已在描述中说明其优先级(例如 Mica 表面优先于不透明色值)，因此同时开启多项前建议先阅读各项描述。

**DirectWrite 文本选项会改变什么？**
DirectWrite 是 Windows 的现代文本渲染器。旧版 Win32 界面通常使用 GDI ClearType，它利用 LCD 屏幕的红、绿、蓝子像素让文字看起来更锐利，通常也会稍显厚重；但这种方式可能产生彩色边缘，也不容易与透明或合成背景自然融合。本模组的这个选项专门使用 DirectWrite 的灰度抗锯齿：它用中性灰色透明度平滑文字，而不是使用彩色子像素，因此能与 Mica 等现代表面保持一致。刚开始看起来可能稍柔和或稍轻，这是正常现象，也是现代 WinUI 应用通常采用的文本风格。

**我用过的某个选项在设置里消失了**
1.0.3 版本合并了若干选项以保持列表简洁。复选框、单选按钮、分组标题与圆角选择背景现已并入**现代控件**；分组框边框并入**现代分隔线与分组框**；三个渐变开关合并为**强调色渐变填充**；组合框下拉列表由**现代菜单与下拉列表**覆盖，并共用其圆角样式。三个导航分隔线开关合并为单个**导航分隔线**选项，指示条及其动画样式合并为单个**导航窗格指示条**选项，ReBar 的仿 Mica 着色成为**现代化旧版 ReBar 控件**的着色取值，图钉图标样式并入**Fluent 图钉图标**。旧设置已被移除，因此你在其中的自定义现在跟随吸收它的那个设置——更新后值得检查一遍。圆角选择背景与圆角下拉列表在合并后默认启用。 **浅色模式现代滚动条**也已更名为**现代滚动条**，现在覆盖深浅两种模式，默认开启。自定义深色模式不再强制使用现代绘制：关闭该选项即可恢复原生滚动条，且仍为深色。

1.0.4 中，**菜单与下拉列表**包含原生或 WinUI 风格的上下文菜单尺寸，**属性窗口选项卡**包含单行布局，**应用强调色**合并界面和拖动选框着色。相关选项仍位于原来的分组中。旧开关的保存值仍会读取；选择新的下拉值后，它将优先于旧的附加设置。

**我关闭了资源管理器表面，但资源管理器仍显示 Mica**
退出 Mica 模式时，已打开窗口的背景材质也会被移除，恢复为资源管理器自身设置的窗口框架。如果某个已打开的窗口仍显示之前表面的残留，关闭它(或重启资源管理器)，它就会以新的表面重新打开。

**为什么打开/保存对话框也跟着变了？**
通用文件选择器有意跟随资源管理器表面，且没有单独的选项：它本就是同一个 Shell 视图，在 Mica 或不透明的资源管理器旁边保留默认色值会显得格格不入。将表面设为“关闭”，二者都会恢复系统外观。

**为什么控制面板没有 Mica？**
控制面板运行在独立的资源管理器进程中，使用旧版窗口框架，其页面从未针对半透明背景绘制：部分区域保持不透明，浅色模式下纯白区域尤为突兀。目前资源管理器表面会让该进程整体保持不透明，包括从控制面板窗口打开的文件夹；深色模式、文字颜色和标题下方的分隔线仍会生效。普通资源管理器窗口不受影响。

**基于 MMC 的程序(任务计划程序、计算机管理、组策略编辑器等)崩溃或显示异常**
自 1.0.3 版本起为实验性支持。若某个程序仍显示异常或运行不正常，请在 Windhawk 的高级设置中把 `mmc.exe` 加入本模组的 “Excluded programs” 列表(这与深色模式排除列表不同——后者只关闭着色，前者会完全阻止注入)。

**发现 Bug？程序运行异常？界面卡死？**
请在 GitHub 提交 Issue，附上你的设置并说明是哪个程序卡死。

**从深色模式切回浅色模式时，部分颜色未恢复：**
这是 Windows 旧版程序自身的限制(uxtheme/comctl32 内部缓存)，重启资源管理器即可解决。

**在 LTSC 或较早的 Windows 11 版本上，任务栏缩略图的工具提示显示为浅色背景上的白色文字：**
这些版本仍使用 Win32 窗口来显示任务栏缩略图及其工具提示。本模组加载时任务栏已经存在，因此只有在任务栏重新创建后才会应用自定义深色模式：请在启用本模组的情况下重启资源管理器。

**我发现深色模式改变了非原生程序的颜色：**
这是预期行为——本模组使用 SetSysColors 更改系统颜色，无法轻易按应用排除，因此任何向 Windows 查询系统颜色的程序都会拿到深色值。如需更精细的排除控制，请使用设置中的深色模式排除列表。在本模组未运行的程序中（在 Windhawk 中被排除，或无法注入的程序），经典对话框的标签可能会成为深色背景上的深色文字而难以阅读；请让模组在其中运行并将该程序加入深色模式排除列表，或关闭自定义深色模式。

**禁用或删除本模组后颜色仍然是深色：**
这是 Windows 快速启动(“混合关机”)的行为，并非本模组所能控制。快速启动会休眠内核会话而非真正重启，因此系统的实时颜色表(由 SetSysColors 设置)可能原封不动地熬过一次“关机 → 开机”。此外，Windows 还可能自行把当时生效的颜色保存到注册表的旧版配色方案(Control Panel\Colors)中，若已发生，即便真正重启也未必足够。解决办法：先执行一次真正的重启(而非“关机”)，或在电源选项中关闭快速启动；若颜色仍未恢复，请在“设置 > 个性化”中重新选择一个主题(或切换浅色/深色模式)，强制 Windows 从头重新定义颜色。

**在部分较旧的 32 位程序中，拖动插入线和磁盘使用图表仍是旧样式：**
列表视图的现代插入标记通过 comctl32 的一个绘制辅助函数实现，而该函数仅在 64 位进程中被拦截：在 32 位版本中它的调用约定是编译器的选择，可能随 Windows 更新而改变，贸然假定会破坏调用方的栈。树形视图在两种位数下都已现代化，而桌面始终是 64 位。驱动器属性中的磁盘使用环形图出于同样原因不在 32 位程序中启用：它在 shell32 和 wpdshext 中的绘制函数在那里通过寄存器传递参数，而这同样可能改变。

- **File Explorer WinUI-Like Content Animation** —— crazyboyybs
- **Smooth Scroll for Win32** —— crazyboyybs
- **Custom Menu Height** —— Kitsune
- **Translucent Windows** —— Undisputed00x
- **Window Border Customizer** —— Lockframe

Completo mostra o fundo atras do painel de navegacao, da lista de arquivos e da barra de status; com painel de conteudo a lista vira um painel mais claro sobre ele, translucido ou solido; opaco usa os mesmos tons WinUI sem fundo Mica. Sair de uma opcao Mica vale para janelas abertas depois.

// ── FPU Guard ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// D2D/D3D can change the FPU control word (single precision, masked exceptions).
// Programs like StartAllBack (Delphi) unmask FPU exceptions — any D2D call from
// our hooks corrupts their FPU state, causing "invalid floating point operation".
// FPUGuard saves/restores the FPU control word around D2D resource creation.
struct FPUGuard {
    unsigned int prev;
    FPUGuard()  { _controlfp_s(&prev, 0, 0); }
    ~FPUGuard() { _controlfp_s(nullptr, prev, _MCW_EM | _MCW_PC | _MCW_RC | _MCW_DN); }
};

// Settings are immutable after publication. Old snapshots stay alive until
// module teardown, so hot hooks need only one atomic pointer load and never
// contend with Wh_ModSettingsChanged or observe fields being overwritten.
static const Settings g_defaultSettings{};
static std::atomic<const Settings*> g_settingsCurrent{ &g_defaultSettings };
static std::mutex g_settingsPublishMutex;

// ============================================================================
// Timer infrastructure (high-resolution, QueryPerformanceCounter-based)
// ============================================================================

static DOUBLE g_recipCyclesPerSecond = 0.0;

static void TimerInitialize()
{
    LARGE_INTEGER freq;
    QueryPerformanceFrequency(&freq);
    g_recipCyclesPerSecond = 1.0 / static_cast<DOUBLE>(freq.QuadPart);
}

static DOUBLE TimerGetSeconds()
{
    LARGE_INTEGER T1;
    QueryPerformanceCounter(&T1);
    return static_cast<DOUBLE>(T1.QuadPart) * g_recipCyclesPerSecond;
}

// ============================================================================
// Theme class cache (avoids repeated uxtheme ordinal calls)
// ============================================================================

typedef HRESULT(WINAPI* GetThemeClass_t)(HTHEME, LPWSTR, INT);
static GetThemeClass_t pGetThemeClass = nullptr;

// HTHEME -> interned class name. Names are a small, process-lifetime set
// (uxtheme class list), so references handed out stay valid across every
// cache clear; g_themeClassCacheGen invalidates the per-thread front cache.
static std::unordered_map<HTHEME, const std::wstring*> g_themeClassCache;
static std::unordered_set<std::wstring> g_themeClassNames;
static std::mutex g_themeClassCacheMutex; // protects both containers
static std::atomic<uint32_t> g_themeClassCacheGen{ 1 };
static void ThemeClassCacheBump()
{
    g_themeClassCacheGen.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_release);
}

// Records the hwnd each HTHEME was actually opened with, captured directly
// from OpenThemeData_hook's own parameter -- reliable regardless of paint
// timing, unlike g_tlsPaintHwnd (only valid inside a BeginPaint bracket).
// Needed because GetThemeColor takes no HWND/HDC at all, so it's the only
// way to scope a per-window color override to a specific theme handle.
static std::unordered_map<HTHEME, HWND> g_themeOpenerHwnd;
static std::unordered_set<HTHEME> g_explorerScrollbarThemes;
static std::mutex g_themeOpenerHwndMutex;
static constexpr size_t kThemeOpenerHwndMax = 256;

struct ThemeOpenerInfo {
    HWND hwnd;
    bool explorerScrollbar;
};

static HWND GetThemeOpenerHwnd(HTHEME hTheme)
{
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(g_themeOpenerHwndMutex);
    auto it = g_themeOpenerHwnd.find(hTheme);
    return it != g_themeOpenerHwnd.end() ? it->second : nullptr;
}

static ThemeOpenerInfo GetThemeOpenerInfo(HTHEME hTheme)
{
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(g_themeOpenerHwndMutex);
    auto it = g_themeOpenerHwnd.find(hTheme);
    return {
        it != g_themeOpenerHwnd.end() ? it->second : nullptr,
        g_explorerScrollbarThemes.contains(hTheme),
    };
}

static void MarkThemeAsExplorerScrollbar(HTHEME hTheme)
{
    if (!hTheme) return;
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(g_themeOpenerHwndMutex);
    if (g_explorerScrollbarThemes.size() >= kThemeOpenerHwndMax &&
        !g_explorerScrollbarThemes.contains(hTheme)) {
        g_explorerScrollbarThemes.clear();
    }
    g_explorerScrollbarThemes.insert(hTheme);
}

// Shared by both OpenThemeData_hook's normal path and its thread_local
// reentrancy-guard early-return path, so an HTHEME opened by a recursive
// OpenThemeData call (uxtheme opening a sub-theme from inside its own
// OpenThemeData_orig) still gets recorded instead of silently missing from
// the map -- GetThemeOpenerHwnd would otherwise fall back to the coarser
// themePaintHwnd heuristic for exactly that HTHEME.
static void RecordThemeOpenerHwnd(HTHEME hTheme, HWND hwnd)
{
    if (!hTheme || !hwnd) return;
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(g_themeOpenerHwndMutex);
    if (g_themeOpenerHwnd.size() >= kThemeOpenerHwndMax &&
        !g_themeOpenerHwnd.contains(hTheme)) {
        g_themeOpenerHwnd.clear();
        g_explorerScrollbarThemes.clear();
    }
    g_themeOpenerHwnd[hTheme] = hwnd;
}

struct ThemeClassFrontEntry { HTHEME theme; uint32_t generation; const std::wstring* cls; };
static thread_local ThemeClassFrontEntry g_themeClassFront[64];

// Interns under g_themeClassCacheMutex. The set is never cleared (pointers
// are held by every thread's front cache); past the cap the name is returned
// uncached through a per-thread scratch string (in the FLS cache) instead.
static const std::wstring* InternThemeClassLocked(const wchar_t* name)
{
    constexpr size_t kThemeClassNamesMax = 256;
    auto it = g_themeClassNames.find(name);
    if (it != g_themeClassNames.end()) return &*it;
    if (g_themeClassNames.size() >= kThemeClassNamesMax) return nullptr;
    return &*g_themeClassNames.emplace(name).first;
}

// The thread's scratch string in the FLS cache (defined with it below).
static std::wstring* ThreadThemeClassScratch();

static const std::wstring& GetCachedThemeClass(HTHEME hTheme)
{
    static const std::wstring kNoClass;
    if (!pGetThemeClass) {
        HMODULE hUx = GetModuleHandleW(L"uxtheme.dll");
        if (hUx) {
            pGetThemeClass = (GetThemeClass_t)GetProcAddress(hUx, "GetThemeClass");
            if (!pGetThemeClass)
                pGetThemeClass = (GetThemeClass_t)GetProcAddress(hUx, MAKEINTRESOURCEA(74));
        }
        if (!pGetThemeClass) return kNoClass;
    }

    const uint32_t generation = g_themeClassCacheGen.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
    ThemeClassFrontEntry& slot =
        g_themeClassFront[(reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(hTheme) >> 4) & 63];
    if (slot.theme == hTheme && slot.generation == generation && slot.cls)
        return *slot.cls;

    const std::wstring* cls = nullptr;
    {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(g_themeClassCacheMutex);
        auto it = g_themeClassCache.find(hTheme);
        if (it != g_themeClassCache.end()) {
            cls = it->second;
        } else {
            // Bulk-cleared on theme change and per handle in CloseThemeData;
            // the cap only guards against handles closed behind our back.
            constexpr size_t kThemeClassCacheMax = 256;
            if (g_themeClassCache.size() >= kThemeClassCacheMax)
                g_themeClassCache.clear();
            WCHAR buf[256] = {};
            if (SUCCEEDED(pGetThemeClass(hTheme, buf, 256))) {
                cls = InternThemeClassLocked(buf);
                if (!cls) {
                    std::wstring* scratch = ThreadThemeClassScratch();
                    if (!scratch)
                        return kNoClass;
                    *scratch = buf;
                    return *scratch;
                }
            } else {
                cls = &kNoClass;
            }
            g_themeClassCache[hTheme] = cls;
        }
    }
    slot = { hTheme, generation, cls };
    return *cls;
}

// The default app mode (Settings > Personalization > Colors), which Explorer
// and apps with a native dark mode follow -- not the Windows mode of the
// taskbar and Start. uxtheme's ordinal 138 (ShouldSystemUseDarkMode) reads
// the latter (SystemUsesLightTheme), and ordinal 132 answers from this
// process's own SetPreferredAppMode, which this mod sets, so the value is
// read directly. Missing means light, the Windows default. Paint paths use
// IsSystemDarkMode(), which caches this until the next theme change.
static bool ReadSystemDarkModeFromRegistry()
{
    DWORD appsUseLightTheme = 1;
    DWORD size = sizeof(appsUseLightTheme);
    if (RegGetValueW(HKEY_CURRENT_USER,
            L"Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Themes\\Personalize",
            L"AppsUseLightTheme", RRF_RT_REG_DWORD, nullptr,
            &appsUseLightTheme, &size) != ERROR_SUCCESS) {
        return false;
    }
    return appsUseLightTheme == 0;
}

static bool IsSystemDarkMode();

// A contrast theme owns every color: the app mode can still read dark under
// one, and the dark palette would replace the user's contrast colors.
static bool ShouldCustomDarkModeBeActive()
{
    return g_settings.EnableDarkMode && IsSystemDarkMode() &&
           !SysHighContrastEnabled();
}

static bool IsSystemTransparencyEnabled()
{
    // Atomic: can be called from whichever thread is painting a #32768
    // popup, and different popups in the same process can be on different
    // UI threads.
    static std::atomic<DWORD> s_lastCheck{ 0 };
    static std::atomic<bool>  s_enabled{ true };

    DWORD now = GetTickCount();
    DWORD last = s_lastCheck.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
    if (last && now - last < 2000)
        return s_enabled.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
    s_lastCheck.store(now, std::memory_order_relaxed);

    BOOL composition = FALSE;
    if (FAILED(DwmIsCompositionEnabled(&composition)) || !composition) {
        s_enabled.store(false, std::memory_order_relaxed);
        return false;
    }

    HKEY hKey = nullptr;
    DWORD val = 1;
    if (RegOpenKeyExW(HKEY_CURRENT_USER,
        L"Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Themes\\Personalize",
        0, KEY_READ, &hKey) == ERROR_SUCCESS)
    {
        DWORD size = sizeof(val);
        RegQueryValueExW(hKey, L"EnableTransparency", nullptr, nullptr,
                         reinterpret_cast<LPBYTE>(&val), &size);
        RegCloseKey(hKey);
    }

    bool enabled = (val != 0);
    s_enabled.store(enabled, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    return enabled;
}

// Per-window dark mode via DWMWA_USE_IMMERSIVE_DARK_MODE=20.
// Falls back to system-wide IsSystemDarkMode() for NULL hwnd (buffered DCs).

static bool ReadAccentPalette(BYTE* palette, DWORD paletteSize)
{
    HKEY hKey;
    if (RegOpenKeyExW(HKEY_CURRENT_USER,
        L"Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Explorer\\Accent",
        0, KEY_READ, &hKey) == ERROR_SUCCESS)
    {
        DWORD size = paletteSize;
        bool ok = (RegQueryValueExW(hKey, L"AccentPalette", nullptr, nullptr,
                                    palette, &size) == ERROR_SUCCESS);
        RegCloseKey(hKey);
        return ok;
    }
    return false;
}

// AccentPalette layout: [Light3=0, Light2=4, Light1=8, Base=12, Dark1=16, Dark2=20, Dark3=24]
// Each entry: R, G, B, padding (4 bytes)

// Generate a full 7-shade palette from a single base color via linear interpolation.
static void GenerateCustomPalette(COLORREF base, BYTE* palette)
{
    const BYTE bR = GetRValue(base), bG = GetGValue(base), bB = GetBValue(base);
    auto lerp = [](BYTE a, BYTE b, float t) -> BYTE {
        return (BYTE)(a + (b - a) * t);
    };
    auto set = [&](int off, BYTE tR, BYTE tG, BYTE tB, float t) {
        palette[off] = lerp(bR, tR, t);
        palette[off+1] = lerp(bG, tG, t);
        palette[off+2] = lerp(bB, tB, t);
        palette[off+3] = 0;
    };
    set(0,  255,255,255, 0.60f); // Light3
    set(4,  255,255,255, 0.40f); // Light2
    set(8,  255,255,255, 0.20f); // Light1
    palette[12] = bR; palette[13] = bG; palette[14] = bB; palette[15] = 0; // Base
    set(16, 0,0,0, 0.20f);      // Dark1
    set(20, 0,0,0, 0.40f);      // Dark2
    set(24, 0,0,0, 0.60f);      // Dark3
    palette[28] = palette[29] = palette[30] = palette[31] = 0;
}

// The palette is read once per invalidation (accent/theme/settings change),
// never per call: GetSysColor and most paint hooks land here on every paint
// in every process, and the registry read alone costs ~13 us.
static std::mutex               g_accentPaletteMutex;
static std::atomic<bool>        g_accentPaletteDirty{ true };
static std::atomic<bool>        g_accentPaletteValid{ false };
static std::atomic<COLORREF>    g_accentPaletteColors[8] = {};

static void AccentPaletteInvalidate()
{
    g_accentPaletteDirty.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
}

static void AccentPaletteRefresh()
{
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(g_accentPaletteMutex);
    if (!g_accentPaletteDirty.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)) return;
    BYTE palette[32] = {};
    bool valid = true;
    if (g_settings.CustomAccentColorSet)
        GenerateCustomPalette(g_settings.CustomAccentColor, palette);
    else
        valid = ReadAccentPalette(palette, sizeof(palette));
    if (valid) {
        for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) {
            g_accentPaletteColors[i].store(
                RGB(palette[i * 4], palette[i * 4 + 1], palette[i * 4 + 2]),
                std::memory_order_relaxed);
        }
    }
    g_accentPaletteValid.store(valid, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    g_accentPaletteDirty.store(false, std::memory_order_release);
}

static COLORREF GetAccentFromPalette(int offset)
{
    if (g_accentPaletteDirty.load(std::memory_order_acquire))
        AccentPaletteRefresh();
    if (g_accentPaletteValid.load(std::memory_order_acquire) &&
        offset >= 0 && offset < 32 && (offset & 3) == 0) {
        return g_accentPaletteColors[offset / 4].load(
            std::memory_order_relaxed);
    }
    DWORD color = 0; BOOL opaque = FALSE;
    if (SUCCEEDED(DwmGetColorizationColor(&color, &opaque)))
        return RGB((color >> 16) & 0xFF, (color >> 8) & 0xFF, color & 0xFF);
    return GetSysColor(COLOR_HOTLIGHT);
}

// AccentFillColorDefault: Light2 in dark, Dark1 in light. Per-window
// callers pass their own dark flag; GetAccentIndicator below is the same
// lookup keyed off the system theme, for callers with no window.
static COLORREF GetAccentFillDefault(bool dark)
{
    return GetAccentFromPalette(dark ? 4 : 16);
}

// Cached "Base" palette entry (offset 12) for the pill's optional gradient
// fill. Invalidated by UpdateThemeColors().
static std::atomic<bool>     g_accentBaseCacheDirty{ true };
static std::atomic<COLORREF> g_cachedAccentBase{ 0 };

static COLORREF GetCachedAccentBase()
{
    if (g_accentBaseCacheDirty.load(std::memory_order_acquire))
    {
        g_cachedAccentBase.store(GetAccentFromPalette(12), std::memory_order_relaxed);
        g_accentBaseCacheDirty.store(false, std::memory_order_release);
    }
    return g_cachedAccentBase.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
}

// Accent indicator color — the authoritative selection/pill color per mode.
// Returns from the cache; RefreshAccentCache() must be called on theme change.
// SKILL: group 1 (Light2, offset 4) dark / group 4 (Dark1, offset 16) light.
// ── Accent / SysColor state ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Cached per-mode accent indicator color.
// Offset 4 (Light2) in dark mode, offset 16 (Dark1) in light mode.
// Invalidated by UpdateThemeColors() on WM_SETTINGCHANGE / WM_THEMECHANGED.
static std::atomic<bool>     g_accentCacheDirty{ true };
static std::atomic<bool>     g_cachedIsDark{ true };
static std::atomic<COLORREF> g_cachedIndicator{ RGB(0x40,0x8E,0xC8) }; // fallback
static std::mutex            g_accentCacheMutex;
static std::atomic<uint64_t> g_tabTextMetricGeneration{ 1 };

// Double-checked locking: atomic flag check on the hot path (no lock),
// mutex only on the dirty path to prevent redundant registry reads and
// guarantee g_cachedIsDark + g_cachedIndicator are always written as a pair.
static void RefreshAccentCache()
{
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(g_accentCacheMutex);
    // Cleared before the read, inside the lock: a theme change that marks
    // the cache dirty while this refresh reads the old values then forces
    // the next caller to read again, instead of being lost.
    if (!g_accentCacheDirty.exchange(false, std::memory_order_acq_rel)) return;
    bool dark = ReadSystemDarkModeFromRegistry();
    COLORREF c = GetAccentFillDefault(dark);
    g_cachedIsDark.store(dark, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    g_cachedIndicator.store(c, std::memory_order_relaxed);
}

// The app mode as of the last theme change: refreshed with the accent cache,
// which every WM_SETTINGCHANGE/WM_THEMECHANGED handler marks dirty.
static bool IsSystemDarkMode()
{
    if (g_accentCacheDirty.load(std::memory_order_acquire))
        RefreshAccentCache();
    return g_cachedIsDark.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
}

static COLORREF GetAccentIndicator()
{
    // Lazy refresh: first call after dirty mark re-reads registry once.
    if (g_accentCacheDirty.load(std::memory_order_acquire))
        RefreshAccentCache();
    return g_cachedIndicator.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
}

static D2D1_COLOR_F GetAccentIndicatorD2D()
{
    COLORREF c = GetAccentIndicator();
    return D2D1::ColorF(GetRValue(c)/255.f, GetGValue(c)/255.f, GetBValue(c)/255.f);
}

// For non-indicator accent use (AccentColorize/AccentMarquee)
static COLORREF GetSystemAccentColor()
{
    if (g_accentCacheDirty.load(std::memory_order_acquire))
        RefreshAccentCache();
    bool dark = g_cachedIsDark.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
    return GetAccentFromPalette(dark ? 8 : 12);
}

// A translucent token flattened over an opaque one, the way XAML composes
// it on a solid surface (per channel, rounded).
constexpr COLORREF FlattenOver(Color fg, COLORREF bg)
{
    const auto mix = [](int f, int b, int a) constexpr {
        return (f * a + b * (0xFF - a) + 0x7F) / 0xFF;
    };
    return RGB(mix(GetRValue(fg.rgb), GetRValue(bg), fg.alpha),
               mix(GetGValue(fg.rgb), GetGValue(bg), fg.alpha),
               mix(GetBValue(fg.rgb), GetBValue(bg), fg.alpha));
}

// Tooltips, context menus and the drag label are the same kind of small
// floating surface, and Windows gives them the same two colors.
//
// The solid is AcrylicInAppFillColorDefaultBrush's FallbackColor -- what the
// surface collapses to when transparency is off, and what a color picker
// reads off these windows: #2C2C2C dark, #F9F9F9 light. Both happen to sit in
// the token table already, one step apart in the solid background ramp.
static COLORREF WinUiFloatingSurfaceColor(bool dark)
{
    return dark ? WinUI::Dark::SolidBackgroundFillColorQuarternary.rgb
                : WinUI::Light::SolidBackgroundFillColorTertiary.rgb;
}

// Their hairline: ControlStrokeColorDefault over that solid -- #3B3B3B dark,
// #EAEAEA light, which is what these surfaces show with transparency off and
// nothing to compose against. Not DividerStrokeColorDefault, which this used
// first: the two share the light value, black at 0x0F, but the divider is
// white at 0x15 in dark against this one's 0x12, and the measured edge is
// #3B3B3B rather than the #3D3D3D that would give. Separators keep the
// divider token -- a divider and the edge of a surface are not the same
// hairline, and only here do the numbers say so.
static COLORREF WinUiFloatingSurfaceStroke(bool dark)
{
    return WinUI::FlattenOver(WinUI::ControlStrokeColorDefault(dark),
                              WinUiFloatingSurfaceColor(dark));
}

static WinUI::Color NavigationItemFillColor(bool dark, bool neutral,
    COLORREF accent, bool selected, bool hot, bool pressed)
{
    WinUI::Color fill = WinUI::SubtleFillColorTransparent(dark);
    if (selected || hot || pressed) {
        const bool tertiary = selected ? (hot && !pressed) : pressed;
        fill = tertiary ? WinUI::SubtleFillColorTertiary(dark)
                        : WinUI::SubtleFillColorSecondary(dark);
    }
    if (!neutral)
        fill.rgb = accent;
    return fill;
}

static WinUI::Color NavigationItemForegroundColor(bool dark, bool neutral,
    COLORREF base, bool pressed)
{
    WinUI::Color foreground = pressed ? WinUI::TextFillColorSecondary(dark)
                                     : WinUI::TextFillColorPrimary(dark);
    if (!neutral)
        foreground.rgb = base;
    return foreground;
}

// Defined later in the file (NavDivider section) -- reused as-is here rather
// than duplicating an EnumChildWindows walk. Resolves hwnd's own root and
// checks whether it IS or CONTAINS a NamespaceTreeControl, caching a
// positive answer as a prop on the root window (no separate map/eviction
// needed: the prop dies with the window, so a reused HWND value can't read
// a stale hit). cacheNegative=false here: see this call site's own use
// below for why a miss must NOT be cached permanently for a paint-hot-path
// caller like this one.
static bool NavDividerRootContainsNamespaceTree(HWND hwnd, bool cacheNegative = true);

// True if hwnd's top-level ancestor is a #32770 common-dialog window that
// hosts a NamespaceTreeControl nav pane (e.g. a modern Explorer-style file
// picker's Open/Save dialog), in a process on the dark-mode exclusion list.
// The NamespaceTreeControl requirement -- the same ancestry signal
// GlyphIsNavPaneTreeView/the old TryForceDarkExcludedFilePicker both used --
// is deliberate: without it, this would match ANY #32770 dialog in an
// excluded process (a plain MessageBox, a Find/Replace dialog, a
// Preferences screen), which is a much bigger surface than "the file
// picker" and was never the intent. Used to keep such dialogs fully native
// -- colors, glyph icons, shell-icon replacement, Explorer-family control
// styling -- so an excluded process's file picker behaves exactly like the
// rest of that process already does under the exclusion, with no partial
// theming.
static bool IsInsideExcludedFilePicker(HWND hwnd)
{
    if (!g_darkModeExcluded || !hwnd) return false;
    HWND root = GetAncestor(hwnd, GA_ROOT);
    if (!root) return false;
    wchar_t rootCls[64] = {};
    if (!GetClassNameW(root, rootCls, ARRAYSIZE(rootCls)) ||
        _wcsicmp(rootCls, L"#32770") != 0)
        return false;
    // cacheNegative=false: this runs from paint hot paths and can fire
    // before the picker's NamespaceTreeControl nav pane finishes
    // constructing -- an uncached miss just re-walks (cheaply, since few
    // children exist yet) until the tree actually appears, instead of
    // permanently deciding "not a file picker" from a too-early first paint.
    return NavDividerRootContainsNamespaceTree(root, /*cacheNegative=*/false);
}

// (ExplorerMicaBackdrop 1..3) its root gets the DWM backdrop, extended
// down to the file list's bottom (FilePickerApplyBackdrop), and the
// surfaces there erase to black (GDI leaves alpha 0, DWM composes the
// backdrop) the way Explorer's do -- nav pane and toolbar band on the
// backdrop, the list on the pane reveal / solid shade, CardStroke rules.
// Mode 4 keeps the same zones and matching scrollbars on opaque shades.
// The file-name area below and the rebar stay opaque in every mode.
static bool IsCurrentProcessExplorer();

// The explorer.exe hosting Control Panel (/factory,{5BD95610-...}): server
// mode 6, the value ExplorerFrame's IsControlPanelProcess and
// CExplorerFrame::ShouldShowTabs test to give its windows the legacy frame
// (no tabs, no WinUI island); the main Explorer runs in mode 3. Its pages and
// that frame are drawn for an opaque window, so the backdrop setting reads as
// off in the whole process. windows.storage exports an accessor returning
// the mode's address; the value is read on every call, as Explorer sets it
// after the mod starts.
static bool IsControlPanelHostProcess()
{
    using ServerModeAccessor = const int* (*)();
    static std::atomic<const int*> serverMode{nullptr};
    const int* mode = serverMode.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
    if (!mode) {
        if (!IsCurrentProcessExplorer())
            return false;
        HMODULE storage = GetModuleHandleW(L"windows.storage.dll");
        auto accessor = storage ? reinterpret_cast<ServerModeAccessor>(
            GetProcAddress(storage, "Global_WindowsStorage_esServerMode")) : nullptr;
        mode = accessor ? accessor() : nullptr;
        if (!mode)
            return false;
        serverMode.store(mode, std::memory_order_release);
    }
    return *mode == 6;
}

// ExplorerMicaBackdrop as it applies to the current process.
static int ExplorerBackdropMode()
{
    const int mode = g_settings.ExplorerMicaBackdrop;
    return mode && IsControlPanelHostProcess() ? 0 : mode;
}

// monitor DPI while the window DC stays at 96, so a pixel round trip through
// that DC (RepairOpaqueHdcAlpha) resamples the text over itself. Only a
// window's context carries the GDI scaling flag; the process and thread
// contexts report plain unaware (measured), so the first window of an
// unaware thread decides, once.
static BOOL CALLBACK GdiScaledFirstWindowProc(HWND hwnd, LPARAM lParam)
{
    *reinterpret_cast<HWND*>(lParam) = hwnd;
    return FALSE;
}

static bool IsGdiScaledProcess()
{
    static std::atomic<int> state{-1};
    const int known = state.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
    if (known >= 0)
        return known != 0;
    if (!AreDpiAwarenessContextsEqual(GetThreadDpiAwarenessContext(),
            DPI_AWARENESS_CONTEXT_UNAWARE)) {
        state.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
        return false;
    }
    HWND window = nullptr;
    EnumThreadWindows(GetCurrentThreadId(), GdiScaledFirstWindowProc,
                      reinterpret_cast<LPARAM>(&window));
    if (!window)
        return false;
    const bool gdiScaled = AreDpiAwarenessContextsEqual(
        GetWindowDpiAwarenessContext(window),
        DPI_AWARENESS_CONTEXT_UNAWARE_GDISCALED);
    state.store(gdiScaled ? 1 : 0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    return gdiScaled;
}

// Not in GDI-scaled processes: the picker's opaque chrome inside the
// extended frame depends on that alpha round trip.
static bool FilePickerMicaActive()
{
    const int mode = ExplorerBackdropMode();
    return mode >= 1 && mode <= 3 && !IsGdiScaledProcess();
}

static bool FilePickerChromeEnabled()
{
    if (g_darkModeExcluded)
        return false;
    return g_darkModeActive || FilePickerMicaActive() ||
           ExplorerOpaqueMode() ||
           (g_settings.ModernSeparators && !IsSystemDarkMode());
}

// Under Mica the chrome takes the status bar's secondary reveal shade.
static COLORREF FilePickerChromeColor(bool dark)
{
    if (FilePickerMicaActive())
        return ExplorerMicaSecondaryRevealColor(dark);
    return dark ? kFilePickerChromeDark : kFilePickerChromeLight;
}

// The opaque file-name area and what its controls compose against: under
// Mica the secondary Mica base WinUI's status bar text is flattened
// against (see ExplorerMicaStatusBarTextColor), the chrome shade otherwise.
static COLORREF FilePickerControlBackground(bool dark)
{
    if (FilePickerMicaActive())
        return dark ? RGB(0x2C, 0x2C, 0x2C) : RGB(0xFB, 0xFB, 0xFB);
    return FilePickerChromeColor(dark);
}

// The picker's nav pane (DirectUI ProperTree module, its NamespaceTreeControl
// tree and that tree's scrollbar): the Win32 dark base, light
// SolidBackgroundFillColorTertiary.
static constexpr COLORREF kFilePickerPaneDark  = ExplorerDarkColor;
static constexpr COLORREF kFilePickerPaneLight = WinUI::Light::SolidBackgroundFillColorTertiary;
// Dark only: the file list lifts to SolidBackgroundFillColorBase over the
// pane (ItemsView FILLCOLOR + the list's scrollbars); light keeps the
// native white list.
static constexpr COLORREF kFilePickerContentDark = WinUI::Dark::SolidBackgroundFillColorBase;

static COLORREF FilePickerPaneColor(bool dark)
{
    if (FilePickerMicaActive())
        return RGB(0, 0, 0);
    return dark ? kFilePickerPaneDark : kFilePickerPaneLight;
}

// The file list's background: the content shade in the mod's dark mode,
// the Explorer pane reveal / solid shade under Mica (black for full Mica).
static COLORREF FilePickerListColor(bool dark)
{
    if (FilePickerMicaActive())
        return ExplorerBackdropMode() >= 2
            ? ExplorerMicaPaneRevealColor(dark) : RGB(0, 0, 0);
    return dark ? kFilePickerContentDark : kExplorerListLight;
}

// Lifted list (dark mode, any real Mica mode, or the opaque surface mode).
static bool FilePickerListShaded()
{
    return FilePickerMicaActive() || ExplorerOpaqueMode() || g_darkModeActive;
}

// The picker's list root fill is rewritten after DirectUI paints it when
// the theme answer can't reach it: solid modes (opaque tiles) in both
// themes, and the light theme's reveal (logged: the light list paints its
// root white from a source other than the ItemsView FILLCOLOR; the dark
// theme's own fill already is the answered reveal).
static bool FilePickerListFillRewritten()
{
    return FilePickerMicaActive() &&
           (ExplorerBackdropMode() == 3 || !g_darkModeActive);
}

// The picker's rules: CardStroke pixels for DWM where the frame is
// extended (band bottom, splitter), WinUI's DividerStrokeColorDefault
// blended onto the opaque surfaces otherwise (the rows at and below the
// view's bottom, and everything without Mica).
static void FilePickerRule(HDC hdc, const RECT& line, bool composited)
{
    if (composited && FilePickerMicaActive())
        WriteExplorerMicaCardStrokePixels(hdc, line);
    else
        BlendPremultipliedPixels(hdc, line,
            g_darkModeActive ? 0x15151515u : 0x0F000000u);
}

// The common file picker dialog owning hwnd, or null: a #32770 root with a
// direct DUIViewWndClassName child (the view host; the cheap pre-check)
// and a NamespaceTreeControl somewhere below (uncached negative, the tree
// is built after the view). Explorer's own windows (CabinetWClass roots),
// its property sheets and the folder browser (#32770 with a tree but no
// view host) never match. Text scope uses this identity without enabling Mica.
static HWND FilePickerDialogRoot(HWND hwnd)
{
    if (!hwnd)
        return nullptr;
    HWND root = GetAncestor(hwnd, GA_ROOT);
    if (!root || !IsClassName(root, L"#32770") ||
        !FindWindowExW(root, nullptr, L"DUIViewWndClassName", nullptr) ||
        !NavDividerRootContainsNamespaceTree(root, /*cacheNegative=*/false))
        return nullptr;
    return root;
}

static HWND FilePickerRoot(HWND hwnd)
{
    return FilePickerChromeEnabled() ? FilePickerDialogRoot(hwnd) : nullptr;
}

static bool IsInsideShellFolderView(HWND hwnd);

// A window of the picker's file list (SHELLDLL_DefView subtree): the list's
// DirectUIHWND host or its ScrollBars.
static bool IsFilePickerListWindow(HWND hwnd)
{
    return FilePickerRoot(hwnd) && IsInsideShellFolderView(hwnd);
}

// The list's DirectUIHWND host of a picker being built: DefView child under
// a DUIViewWndClassName in a #32770 -- no namespace tree required, since
// the view is created before the nav pane and resolves its theme colors
// then (logged: the ItemsView FILLCOLOR queries come at creation, with
// only the host's own theme handle to tell them by).
static bool IsFilePickerListHost(HWND hwnd)
{
    if (!hwnd || !FilePickerChromeEnabled() || !IsClassName(hwnd, L"DirectUIHWND") ||
        !IsClassName(GetParent(hwnd), L"SHELLDLL_DefView"))
        return false;
    bool viewHost = false;
    for (HWND p = GetParent(hwnd); p && !viewHost; p = GetParent(p))
        viewHost = IsClassName(p, L"DUIViewWndClassName");
    HWND root = GetAncestor(hwnd, GA_ROOT);
    return viewHost && root && IsClassName(root, L"#32770");
}

// The windows the picker's view opens its ItemsView theme on (logged:
// the DUIViewWndClassName view host, then SHELLDLL_DefView), besides the
// list host itself.
static bool IsFilePickerViewThemeOpener(HWND hwnd)
{
    if (!hwnd || !FilePickerChromeEnabled())
        return false;
    if (IsFilePickerListHost(hwnd))
        return true;
    HWND root = GetAncestor(hwnd, GA_ROOT);
    if (!root || !IsClassName(root, L"#32770"))
        return false;
    if (IsClassName(hwnd, L"DUIViewWndClassName"))
        return GetParent(hwnd) == root;
    if (!IsClassName(hwnd, L"SHELLDLL_DefView"))
        return false;
    for (HWND p = GetParent(hwnd); p && p != root; p = GetParent(p))
        if (IsClassName(p, L"DUIViewWndClassName"))
            return true;
    return false;
}

// A picker nav pane window: its NamespaceTreeControl or that control's
// SysTreeView32 (background swapped at TVM_SETBKCOLOR in SendMessageW_hook,
// scrollbar told apart by FilePickerBracketSubclassProc).
static bool IsFilePickerNavPaneTree(HWND hwnd)
{
    if (!hwnd)
        return false;
    HWND host = hwnd;
    if (IsClassName(hwnd, L"SysTreeView32"))
        host = GetParent(hwnd);
    return host && IsClassName(host, L"NamespaceTreeControl") && FilePickerRoot(host);
}

// The picker root when hwnd is the dialog itself, a nested template dialog
// or a control of the file-name area: the parent chain reaches the root
// without crossing the view host (DUIViewWndClassName) or the rebar's
// WorkerW. Null elsewhere in the picker and for every other window.
static HWND FilePickerChromeRoot(HWND hwnd)
{
    HWND root = FilePickerRoot(hwnd);
    if (!root)
        return nullptr;
    for (HWND w = hwnd; w && w != root; w = GetParent(w)) {
        if (IsClassName(w, L"DUIViewWndClassName") || IsClassName(w, L"WorkerW"))
            return nullptr;
    }
    return root;
}

// Save templates can host their file-name/type controls inside the same
// DUIViewWndClassName as the folder view. They still sit on the chrome shade,
// but FilePickerChromeRoot intentionally rejects the whole DirectUI host so
// list/view controls don't inherit that shade. Distinguish only controls whose
// window begins below the actual SHELLDLL_DefView in screen coordinates.
static HWND FilePickerChromeBackgroundRoot(HWND hwnd)
{
    HWND root = FilePickerRoot(hwnd);
    if (!root)
        return nullptr;

    HWND viewHost = nullptr;
    for (HWND w = hwnd; w && w != root; w = GetParent(w)) {
        if (IsClassName(w, L"WorkerW"))
            return nullptr;
        if (IsClassName(w, L"DUIViewWndClassName")) {
            viewHost = w;
            break;
        }
    }
    if (!viewHost)
        return root;

    HWND duiHost = FindWindowExW(viewHost, nullptr, L"DirectUIHWND", nullptr);
    if (!duiHost)
        return nullptr;
    HWND defView = nullptr;
    for (HWND sink = FindWindowExW(duiHost, nullptr, L"CtrlNotifySink", nullptr);
         sink; sink = FindWindowExW(duiHost, sink, L"CtrlNotifySink", nullptr)) {
        defView = FindWindowExW(sink, nullptr, L"SHELLDLL_DefView", nullptr);
        if (defView)
            break;
    }

    RECT controlRect = {}, viewRect = {};
    return defView && IsWindowVisible(defView) &&
           GetWindowRect(hwnd, &controlRect) && GetWindowRect(defView, &viewRect) &&
           controlRect.top >= viewRect.bottom
        ? root : nullptr;
}

// Opaque dark-mode background fill color for corner/erase fills, aware of
// whether hwnd is inside an excluded process's file picker (native shade,
// kNativeExcludedPickerDarkBg), a property-sheet page (kElevatedPaneDark -- the
// same lighter elevated shade the page's own WM_CTLCOLORBTN/WM_ERASEBKGND
// background uses, so a button's corner cutout matches what's actually
// behind it there instead of the darker base shade), or the mod's own
// actively-styled dark window generally (Win32MainDark). Callers still gate
// this behind their own dark-mode check (DarkModeActiveForPaint/
// IsDarkForExcludedAwarePaint) -- this only picks which dark shade to use,
// not whether dark applies at all.
static bool IsCurrentProcessExplorer();
static bool IsCurrentProcessTaskManager();

static COLORREF DarkBgForPaint(HWND hwnd)
{
    if (IsInsideExcludedFilePicker(hwnd)) return kNativeExcludedPickerDarkBg;
    if (FilePickerChromeBackgroundRoot(hwnd)) return FilePickerControlBackground(true);
    if (IsInsidePropSheetPage(hwnd)) return kElevatedPaneDark;
    // File Explorer's views sit on the native list's shell shade (e.g. the
    // list's ScrollBar windows asking their DirectUI host).
    if (IsCurrentProcessExplorer() && IsInsideShellFolderView(hwnd))
        return ExplorerDarkColor;
    // Task Manager's DirectUI pages sit on that same shade: their host and
    // the HWND controls it holds under CtrlNotifySink (the lists' ScrollBar
    // windows).
    if (IsCurrentProcessTaskManager() && hwnd &&
        (IsClassName(hwnd, L"DirectUIHWND") ||
         IsClassName(GetParent(hwnd), L"CtrlNotifySink")))
        return ExplorerDarkColor;
    return Win32MainDark;
}

static std::mutex g_staticBrushCacheMutex;
static std::unordered_map<COLORREF, HBRUSH> g_staticBrushCache;
// The previous generation of brushes, deleted only when the cache fills
// again: a brush another thread (or a WM_CTLCOLOR* caller) is still using
// outlives the eviction that dropped it.
static std::vector<HBRUSH> g_retiredStaticBrushes;

static HBRUSH GetCachedSolidBrush(COLORREF color)
{
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(g_staticBrushCacheMutex);
    auto it = g_staticBrushCache.find(color);
    if (it != g_staticBrushCache.end())
        return it->second;

    // Some callers pass sampled or app-provided colors, so the set is
    // effectively unbounded -- cap the real GDI brush count (two generations)
    // instead of growing towards the per-process GDI object quota.
    constexpr size_t kStaticBrushCacheMax = 64;
    if (g_staticBrushCache.size() >= kStaticBrushCacheMax) {
        for (HBRUSH retired : g_retiredStaticBrushes)
            DeleteObject(retired);
        g_retiredStaticBrushes.clear();
        for (auto& kv : g_staticBrushCache)
            if (kv.second)
                g_retiredStaticBrushes.push_back(kv.second);
        g_staticBrushCache.clear();
    }

    HBRUSH brush = CreateSolidBrush(color);
    if (brush)
        g_staticBrushCache.emplace(color, brush);
    return brush;
}

// The two separator line colors DrawEdge_hook draws with; released together
// with the brush cache.
static HPEN g_drawEdgePens[2] = {};

static HPEN GetDrawEdgePen(bool dark)
{
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(g_staticBrushCacheMutex);
    HPEN& pen = g_drawEdgePens[dark ? 1 : 0];
    if (!pen)
        pen = CreatePen(PS_SOLID, 1, dark ? RGB(48, 48, 48) : RGB(224, 224, 224));
    return pen;
}

static void StaticBrushCacheClear()
{
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(g_staticBrushCacheMutex);
    for (auto& kv : g_staticBrushCache)
        if (kv.second)
            DeleteObject(kv.second);
    g_staticBrushCache.clear();
    for (HBRUSH retired : g_retiredStaticBrushes)
        DeleteObject(retired);
    g_retiredStaticBrushes.clear();
    g_retiredStaticBrushes.shrink_to_fit();
    for (HPEN& pen : g_drawEdgePens) {
        if (pen) DeleteObject(pen);
        pen = nullptr;
    }
}

// Set at the start of Wh_ModUninit and never cleared: every GDI+ startup in
// the mod refuses from then on, so the shutdowns at the end of the unload
// are final.
static std::atomic<bool> g_gdipUnloading{false};
// Set at the start of Wh_ModUninit: no new dark or backdrop styling from then on.
static std::atomic<bool> g_darkModeUnloading{ false };

// GDI+ runtime shared by scrollbar, rounded tab-pane, spin-button and button
// surfaces; RoundedHdcEnsureGdipLocked/RoundedHdcAddPath are defined with the
// tab-pane code further down.
struct RoundedHdcGdipRuntime {
    ULONG_PTR token = 0;
    bool startupAttempted = false;
    bool ready = false;
};
static RoundedHdcGdipRuntime g_roundedHdcGdip;
// Exclusive only to start and shut GDI+ down. Drawing shares it: every
// Graphics, path and brush is per call, so Explorer's UI threads don't
// queue behind each other's scrollbar, tab and button paints.
static std::shared_mutex g_roundedHdcGdipMutex;
static bool RoundedHdcEnsureGdipLocked();

// Holds GDI+ running for one paint; false when it can't be started.
class RoundedHdcGdipDrawLock {
public:
    RoundedHdcGdipDrawLock() : lock_(g_roundedHdcGdipMutex)
    {
        ready_ = g_roundedHdcGdip.ready;
        if (!ready_) {
            lock_.unlock();
            {
                std::unique_lock<std::shared_mutex> startup(g_roundedHdcGdipMutex);
                RoundedHdcEnsureGdipLocked();
            }
            lock_.lock();
            ready_ = g_roundedHdcGdip.ready;
        }
    }
    explicit operator bool() const { return ready_; }

private:
    std::shared_lock<std::shared_mutex> lock_;
    bool ready_ = false;
};
static bool RoundedHdcAddPath(Gdiplus::GraphicsPath& path,
    const Gdiplus::RectF& bounds, float radius,
    bool roundTopLeft, bool roundTopRight,
    bool roundBottomRight, bool roundBottomLeft);

static Gdiplus::Color GdipColor(const D2D1_COLOR_F& c)
{
    auto ch = [](float v) { return (BYTE)std::lround(std::clamp(v, 0.f, 1.f) * 255.f); };
    return Gdiplus::Color(ch(c.a), ch(c.r), ch(c.g), ch(c.b));
}

static Gdiplus::Color GdipColor(COLORREF c, BYTE alpha = 255)
{
    return Gdiplus::Color(alpha, GetRValue(c), GetGValue(c), GetBValue(c));
}

// Translucent or opaque rounded fill composited over the DC's own pixels.
static bool FillRoundedRectGdip(HDC hdc, const Gdiplus::RectF& bounds,
    float radius, Gdiplus::Color color)
{
    if (!hdc || bounds.Width <= 0.f || bounds.Height <= 0.f)
        return false;
    RoundedHdcGdipDrawLock gdipLock;
    if (!gdipLock)
        return false;
    Gdiplus::Graphics graphics(hdc);
    if (graphics.GetLastStatus() != Gdiplus::Ok ||
        graphics.SetSmoothingMode(Gdiplus::SmoothingModeAntiAlias) != Gdiplus::Ok ||
        graphics.SetPixelOffsetMode(Gdiplus::PixelOffsetModeHalf) != Gdiplus::Ok)
        return false;
    Gdiplus::GraphicsPath path;
    if (!RoundedHdcAddPath(path, bounds, radius, true, true, true, true))
        return false;
    Gdiplus::SolidBrush brush(color);
    return graphics.FillPath(&brush, &path) == Gdiplus::Ok;
}

// Antialiased rounded outline centered on `bounds`, over the DC's pixels.
static bool StrokeRoundedRectGdip(HDC hdc, const Gdiplus::RectF& bounds,
    float radius, float width, Gdiplus::Color color)
{
    if (!hdc || bounds.Width <= 0.f || bounds.Height <= 0.f || width <= 0.f)
        return false;
    RoundedHdcGdipDrawLock gdipLock;
    if (!gdipLock)
        return false;
    Gdiplus::Graphics graphics(hdc);
    if (graphics.GetLastStatus() != Gdiplus::Ok ||
        graphics.SetSmoothingMode(Gdiplus::SmoothingModeAntiAlias) != Gdiplus::Ok ||
        graphics.SetPixelOffsetMode(Gdiplus::PixelOffsetModeHalf) != Gdiplus::Ok)
        return false;
    Gdiplus::GraphicsPath path;
    if (!RoundedHdcAddPath(path, bounds, radius, true, true, true, true))
        return false;
    Gdiplus::Pen pen(color, width);
    return graphics.DrawPath(&pen, &path) == Gdiplus::Ok;
}

// A GDI+ scene rendered into a premultiplied 32bpp DIB the size of the
// part and composed onto the DC with AlphaBlend, which applies source-over
// to the destination alpha as well (verified on 32bpp DIBs). That keeps a
// Mica or solid pane surface correct where GDI+ drawn straight into the DC
// would zero the alpha of every pixel it touches. The draw callback works
// in the part's own coordinates.
template <typename Draw>
static bool PaintAlphaSceneGdip(HDC hdc, LPCRECT pRect, Draw&& draw)
{
    if (!hdc || !pRect)
        return false;
    const int w = pRect->right - pRect->left;
    const int h = pRect->bottom - pRect->top;
    if (w <= 0 || h <= 0)
        return false;
    RoundedHdcGdipDrawLock gdipLock;
    if (!gdipLock)
        return false;

    BITMAPINFO bi = {};
    bi.bmiHeader.biSize = sizeof(bi.bmiHeader);
    bi.bmiHeader.biWidth = w;
    bi.bmiHeader.biHeight = -h;
    bi.bmiHeader.biPlanes = 1;
    bi.bmiHeader.biBitCount = 32;
    bi.bmiHeader.biCompression = BI_RGB;
    void* bits = nullptr;
    HBITMAP dib = CreateDIBSection(nullptr, &bi, DIB_RGB_COLORS, &bits, nullptr, 0);
    if (!dib || !bits) {
        if (dib) DeleteObject(dib);
        return false;
    }
    bool drawn = false;
    {
        Gdiplus::Bitmap bitmap(w, h, w * 4, PixelFormat32bppPARGB, static_cast<BYTE*>(bits));
        Gdiplus::Graphics graphics(&bitmap);
        if (bitmap.GetLastStatus() == Gdiplus::Ok &&
            graphics.GetLastStatus() == Gdiplus::Ok &&
            graphics.SetSmoothingMode(Gdiplus::SmoothingModeAntiAlias) == Gdiplus::Ok &&
            graphics.SetPixelOffsetMode(Gdiplus::PixelOffsetModeHalf) == Gdiplus::Ok) {
            draw(graphics);
            graphics.Flush(Gdiplus::FlushIntentionSync);
            drawn = true;
        }
    }
    if (drawn) {
        if (HDC mem = CreateCompatibleDC(hdc)) {
            HGDIOBJ old = SelectObject(mem, dib);
            const BLENDFUNCTION bf = { AC_SRC_OVER, 0, 255, AC_SRC_ALPHA };
            drawn = AlphaBlend(hdc, pRect->left, pRect->top, w, h, mem, 0, 0, w, h, bf) != FALSE;
            SelectObject(mem, old);
            DeleteDC(mem);
        } else {
            drawn = false;
        }
    }
    DeleteObject(dib);
    return drawn;
}

// GDI preserves RGB but commonly clears alpha on a DWM-composited DC. Copy
// the completed pixels through a 32bpp DIB and make that final surface opaque
// without changing its already-correct colors.
static bool RepairOpaqueHdcAlpha(
    HDC hdc, const RECT& rect, HRGN outputClip = nullptr,
    bool replaceOutputClip = false)
{
    if (!hdc)
        return false;
    const int width = rect.right - rect.left;
    const int height = rect.bottom - rect.top;
    if (width <= 0 || height <= 0)
        return false;

    BITMAPINFO bitmapInfo = {};
    bitmapInfo.bmiHeader.biSize = sizeof(bitmapInfo.bmiHeader);
    bitmapInfo.bmiHeader.biWidth = width;
    bitmapInfo.bmiHeader.biHeight = -height;
    bitmapInfo.bmiHeader.biPlanes = 1;
    bitmapInfo.bmiHeader.biBitCount = 32;
    bitmapInfo.bmiHeader.biCompression = BI_RGB;
    void* bits = nullptr;
    HBITMAP bitmap = CreateDIBSection(
        hdc, &bitmapInfo, DIB_RGB_COLORS, &bits, nullptr, 0);
    if (!bitmap || !bits) {
        if (bitmap)
            DeleteObject(bitmap);
        return false;
    }

    bool repaired = false;
    if (HDC memoryDc = CreateCompatibleDC(hdc)) {
        HGDIOBJ previous = SelectObject(memoryDc, bitmap);
        if (previous && previous != HGDI_ERROR &&
            BitBlt(memoryDc, 0, 0, width, height,
                hdc, rect.left, rect.top, SRCCOPY) &&
            GdiFlush()) {
            DWORD* pixels = static_cast<DWORD*>(bits);
            const size_t pixelCount =
                static_cast<size_t>(width) * height;
            for (size_t i = 0; i < pixelCount; ++i)
                pixels[i] |= 0xFF000000u;
            int savedDc = 0;
            bool clipReady = true;
            if (outputClip) {
                savedDc = SaveDC(hdc);
                clipReady = savedDc > 0 &&
                    (replaceOutputClip
                            ? SelectClipRgn(hdc, outputClip)
                            : ExtSelectClipRgn(
                                  hdc, outputClip, RGN_AND)) != ERROR;
            }
            if (clipReady) {
                repaired = BitBlt(
                    hdc, rect.left, rect.top, width, height,
                    memoryDc, 0, 0, SRCCOPY) != FALSE;
            }
            if (savedDc > 0)
                RestoreDC(hdc, savedDc);
        }
        if (previous && previous != HGDI_ERROR)
            SelectObject(memoryDc, previous);
        DeleteDC(memoryDc);
    }
    DeleteObject(bitmap);
    return repaired;
}

static ID2D1Factory1* EnsureD2DFactory()
{
    // g_d2dFactory is normally already set by Wh_ModInit's eager, single-
    // threaded creation, so this fast path is the common case and needs no
    // lock. The lock only guards the fallback path for the (unexpected)
    // case where that eager creation failed -- without it, two threads
    // racing here for the first time could both call D2D1CreateFactory and
    // clobber each other's write to this raw pointer.
    if (g_d2dFactory) return g_d2dFactory;
    static std::mutex s_factoryMutex;
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(s_factoryMutex);
    if (!g_d2dFactory)
    {
        FPUGuard fpu; // D2D1CreateFactory may change FPU control word
        D2D1_FACTORY_OPTIONS options = {};
        // MULTI_THREADED required: pill animation thread uses D2D from background thread
        D2D1CreateFactory(D2D1_FACTORY_TYPE_MULTI_THREADED, options, &g_d2dFactory);
    }
    return g_d2dFactory;
}

static UINT GetDpiFromMonitor()
{
    HMONITOR hPrimary = MonitorFromPoint({0,0}, MONITOR_DEFAULTTOPRIMARY);
    UINT dpiX = USER_DEFAULT_SCREEN_DPI, dpiY = USER_DEFAULT_SCREEN_DPI;
    if (SUCCEEDED(GetDpiForMonitor(hPrimary, MDT_EFFECTIVE_DPI, &dpiX, &dpiY)))
        return dpiY;
    return USER_DEFAULT_SCREEN_DPI;
}
static bool IsCurrentProcessExplorer()
{
    static int cached = -1;
    if (cached == -1)
    {
        wchar_t path[MAX_PATH] = {};
        GetModuleFileNameW(nullptr, path, MAX_PATH);
        wchar_t* name = wcsrchr(path, L'\\');
        cached = (name && _wcsicmp(name + 1, L"explorer.exe") == 0) ? 1 : 0;

// cleanmgr.exe's file-category ListView (LVS_EX_CHECKBOXES) bakes its
// checkbox state-image bitmaps once, early during WM_INITDIALOG, before this
// mod's own dark-mode attribute is applied to the dialog -- comctl32 never
// redoes that bake, so the checkboxes stay stuck light even once the rest
// of the dialog goes dark. Toggling LVS_EX_CHECKBOXES off then back on
// forces a fresh bake through the (by-then-correct) theming hooks. Scoped
// to cleanmgr.exe only -- not a general fix for every checkbox ListView.
// Runs on g_msgWnd's thread (the WinEvent hook's owner), so the ListView is
// another thread's: bounded sends keep a hung dialog from holding that thread
// and the unload join behind it.
static BOOL CALLBACK CleanmgrFixListViewCheckboxesEnum(HWND hwnd, LPARAM)
{
    wchar_t cls[32] = {};
    GetClassNameW(hwnd, cls, ARRAYSIZE(cls));
    if (_wcsicmp(cls, L"SysListView32") == 0) {
        constexpr UINT kFlags = SMTO_ABORTIFHUNG | SMTO_BLOCK;
        constexpr UINT kTimeoutMs = 1000;
        DWORD_PTR exStyle = 0;
        if (!SendMessageTimeoutW(hwnd, LVM_GETEXTENDEDLISTVIEWSTYLE, 0, 0,
                kFlags, kTimeoutMs, &exStyle))
            return TRUE;
        if (exStyle & LVS_EX_CHECKBOXES) {
            DWORD_PTR ignored = 0;
            SendMessageTimeoutW(hwnd, LVM_SETEXTENDEDLISTVIEWSTYLE, 0,
                exStyle & ~LVS_EX_CHECKBOXES, kFlags, kTimeoutMs, &ignored);
            SendMessageTimeoutW(hwnd, LVM_SETEXTENDEDLISTVIEWSTYLE, 0,
                exStyle, kFlags, kTimeoutMs, &ignored);
            InvalidateRect(hwnd, nullptr, TRUE);
        }
    }
    return TRUE;
}

// EVENT_OBJECT_SHOW (not CREATE) -- by the time the dialog is actually
// shown, WM_INITDIALOG has fully finished, so this mod's own dark-mode
// styling for the dialog is guaranteed to have already been applied.
static void CALLBACK CleanmgrWinEventProc(HWINEVENTHOOK, DWORD event, HWND hWnd,
    LONG idObject, LONG idChild, DWORD, DWORD)
{
    if (!IsCustomDarkModeAllowed())
        return;
    if (idObject != OBJID_WINDOW || idChild != CHILDID_SELF)
        return;
    if (event != EVENT_OBJECT_SHOW)
        return;
    if (!hWnd || !IsWindow(hWnd) || GetWindow(hWnd, GW_OWNER))
        return; // top-level dialog only
    wchar_t cls[16] = {};
    GetClassNameW(hWnd, cls, ARRAYSIZE(cls));
    if (_wcsicmp(cls, L"#32770") != 0)
        return;

    EnumChildWindows(hWnd, CleanmgrFixListViewCheckboxesEnum, 0);
}
