// COMBOBOX DROPDOWN — rounded corners + themed colors
// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
// INSERTION MARK
// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

constexpr UINT TVM_GETITEMRECT_   = 0x1104;

// Accent (or the configured color) for the bar. Taken from the DC because the
// only place the mark can be restyled hands over a DC and nothing else, and
// that DC is often the control's own double buffer, with no window to ask.
static COLORREF InsertMarkColor(HDC hdc)
{
    if (!g_settings.InsertMarkUseAccent)
        return g_settings.InsertMarkClr;

    if (g_accentCacheDirty.load(std::memory_order_acquire))
        RefreshAccentCache();
    const bool dark = IsDarkForExcludedAwarePaintHdc(hdc);
    if (dark == g_cachedIsDark.load(std::memory_order_relaxed))
        return g_cachedIndicator.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
    return GetAccentFillDefault(dark);
}

// The mark itself: a capsule in the DC's coordinates. GDI+ and not Direct2D
// on purpose -- a DC render target pays for a bind and a flush through GDI
// interop on every call, measured at ~700us against ~6us here for the same
// shape, and this is redrawn on every frame of a drag. The bar always sits
// inside the rect comctl32 measured, so its antialiased edges never reach the
// edge of a buffer that someone else composes later.
static bool DrawInsertMarkBar(HDC hdc, const RECT& bar, COLORREF color)
{
    const float w = (float)(bar.right - bar.left);
    const float h = (float)(bar.bottom - bar.top);
    if (w <= 0.f || h <= 0.f)
        return false;
    return FillRoundedRectGdip(hdc,
        Gdiplus::RectF((float)bar.left, (float)bar.top, w, h),
        std::min(w, h) * 0.5f, GdipColor(color));
}

static void DrawInsertMarkBarGdi(HDC hdc, const RECT& bar, COLORREF color)
{
    if (bar.right <= bar.left || bar.bottom <= bar.top)
        return;
    if (HBRUSH brush = CreateSolidBrush(color)) {
        FillRect(hdc, &bar, brush);
        DeleteObject(brush);
    }
}

// The same stroke the nav pane pill is drawn with: both are accent marks in
// the same surface, and both are full capsules, so the radius follows from it.
static LONG InsertMarkThickness(UINT dpi)
{
    return std::max<LONG>(1, MulDiv((int)NAV_PILL_WIDTH_DIP, (int)dpi,
                                    USER_DEFAULT_SCREEN_DPI));
}

// Narrows comctl32's own mark rect down to the bar drawn in its place. Which
// way the mark runs is the caller's answer rather than a guess from the rect's
// proportions: a list arranges icons in rows or in columns, so the gap between
// two of them is horizontal in one case and vertical in the other.
static bool InsertMarkBar(HDC hdc, const RECT& native, BOOL vertical,
                          RECT* outBar)
{
    if (!outBar || native.right <= native.left || native.bottom <= native.top)
        return false;

    const UINT dpi = DpiForPaintHdc(hdc);
    const LONG thickness = InsertMarkThickness(dpi);
    const LONG inset = MulDiv(2, (int)dpi, USER_DEFAULT_SCREEN_DPI);

    if (vertical) {
        const LONG centerX = (native.left + native.right) / 2;
        outBar->left = centerX - thickness / 2;
        outBar->right = outBar->left + thickness;
        outBar->top = native.top + inset;
        outBar->bottom = native.bottom - inset;
        return outBar->bottom > outBar->top;
    }

    const LONG centerY = (native.top + native.bottom) / 2;
    outBar->top = centerY - thickness / 2;
    outBar->bottom = outBar->top + thickness;

    // A tree's mark reads as a divider between two rows, so it spans the pane
    // like the WinUI reorder indicator instead of stopping at the item rect
    // comctl32 measured, which starts past the indentation and ends at the
    // label. Everywhere else the measured rect is the gap itself and is kept.
    outBar->left = native.left + inset;
    outBar->right = native.right - inset;
    return outBar->right > outBar->left;
}

// comctl32 draws every insertion mark it owns through this one helper -- list
// views, tree views and toolbars alike -- from inside the control's own paint,
// with the DC and the rect it has already prepared. That makes it the only
// workable place to restyle the mark. Answering LVM_SETINSERTMARK covers just
// the apps that send it: during a drag the control sets the mark itself
// through an internal call no subclass can observe, and the state it reports
// back cannot be written again (the private flag it returns is refused on the
// way in, after which it stops reporting a rect at all).
//
// Hooked on 64-bit only. The 32-bit build decorates this as __stdcall yet
// passes the first two arguments in registers and returns popping three: a
// convention the compiler chose for that build, which a hook cannot assume
// still holds in the next one.
using CCDrawInsertMark_t = void(WINAPI*)(HDC, const RECT*, BOOL, COLORREF,
                                         void*);

static CCDrawInsertMark_t CCDrawInsertMark_orig;

// Unreferenced on 32-bit, where InsertMarkInstallHook installs nothing.
[[maybe_unused]] static void WINAPI CCDrawInsertMark_hook(HDC hdc, const RECT* prc,
                                         BOOL vertical, COLORREF color,
                                         void* reserved)
{
    RECT bar{};
    if (!g_settings.ModernInsert || SysHighContrastEnabled() || !hdc || !prc ||
        !InsertMarkBar(hdc, *prc, vertical, &bar)) {
        CCDrawInsertMark_orig(hdc, prc, vertical, color, reserved);
        return;
    }

    const COLORREF barColor = InsertMarkColor(hdc);
    if (!DrawInsertMarkBar(hdc, bar, barColor))
        DrawInsertMarkBarGdi(hdc, bar, barColor);
}



// ── Tree views ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// The one control the draw helper cannot serve. A tree's mark reads as a
// divider between two rows and spans the pane, but comctl32 draws marks item
// by item with the DC clipped to the item it sits on, so a wider bar is cut
// back there, and the rows painted afterwards would cover what survived.
// A tree mark always arrives as TVM_SETINSERTMARK -- the control has no drag
// of its own to set one internally, which is exactly what made the list case
// need the helper -- so the message is answered here instead. comctl32 is
// left with no mark to draw, and the bar goes down last, over a finished
// client.
constexpr UINT TVM_SETINSERTMARK_ = 0x111A;

static void TreeInsertMarkClearProperties(HWND tv)
{
    RemovePropW(tv, PROP_TV_INSERT_ITEM);
    RemovePropW(tv, PROP_TV_INSERT_AFTER);
}

static bool TreeInsertMarkBar(HWND tv, HTREEITEM item, BOOL after,
                              RECT* outBar)
{
    if (!item || !outBar)
        return false;
    RECT ir = {};
    *reinterpret_cast<HTREEITEM*>(&ir) = item;
    if (!SendMessageW(tv, TVM_GETITEMRECT_, TRUE, (LPARAM)&ir))
        return false;

    RECT cr{};
    GetClientRect(tv, &cr);
    UINT dpi = GetDpiForWindow(tv);
    if (!dpi) dpi = USER_DEFAULT_SCREEN_DPI;
    const LONG thickness = InsertMarkThickness(dpi);
    const LONG margin = MulDiv(4, (int)dpi, USER_DEFAULT_SCREEN_DPI);
    const LONG lineY = after ? ir.bottom : ir.top;
    const LONG top = std::clamp<LONG>(lineY - thickness / 2, 0,
        std::max<LONG>(0, cr.bottom - thickness));
    outBar->left = margin;
    outBar->right = std::max<LONG>(margin + thickness, cr.right - margin);
    outBar->top = top;
    outBar->bottom = top + thickness;
    return true;
}

static LRESULT CALLBACK TreeViewSubclass(HWND hWnd, UINT uMsg, WPARAM wParam,
                                         LPARAM lParam, DWORD_PTR)
{
    if (uMsg == TVM_SETINSERTMARK_ && SysHighContrastEnabled()) {
        TreeInsertMarkClearProperties(hWnd);
        return DefSubclassProc(hWnd, uMsg, wParam, lParam);
    }
    if (uMsg == TVM_SETINSERTMARK_ && g_settings.ModernInsert) {
        HTREEITEM item = (HTREEITEM)lParam;
        if (!item) {
            TreeInsertMarkClearProperties(hWnd);
            auto r = DefSubclassProc(hWnd, uMsg, wParam, lParam);
            InvalidateRect(hWnd, nullptr, TRUE);
            return r;
        }

        if (!SetPropW(hWnd, PROP_TV_INSERT_ITEM, item) ||
            ((BOOL)wParam && !SetPropW(hWnd, PROP_TV_INSERT_AFTER, (HANDLE)1))) {
            TreeInsertMarkClearProperties(hWnd);
            return DefSubclassProc(hWnd, uMsg, wParam, lParam);
        }
        if (!(BOOL)wParam)
            RemovePropW(hWnd, PROP_TV_INSERT_AFTER);
        InvalidateRect(hWnd, nullptr, FALSE);
        return TRUE;
    }
    if (uMsg == WM_PAINT) {
        HTREEITEM item = (HTREEITEM)GetPropW(hWnd, PROP_TV_INSERT_ITEM);
        if (!g_settings.ModernInsert || !item || SysHighContrastEnabled())
            return DefSubclassProc(hWnd, uMsg, wParam, lParam);
        const BOOL after = GetPropW(hWnd, PROP_TV_INSERT_AFTER) != nullptr;

        PAINTSTRUCT ps{};
        HDC hdc = BeginPaint(hWnd, &ps);
        if (!hdc)
            return DefSubclassProc(hWnd, uMsg, wParam, lParam);
        {
            RECT rc{};
            GetClientRect(hWnd, &rc);
            HDC memDC = rc.right > 0 && rc.bottom > 0 ? CreateCompatibleDC(hdc)
                                                      : nullptr;
            HBITMAP bmp = memDC
                ? CreateCompatibleBitmap(hdc, rc.right, rc.bottom) : nullptr;
            HGDIOBJ oldBmp = bmp ? SelectObject(memDC, bmp) : nullptr;
            const bool buffered = memDC && bmp && oldBmp && oldBmp != HGDI_ERROR;
            HDC target = buffered ? memDC : hdc;

            DefSubclassProc(hWnd, WM_PRINTCLIENT, (WPARAM)target, PRF_CLIENT);
            RECT bar{};
            if (TreeInsertMarkBar(hWnd, item, after, &bar)) {
                const COLORREF color = InsertMarkColor(target);
                if (!DrawInsertMarkBar(target, bar, color))
                    DrawInsertMarkBarGdi(target, bar, color);
            }
            if (buffered)
                BitBlt(hdc, 0, 0, rc.right, rc.bottom, memDC, 0, 0, SRCCOPY);

            if (buffered)
                SelectObject(memDC, oldBmp);
            if (bmp)
                DeleteObject(bmp);
            if (memDC)
                DeleteDC(memDC);
            EndPaint(hWnd, &ps);
        }
        return 0;
    }
    if (uMsg == WM_NCDESTROY) {
        RemovePropW(hWnd, PROP_TV_SUB);
        TreeInsertMarkClearProperties(hWnd);
    }
    return DefSubclassProc(hWnd, uMsg, wParam, lParam);
}

// Both comctl32 versions can be loaded at once under the same module name and
// only the v6 one draws these marks, so each match is offered the hook until
// one of them takes it.
static void InsertMarkEnsureHook(bool applyHooks);

// Guards the set below. The installer runs from the message window's thread
// and from the settings-change callback, and holding it across the whole pass
// also keeps two callers from starting the same symbol lookup at once. Both
// live under the installer's own guard: the hook is 64-bit only (see
// CCDrawInsertMark_t), so a 32-bit build has no user for either.
#ifdef _WIN64
static std::mutex g_insertMarkTriedMutex;
static std::unordered_set<HMODULE> g_insertMarkTriedModules;
#endif

static void InsertMarkInstallHook()
{
#ifdef _WIN64
    if (CCDrawInsertMark_orig)
        return;

    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> triedLock(g_insertMarkTriedMutex);
    if (CCDrawInsertMark_orig)
        return;

    HANDLE snapshot = CreateToolhelp32Snapshot(
        TH32CS_SNAPMODULE | TH32CS_SNAPMODULE32, GetCurrentProcessId());
    if (snapshot == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) {
        Wh_Log(L"Insertion mark: failed to enumerate comctl32 modules, "
               L"error=%lu", GetLastError());
        return;
    }

    // Each module is offered the hook once. A process that only ever loads
    // the v5 comctl32 -- which has no such helper, and whose list views this
    // mod leaves alone anyway -- would otherwise pay for the lookup again on
    // every later pass, and say so in the log every time.
    bool attempted = false;
    MODULEENTRY32W module = {};
    module.dwSize = sizeof(module);
    if (Module32FirstW(snapshot, &module)) {
        do {
            if (_wcsicmp(module.szModule, L"comctl32.dll") != 0)
                continue;
            // Both versions answer to that name, and only the v6 one has the
            // helper at all -- asking a v5 module costs a symbol lookup that
            // can never succeed. TaskDialogIndirect arrived with v6 and says
            // which one this is without reading the file.
            if (!GetProcAddress(module.hModule, "TaskDialogIndirect"))
                continue;
            if (!g_insertMarkTriedModules.insert(module.hModule).second)
                continue;
            attempted = true;
            SetResolvedSymbolHook(
                Comctl32ResolveSymbols(module.hModule).ccDrawInsertMark,
                CCDrawInsertMark_hook, &CCDrawInsertMark_orig);
        } while (!CCDrawInsertMark_orig && Module32NextW(snapshot, &module));
    }
    CloseHandle(snapshot);

    if (attempted && !CCDrawInsertMark_orig) {
        Wh_Log(L"Insertion mark: CCDrawInsertMark symbol unavailable; "
               L"native marks stay in place");
    }
#endif
}


// Marks a window as currently carrying TreeCursorSubclassProc, so
// Wh_ModUninit's RemoveSubclassesFromWindow sweep knows to remove it
// without unconditionally messaging every enumerated window.
static constexpr LPCWSTR kTreeCursorSubclassProp = L"WH_MW_TREE_CURSOR_SUB";
static constexpr LPCWSTR kPropNavHoverFadeState =
    L"Win32UIModernizer.NavHoverFadeState";
// Registered at runtime via RegisterWindowMessageW in Wh_ModInit, not a
// fixed WM_APP+N value -- this is SendMessageW'd to Explorer's/a file
// picker's own SysTreeView32 (a window this mod doesn't own), and WM_APP+N
// is the range reserved for the *application*, so a hardcoded offset here
// could collide with Explorer's or another mod's own private message on
// that window. Same treatment as Win32UIModernizer.DefViewBorderPaint.
static std::atomic<UINT> g_navHoverFadeResetMessage{0};
static constexpr UINT kNavHoverFadeTimerIntervalMs = 16;
static constexpr DOUBLE kNavHoverFadeDurationSeconds = 0.14;
// Fade-out only: hold the pill fully visible for this long after the mouse
// leaves before the actual shrink/fade curve starts, so a quick pass-over
// doesn't read as an instant pop. Fade-in has no equivalent hold -- growing
// in should start immediately, only leaving benefits from a beat first.
static constexpr DOUBLE kNavHoverFadeOutHoldSeconds = 0.02;
static constexpr float kNavHoverFadeInitialScale = 0.97f;
static int g_navHoverFadeTimerTag;

struct NavHoverFadeState {
    HTREEITEM hotItem = nullptr;   // item currently fading in / settled hot
    RECT rect = {};
    DOUBLE startTime = 0.0;
    bool trackingLeave = false;
    bool timerActive = false;
    bool fadingOut = false;  // used only by Regedit's rg_hoverFade -- see RgHoverFadeRetarget
    // hotItem was selected at some point while hot -- comctl32 paints a
    // selected+hot row as TREIS_HOTSELECTED, not the plain hot state
    // DrawRoundedItemBg's pill logic reacts to, so no pill of ours was ever
    // shown for it (see the exclusion check below). Stays excluded from
    // fading out even after a later deselect, since a live TVIS_SELECTED
    // check alone can't catch that after the fact.
    bool hotEverSelected = false;

    // The item the mouse just left, fading out independently of whatever is
    // now fading in via hotItem -- lets a direct hop from one item to its
    // neighbor show both animations at once instead of the old item just
    // vanishing. Bounded to one slot: a third item arriving before this
    // one's fade-out finishes cuts it short rather than queuing it.
    HTREEITEM outItem = nullptr;
    RECT outRect = {};  // exact pill bounds, not the narrower label bounds
    DOUBLE outStartTime = 0.0;
};

static UINT_PTR NavHoverFadeTimerId()
{
    return reinterpret_cast<UINT_PTR>(&g_navHoverFadeTimerTag);
}

static bool NavHoverTrackingEnabled()
{
    return !g_msgWndUnloading.load(std::memory_order_acquire) &&
        g_settings.ExplorerSection &&
        RoundedSelectionVisualsEnabled();
}

static bool NavHoverFadeSettingsEnabled()
{
    return NavHoverTrackingEnabled() &&
        g_settings.NavPaneHoverFade &&
        SysAnimationsEnabled();
}

static NavHoverFadeState* NavHoverFadeGetState(HWND hwnd)
{
    return reinterpret_cast<NavHoverFadeState*>(
        GetPropW(hwnd, kPropNavHoverFadeState));
}

// Same technique as GetNavFocusItemRect (see e3c811a): the FALSE/full-item
// variant of TVM_GETITEMRECT can come back spanning into a neighboring
// section divider's row instead of just this item's own, so the vertical
// bounds are taken from the TRUE/label-only variant instead -- that one
// stays tight to the real per-item content. FALSE is still used for the
// left/right edge below (overwritten to the full client width anyway) and
// as the up-front "is this even a real item" check divider rows already
// fail (see NavHoverFadeItemIsRealTarget, same TRUE-variant check).
static bool NavHoverFadeGetItemRect(
    HWND hwnd, HTREEITEM item, RECT* rect)
{
    if (!hwnd || !item || !rect ||
        !TreeView_GetItemRect(hwnd, item, rect, FALSE)) {
        return false;
    }

    RECT labelRect = {};
    if (!TreeView_GetItemRect(hwnd, item, &labelRect, TRUE) ||
        labelRect.bottom <= labelRect.top) {
        return false;
    }
    rect->top = labelRect.top;
    rect->bottom = labelRect.bottom;

    RECT client = {};
    if (GetClientRect(hwnd, &client)) {
        rect->left = client.left;
        rect->right = client.right;
    }
    return rect->bottom > rect->top;
}

// Shared smoothstep curve underneath both hover fade directions -- reverse=
// false ramps 0->1 from startTime (fade in, "parked" at 1 once startTime<=0),
// reverse=true ramps 1->0 (fade out, 0 once startTime<=0 -- never parked,
// since an out-fade with no start time means it hasn't begun animating yet,
// not that it settled). holdSeconds (fade-out only in practice) keeps the
// pre-curve value (1.f for reverse) for that long before elapsed starts
// feeding the curve at all -- a flat hold, not a slower ramp.
static float NavFadeCurveProgress(
    DOUBLE startTime, DOUBLE now, bool reverse, DOUBLE holdSeconds = 0.0)
{
    if (startTime <= 0.0)
        return reverse ? 0.f : 1.f;

    DOUBLE elapsed = now - startTime;
    if (holdSeconds > 0.0) {
        if (elapsed <= holdSeconds)
            return reverse ? 1.f : 0.f;
        elapsed -= holdSeconds;
    }
    float t;
    if (elapsed <= 0.0)
        t = 0.f;
    else if (elapsed >= kNavHoverFadeDurationSeconds)
        t = 1.f;
    else {
        t = static_cast<float>(elapsed / kNavHoverFadeDurationSeconds);
        t = t * t * (3.f - 2.f * t);
    }
    return reverse ? (1.f - t) : t;
}

static float NavHoverFadeProgress(
    const NavHoverFadeState& state, DOUBLE now)
{
    if (!state.hotItem)
        return 0.f;
    // Hold applies only while actually fading out -- the nav pane never
    // reaches this function with fadingOut true (its own fade-out reads
    // through the dedicated outItem/NavHoverFadeOutProgress pair instead),
    // so this only ever matters for Regedit's rg_hoverFade, the sole
    // remaining caller that reuses this same field for both directions.
    return NavFadeCurveProgress(state.startTime, now, state.fadingOut,
        state.fadingOut ? kNavHoverFadeOutHoldSeconds : 0.0);
}

// Mirrors NavHoverFadeProgress's curve but for outItem specifically -- always
// fading 1->0 from the moment it starts, never "parked" at a settled value
// the way hotItem's startTime<=0 can mean. Carries the fade-out hold (see
// kNavHoverFadeOutHoldSeconds).
static float NavHoverFadeOutProgress(
    const NavHoverFadeState& state, DOUBLE now)
{
    if (!state.outItem)
        return 0.f;
    return NavFadeCurveProgress(
        state.outStartTime, now, true, kNavHoverFadeOutHoldSeconds);
}

static void NavHoverFadeStopTimer(
    HWND hwnd, NavHoverFadeState* state)
{
    if (!state || !state->timerActive)
        return;

    (void)KillTimer(hwnd, NavHoverFadeTimerId());
    state->timerActive = false;
}

static void NavHoverFadeDestroyState(HWND hwnd, bool invalidate)
{
    auto* state = reinterpret_cast<NavHoverFadeState*>(
        RemovePropW(hwnd, kPropNavHoverFadeState));
    if (!state)
        return;

    NavHoverFadeStopTimer(hwnd, state);
    if (invalidate) {
        if (state->hotItem)
            InvalidateRect(hwnd, &state->rect, FALSE);
        if (state->outItem)
            InvalidateRect(hwnd, &state->outRect, FALSE);
    }
    delete state;
}

// Called from TVN_DELETEITEM so a deleted item's HTREEITEM can never be
// dereferenced again by the timer tick -- comctl32 frees the item's backing
// storage on delete, so holding onto a stale handle across the fade's
// ~140ms window is a real dangling-pointer hazard, not just a stale rect.
// Clears only the matching slot -- an unrelated item fading in the other
// slot has nothing to do with this one being deleted.
static void NavHoverFadeInvalidateItem(HWND hwnd, HTREEITEM deletedItem)
{
    NavHoverFadeState* state = NavHoverFadeGetState(hwnd);
    if (!state)
        return;
    if (state->hotItem == deletedItem) {
        state->hotItem = nullptr;
        state->startTime = 0.0;
    }
    if (state->outItem == deletedItem) {
        state->outItem = nullptr;
        state->outStartTime = 0.0;
    }
    if (!state->hotItem && !state->outItem)
        NavHoverFadeDestroyState(hwnd, false);
}

static NavHoverFadeState* NavHoverFadeEnsureState(HWND hwnd)
{
    if (auto* state = NavHoverFadeGetState(hwnd))
        return state;

    auto* state = new (std::nothrow) NavHoverFadeState{};
    if (!state)
        return nullptr;
    if (!SetPropW(hwnd, kPropNavHoverFadeState, state)) {
        delete state;
        return nullptr;
    }
    return state;
}

static bool NavHoverFadeStartTimer(
    HWND hwnd, NavHoverFadeState* state)
{
    if (!NavHoverFadeSettingsEnabled())
        return false;
    if (!state || state->timerActive)
        return state != nullptr;
    if (!SetTimer(
            hwnd, NavHoverFadeTimerId(),
            kNavHoverFadeTimerIntervalMs, nullptr)) {
        return false;
    }

    state->timerActive = true;
    return true;
}

static bool IsTreeItemPressed(HWND hwnd, LPCRECT itemRect);
static bool DrawRoundedItemBg(HDC hdc, LPCRECT pRect, INT iStateId, bool isTreeView,
    float progressOverride = -1.f);

// TVM_GETITEMRECT(TRUE) (GetNavFocusItemRect's own rect) is sized to wrap a
// focus OUTLINE around the item's content -- deliberately roomier than the
// content itself, not the tight row height uxtheme's native hot-pill fill
// actually paints at. TVM_GETITEMHEIGHT returns the tree's real configured
// per-row height instead (what comctl32 itself uses internally), centered
// on the label rect's own vertical midpoint -- that midpoint is reliable
// for "where is this row" even though the label rect's own height isn't
// the right one to fill with.
static bool NavHoverFadePillRect(HWND hwnd, HTREEITEM item, RECT* out)
{
    RECT labelRect = {};
    if (!TreeView_GetItemRect(hwnd, item, &labelRect, TRUE) ||
        labelRect.bottom <= labelRect.top)
        return false;

    RECT client = {};
    if (GetClientRect(hwnd, &client)) {
        out->left = client.left;
        out->right = client.right;
    } else {
        out->left = labelRect.left;
        out->right = labelRect.right;
    }

    const int rowHeight = (int)SendMessageW(hwnd, TVM_GETITEMHEIGHT, 0, 0);
    if (rowHeight <= 0) {
        out->top = labelRect.top;
        out->bottom = labelRect.bottom;
        return true;
    }
    const int centerY = (labelRect.top + labelRect.bottom) / 2;
    out->top = centerY - rowHeight / 2;
    out->bottom = out->top + rowHeight;

    // TVM_GETITEMHEIGHT reports the tree's full configured row height --
    // with WinUI metrics on, that's the OUTER bound NavMetricsApplyToTree
    // sets (kNavMetricsItemHeight), not the inset content area everything
    // actually paints into: NavMetricsApplyItemMargin shrinks that same
    // NM_CUSTOMDRAW rect by this exact margin on every real paint. Mirror
    // that inset here, under the same setting gate, or the pill comes out
    // taller than the native fill by 2x this margin.
    if (g_settings.NavPaneWinUIMetrics) {
        const int margin = NavMetricsScale(hwnd, kNavMetricsItemMarginV);
        if (out->bottom - out->top > margin * 2) {
            out->top += margin;
            out->bottom -= margin;
        }
    }
    return out->bottom > out->top;
}

// Paints outItem's fade-out pill, called from CDDS_ITEMPOSTPAINT for every
// nav-pane row on every repaint (see the forward-declared use in
// SendMessageW_hook). Bails immediately (one GetPropW) for the overwhelming
// majority of rows that aren't outItem -- same near-zero-cost-when-inactive
// shape as the SysLink capture. Getting hItem/hdc handed to us fresh here,
// straight from comctl32's own per-item paint loop, is what makes this
// simpler than tracking/re-deriving that geometry independently the way an
// earlier WM_PAINT-driven version of this had to: there's nothing to go
// stale between the mouse leaving and the next repaint, because this always
// fires as part of that repaint, for the right item, with the right hdc.
static void NavHoverFadeOutPaint(HWND tv, HTREEITEM hItem, HDC hdc)
{
    NavHoverFadeState* state = NavHoverFadeGetState(tv);
    if (!state || hItem != state->outItem || !NavHoverFadeSettingsEnabled())
        return;
    const float progress = NavHoverFadeOutProgress(*state, TimerGetSeconds());
    if (progress <= 0.f)
        return;
    RECT itemRect = {};
    if (NavHoverFadePillRect(tv, hItem, &itemRect))
        DrawRoundedItemBg(hdc, &itemRect, 2, true, progress);
}

// Section dividers in the nav pane are real HTREEITEMs with no real label
// rect (TVM_GETITEMRECT TRUE fails or comes back with zero/negative height
// for one -- same technique GetNavFocusItemRect already uses for the custom
// focus rect). That alone isn't enough here, though: TreeView_HitTest's own
// row-boundary math attributes a divider's physical space to the real item
// below it rather than to the divider's own HTREEITEM, so a hit-test at a
// point still visually over the divider already resolves straight to that
// neighbor -- letting the fade start (and often finish, since it's short)
// before the cursor is anywhere near the item's actual content. Re-checking
// hitY against the item's own tight label rect catches that: the hit-tested
// item is only accepted once the cursor is actually within its real bounds.
static bool NavHoverFadeItemIsRealTarget(HWND hwnd, HTREEITEM item, LONG hitY)
{
    RECT labelRect = {};
    if (!TreeView_GetItemRect(hwnd, item, &labelRect, TRUE) ||
        labelRect.bottom <= labelRect.top)
        return false;
    return hitY >= labelRect.top && hitY < labelRect.bottom;
}

// Reconcile hover only after native input/layout transitions. A modal click
// loop can consume mouse messages or cancel our TME_LEAVE subscription.
static bool TreeHoverCursorClientPoint(HWND hwnd, POINT* point)
{
    POINT screen = {};
    RECT client = {};
    if (!point || !GetCursorPos(&screen) || WindowFromPoint(screen) != hwnd ||
        !ScreenToClient(hwnd, &screen) || !GetClientRect(hwnd, &client) ||
        !PtInRect(&client, screen)) {
        return false;
    }
    *point = screen;
    return true;
}

// hotItem tracks whatever's currently fading in (or settled hot); outItem
// independently tracks whatever was hotItem a moment ago and is now fading
// out, so a direct hop from one item to its neighbor shows both animations
// at once instead of the old item just popping off.
static void NavHoverFadeRetarget(HWND hwnd, HTREEITEM newHotItem)
{
    NavHoverFadeState* state = NavHoverFadeGetState(hwnd);
    if (!state && !newHotItem)
        return;
    if (!state) {
        state = NavHoverFadeEnsureState(hwnd);
        if (!state)
            return;
    }
    if (state->hotItem == newHotItem)
        return;

    const bool fadeEnabled = NavHoverFadeSettingsEnabled();
    if (!fadeEnabled) {
        NavHoverFadeStopTimer(hwnd, state);
        if (state->outItem)
            InvalidateRect(hwnd, &state->outRect, FALSE);
        state->outItem = nullptr;
        state->outStartTime = 0.0;
    }
    const bool selected = newHotItem &&
        (TreeView_GetItemState(
            hwnd, newHotItem, TVIS_SELECTED) & TVIS_SELECTED);

    // Whatever was hot becomes the new fading-out item, replacing whatever
    // was already fading out (a third item arriving before the previous
    // out-fade finishes cuts that one short rather than queuing it) -- the
    // bumped item's own rect needs one last invalidate here, or its partial-
    // opacity overlay is never erased: nothing will reference it again to
    // paint it (or a plain, pill-less repaint over it) after this point.
    // Excluded if selected right now, or if it was selected at any point
    // while it was hot (hotEverSelected) -- same as the animate check below
    // excludes a selected item from fading in: it was never shown via an
    // animated hot pill to begin with (comctl32 paints a selected+hot row as
    // TREIS_HOTSELECTED, not the plain hot state DrawRoundedItemBg's pill
    // logic reacts to), so there is nothing of ours to fade out of it.
    if (state->hotItem) {
        // Selected+hot now has its own fill, even though it does not fade.
        // Always repaint the old row when dropping its hover state.
        InvalidateRect(hwnd, &state->rect, FALSE);
        if (fadeEnabled && !state->hotEverSelected &&
            !(TreeView_GetItemState(
                hwnd, state->hotItem, TVIS_SELECTED) & TVIS_SELECTED)) {
            if (state->outItem)
                InvalidateRect(hwnd, &state->outRect, FALSE);
            state->outItem = state->hotItem;
            if (!NavHoverFadePillRect(
                    hwnd, state->outItem, &state->outRect)) {
                state->outRect = state->rect;
            }
            state->outStartTime = TimerGetSeconds();
            InvalidateRect(hwnd, &state->outRect, FALSE);
        }
    }

    state->hotItem = newHotItem;
    state->hotEverSelected = selected;
    state->startTime = 0.0;
    if (newHotItem) {
        if (!NavHoverFadeGetItemRect(hwnd, newHotItem, &state->rect)) {
            state->hotItem = nullptr;
        } else {
            const bool animate =
                fadeEnabled && !selected && !IsTreeItemPressed(hwnd, &state->rect);
            if (animate)
                state->startTime = TimerGetSeconds();
            InvalidateRect(hwnd, &state->rect, FALSE);
        }
    }

    const bool needsTimer = state->startTime > 0.0 || state->outStartTime > 0.0;
    if (needsTimer && !NavHoverFadeStartTimer(hwnd, state)) {
        state->startTime = 0.0;
        state->outItem = nullptr;
        state->outStartTime = 0.0;
        NavHoverFadeStopTimer(hwnd, state);
    }
    if (!state->hotItem && !state->outItem)
        NavHoverFadeDestroyState(hwnd, false);
}

static void NavHoverFadeHandleMouseMove(HWND hwnd, LPARAM lParam)
{
    if (!NavHoverTrackingEnabled()) {
        NavHoverFadeDestroyState(hwnd, true);
        return;
    }

    TVHITTESTINFO hit = {};
    hit.pt.x = static_cast<SHORT>(LOWORD(lParam));
    hit.pt.y = static_cast<SHORT>(HIWORD(lParam));
    HTREEITEM item = TreeView_HitTest(hwnd, &hit);
    if (item && !NavHoverFadeItemIsRealTarget(hwnd, item, hit.pt.y))
        item = nullptr;

    NavHoverFadeState* state = NavHoverFadeGetState(hwnd);
    if (state && state->hotItem == item) {
        if (!state->trackingLeave) {
            TRACKMOUSEEVENT tme = {
                sizeof(tme), TME_LEAVE, hwnd, 0
            };
            state->trackingLeave =
                TrackMouseEvent(&tme) != FALSE;
        }
        return;
    }
    NavHoverFadeRetarget(hwnd, item);
    state = NavHoverFadeGetState(hwnd);
    if (state && !state->trackingLeave) {
        TRACKMOUSEEVENT tme = {
            sizeof(tme), TME_LEAVE, hwnd, 0
        };
        state->trackingLeave = TrackMouseEvent(&tme) != FALSE;
    }
}

static void NavHoverFadeSyncCursor(HWND hwnd, bool rearmLeave)
{
    NavHoverFadeState* state = NavHoverFadeGetState(hwnd);
    if (!state)
        return;
    if (!NavHoverTrackingEnabled()) {
        NavHoverFadeDestroyState(hwnd, true);
        return;
    }
    if (rearmLeave)
        state->trackingLeave = false;
    POINT point = {};
    if (!TreeHoverCursorClientPoint(hwnd, &point)) {
        NavHoverFadeRetarget(hwnd, nullptr);
        return;
    }
    // Refresh both the old and new row bounds if native layout moved them.
    const RECT previousRect = state->rect;
    RECT currentRect = {};
    if (state->hotItem &&
        NavHoverFadeGetItemRect(hwnd, state->hotItem, &currentRect) &&
        !EqualRect(&previousRect, &currentRect)) {
        InvalidateRect(hwnd, &previousRect, FALSE);
        InvalidateRect(hwnd, &currentRect, FALSE);
        state->rect = currentRect;
    }
    NavHoverFadeHandleMouseMove(hwnd, MAKELPARAM(point.x, point.y));
}

static void NavHoverFadeTimerTick(HWND hwnd)
{
    NavHoverFadeState* state = NavHoverFadeGetState(hwnd);
    if (!state || !state->timerActive)
        return;
    if (!NavHoverTrackingEnabled()) {
        NavHoverFadeDestroyState(
            hwnd,
            !g_msgWndUnloading.load(std::memory_order_acquire));
        return;
    }
    if (!NavHoverFadeSettingsEnabled()) {
        // Stop animation without losing the selected row's hover tracking.
        NavHoverFadeStopTimer(hwnd, state);
        state->startTime = 0.0;
        if (state->hotItem)
            InvalidateRect(hwnd, &state->rect, FALSE);
        if (state->outItem)
            InvalidateRect(hwnd, &state->outRect, FALSE);
        state->outItem = nullptr;
        state->outStartTime = 0.0;
        if (!state->hotItem)
            NavHoverFadeDestroyState(hwnd, false);
        return;
    }

    const DOUBLE now = TimerGetSeconds();
    bool stillAnimating = false;

    if (state->hotItem) {
        RECT previousRect = state->rect;
        if (!NavHoverFadeGetItemRect(hwnd, state->hotItem, &state->rect)) {
            InvalidateRect(hwnd, &previousRect, FALSE);
            state->hotItem = nullptr;
            state->startTime = 0.0;
        } else {
            if (!EqualRect(&previousRect, &state->rect))
                InvalidateRect(hwnd, &previousRect, FALSE);
            InvalidateRect(hwnd, &state->rect, FALSE);
            if (state->startTime > 0.0) {
                if (now - state->startTime >= kNavHoverFadeDurationSeconds)
                    state->startTime = 0.0;
                else
                    stillAnimating = true;
            }
        }
    }

    if (state->outItem) {
        RECT previousRect = state->outRect;
        const bool rectOk =
            NavHoverFadePillRect(hwnd, state->outItem, &state->outRect);
        // The hold adds to the total time outItem stays alive (see
        // kNavHoverFadeOutHoldSeconds) -- without adding it here too, this
        // would clear outItem (and stop painting it) partway through its
        // own held-then-fading curve, popping it off mid-animation.
        const bool elapsed = now - state->outStartTime >=
            kNavHoverFadeDurationSeconds + kNavHoverFadeOutHoldSeconds;
        if (!rectOk || elapsed) {
            InvalidateRect(hwnd, &previousRect, FALSE);
            if (rectOk && !EqualRect(&previousRect, &state->outRect))
                InvalidateRect(hwnd, &state->outRect, FALSE);
            state->outItem = nullptr;
            state->outStartTime = 0.0;
        } else {
            if (!EqualRect(&previousRect, &state->outRect))
                InvalidateRect(hwnd, &previousRect, FALSE);
            InvalidateRect(hwnd, &state->outRect, FALSE);
            stillAnimating = true;
        }
    }

    if (!stillAnimating)
        NavHoverFadeStopTimer(hwnd, state);
    if (!state->hotItem && !state->outItem)
        NavHoverFadeDestroyState(hwnd, false);
}

static float NavHoverFadeProgressForWindow(HWND hwnd)
{
    NavHoverFadeState* state = NavHoverFadeGetState(hwnd);
    if (!state || state->startTime <= 0.0 || !NavHoverFadeSettingsEnabled())
        return 1.f;
    return NavHoverFadeProgress(
        *state, TimerGetSeconds());
}

// Set by GlyphSampleEraseColor (near DrawSvgGeom, much later in this file)
// on whichever window it last painted a glyph background for. Defined here,
// next to kTreeCursorSubclassProp, so the two subclasses that actually see
// every window a glyph background gets painted on -- nav-pane TreeViews via
// TreeCursorSubclassProc below, and the classic Places Bar toolbar via
// PlacesBarAnimSubclassProc -- can remove it in their own WM_NCDESTROY
// without needing a forward declaration.
static constexpr LPCWSTR kPropGlyphEraseWarm = L"Win32UIModernizer.GlyphEraseWarm";

static HCURSOR TreeArrowCursor()
{
    static HCURSOR s_arrow = LoadCursorW(nullptr, IDC_ARROW);
    return s_arrow ? s_arrow : LoadCursorW(nullptr, IDC_ARROW);
}

static LRESULT CALLBACK TreeCursorSubclassProc(HWND hWnd, UINT uMsg,
    WPARAM wParam, LPARAM lParam, DWORD_PTR dwRefData)
{
    UNREFERENCED_PARAMETER(dwRefData);

    if (const UINT resetMsg = g_navHoverFadeResetMessage.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
        resetMsg && uMsg == resetMsg) {
        TreePressedHoldReset(hWnd, false);
        NavHoverFadeDestroyState(
            hWnd,
            !g_msgWndUnloading.load(std::memory_order_acquire));
        return 0;
    }

    if ((uMsg == WM_LBUTTONDOWN || uMsg == WM_LBUTTONDBLCLK) &&
        g_settings.RoundedButtons) {
        TreePressedHoldBegin(hWnd, lParam);
        const LRESULT result = DefSubclassProc(hWnd, uMsg, wParam, lParam);
        // Explorer's namespace TreeView runs a modal click-tracking loop
        // inside WM_LBUTTONDOWN and consumes WM_LBUTTONUP itself. In that
        // path DefSubclassProc only returns after release and selection.
        if (!(GetKeyState(VK_LBUTTON) & 0x8000))
            TreePressedHoldCommitFromCursor(hWnd);
        NavHoverFadeSyncCursor(hWnd, true);
        return result;
    }

    if (uMsg == WM_LBUTTONUP) {
        const LRESULT result = DefSubclassProc(hWnd, uMsg, wParam, lParam);
        TreePressedHoldCommit(hWnd, lParam);
        NavHoverFadeSyncCursor(hWnd, true);
        return result;
    }

    if (uMsg == WM_MOUSEMOVE &&
        NavHoverTrackingEnabled()) {
        NavHoverFadeHandleMouseMove(hWnd, lParam);
    }

    if (uMsg == WM_MOUSELEAVE) {
        if (auto* state = NavHoverFadeGetState(hWnd)) {
            state->trackingLeave = false;
            if (NavHoverTrackingEnabled()) {
                NavHoverFadeRetarget(hWnd, nullptr);
            } else {
                NavHoverFadeDestroyState(
                    hWnd,
                    !g_msgWndUnloading.load(
                        std::memory_order_acquire));
            }
        }
    }

    if (uMsg == WM_TIMER &&
        wParam == NavHoverFadeTimerId()) {
        NavHoverFadeTimerTick(hWnd);
        return 0;
    }

    if (uMsg == WM_TIMER &&
        wParam == TreePressedHoldTimerId()) {
        TreePressedHoldTimerTick(hWnd);
        return 0;
    }

    if (uMsg == WM_SETTINGCHANGE || uMsg == WM_THEMECHANGED) {
        TreePressedHoldReset(hWnd, true);
        NavHoverFadeDestroyState(hWnd, true);
    }

    if (uMsg == WM_CANCELMODE || uMsg == WM_KILLFOCUS ||
        (uMsg == WM_CAPTURECHANGED && lParam != 0)) {
        TreePressedHoldReset(hWnd, true);
    }

    if (uMsg == WM_CAPTURECHANGED) {
        const LRESULT result = DefSubclassProc(hWnd, uMsg, wParam, lParam);
        NavHoverFadeSyncCursor(hWnd, true);
        return result;
    }

    if (uMsg == WM_SETCURSOR && LOWORD(lParam) == HTCLIENT
        && GlyphIsNavPaneTreeView(hWnd)) {
        SetCursor(TreeArrowCursor());
        return TRUE;
    }

    // TreeView can scroll its existing pixels before repainting exposed rows.
    // outRect then describes where our overlay was, while the copied pixels
    // can already be at the item's new bounds. Clear both locations before
    // dropping the fade; this stays much cheaper than invalidating the tree.
    if (uMsg == TVM_EXPAND || uMsg == TVM_ENSUREVISIBLE ||
        uMsg == WM_VSCROLL || uMsg == WM_HSCROLL ||
        uMsg == WM_MOUSEWHEEL || uMsg == WM_MOUSEHWHEEL ||
        uMsg == WM_KEYDOWN || uMsg == WM_SIZE) {
        const LRESULT result = DefSubclassProc(hWnd, uMsg, wParam, lParam);
        // TVM_ENSUREVISIBLE can be sent reentrantly by comctl32 while the
        // outer WM_LBUTTONUP is still committing selection. Preserve that
        // uncommitted press; only a released hold can leave copied pixels at
        // stale coordinates and needs cancellation here.
        TreePressedHoldCancelVisible(hWnd, true);
        if (NavHoverFadeState* state = NavHoverFadeGetState(hWnd);
            state && state->outItem) {
            const RECT previousRect = state->outRect;
            RECT currentRect = {};
            const bool currentRectValid =
                NavHoverFadePillRect(hWnd, state->outItem, &currentRect);
            InvalidateRect(hWnd, &previousRect, FALSE);
            if (currentRectValid) {
                if (!EqualRect(&previousRect, &currentRect))
                    InvalidateRect(hWnd, &currentRect, FALSE);
            } else {
                InvalidateRect(hWnd, nullptr, FALSE);
            }
            state->outItem = nullptr;
            state->outStartTime = 0.0;
            if (!state->hotItem)
                NavHoverFadeDestroyState(hWnd, false);
        }
        NavHoverFadeSyncCursor(hWnd, false);
        return result;
    }

    if (uMsg == WM_NCDESTROY) {
        TreePressedHoldReset(hWnd, false);
        NavHoverFadeDestroyState(hWnd, false);
        // DestroyWindow delivers the destroy messages directly, never
        // through SendMessageW, so this is where the tree's own image list
        // is freed.
        NavMetricsRestoreTree(hWnd, true);
        GlyphTreeOwnerCleanup(hWnd);
        RemovePropW(hWnd, kTreeCursorSubclassProp);
        RemovePropW(hWnd, kPropGlyphEraseWarm);
        WindhawkUtils::RemoveWindowSubclassFromAnyThread(hWnd, TreeCursorSubclassProc);
    }

    return DefSubclassProc(hWnd, uMsg, wParam, lParam);
}

static void TreeCursorTrySubclass(HWND hwnd)
{
    if (g_msgWndUnloading.load(std::memory_order_acquire) ||
        !g_settings.ExplorerSection ||
        !GlyphIsNavPaneTreeView(hwnd)) {
        return;
    }

    if (!GetPropW(hwnd, kTreeCursorSubclassProp) &&
        WindhawkUtils::SetWindowSubclassFromAnyThread(hwnd, TreeCursorSubclassProc, 0)) {
        SetPropW(hwnd, kTreeCursorSubclassProp, (HANDLE)1);
    }
}

// Lightweight WM_SETCURSOR-only counterpart for third-party trees where
// ApplyTreeRuntimeSettings forced TVS_TRACKSELECT: comctl32's own
// TREEVIEW_SetCursor (confirmed via Wine/ReactOS) sets a hand cursor over any
// hit item once that style is set and returns without reaching
// DefWindowProc, so nothing short of intercepting WM_SETCURSOR ourselves can
// restore the arrow. Reuses the same cached TreeArrowCursor() as
// TreeCursorSubclassProc, but skips all of its nav-pane hover-fade/glyph
// machinery -- this population is never the nav pane (see IsInsideExplorer/
// IsInsidePickerNamespaceTree in the caller).
static LRESULT CALLBACK TvTrackSelectCursorSubclassProc(HWND hWnd, UINT uMsg,
    WPARAM wParam, LPARAM lParam, DWORD_PTR)
{
    if (uMsg == WM_SETCURSOR && LOWORD(lParam) == HTCLIENT) {
        SetCursor(TreeArrowCursor());
        return TRUE;
    }
    if (uMsg == WM_NCDESTROY) {
        RemovePropW(hWnd, PROP_TV_TRACKSELECT_CURSOR_SUB);
        WindhawkUtils::RemoveWindowSubclassFromAnyThread(hWnd, TvTrackSelectCursorSubclassProc);
    }
    return DefSubclassProc(hWnd, uMsg, wParam, lParam);
}

static void TreeCursorRemoveFromWindow(HWND hwnd)
{
    if (GetPropW(hwnd, kTreeCursorSubclassProp)) {
        // Run timer/state cleanup on the tree's UI thread. The registered
        // message resets both hover fade and the short pressed hold.
        if (const UINT resetMsg =
                g_navHoverFadeResetMessage.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) {
            (void)SendMessageW(hwnd, resetMsg, 0, 0);
        } else {
            // If registration failed, sending WM_NULL wouldn't reach the
            // guarded handler. WM_CANCELMODE still reaches the subclass on
            // the owning UI thread and clears its thread-local pressed hold.
            (void)SendMessageW(hwnd, WM_CANCELMODE, 0, 0);
            if (GetPropW(hwnd, kPropNavHoverFadeState)) {
                NavHoverFadeDestroyState(
                    hwnd, !g_msgWndUnloading.load(std::memory_order_acquire));
            }
        }
        WindhawkUtils::RemoveWindowSubclassFromAnyThread(hwnd, TreeCursorSubclassProc);
        RemovePropW(hwnd, kTreeCursorSubclassProp);
    }
}

static BOOL CALLBACK TreeCursorRemoveChildEnum(HWND hwnd, LPARAM)
{
    TreeCursorRemoveFromWindow(hwnd);
    return TRUE;
}

// Sweeps every top-level window of this process when ExplorerSection is
// toggled off live -- nav-pane TreeViews are essentially always alive for
// the life of Explorer, so without this the subclass would otherwise
// outlive the setting until the window itself is destroyed.
static BOOL CALLBACK TreeCursorRemoveEnum(HWND hwnd, LPARAM)
{
    DWORD pid = 0;
    GetWindowThreadProcessId(hwnd, &pid);
    if (pid != GetCurrentProcessId())
        return TRUE;
    TreeCursorRemoveFromWindow(hwnd);
    EnumChildWindows(hwnd, TreeCursorRemoveChildEnum, 0);
    return TRUE;
}

// MODERN FOCUS RECTANGLE
// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

static std::mutex                       g_cbtHooksMutex;
// Per thread ID, with the creation time of the thread that ID belonged to: a
// thread that exits takes its hook with it, and a new thread can reuse the ID.
struct CbtThreadHook {
    HHOOK hook = nullptr;
    FILETIME created = {};
};
static std::unordered_map<DWORD, CbtThreadHook> g_cbtHooks;
// The calling thread already carries its hook: the common case, checked for
// free on every call. InitCbtHooks_Cleanup (unload, or both features turned
// off) bumps the generation, so a flag set before it no longer counts.
static thread_local bool t_cbtHookInstalled = false;
static thread_local unsigned t_cbtHookGeneration = 0;
static std::atomic<unsigned> g_cbtHooksGeneration{0};

// Callback for EnumChildWindows — applies dark mode to children of flyout windows



// WH_CBT rather than WH_CALLWNDPROC: a WH_CALLWNDPROC hook on a thread makes
// user32 route every same-thread SendMessage through the kernel instead of
// calling the window procedure directly (~2 us instead of ~0.06 us per call,
// in every process with a top-level window), and both users of this hook only
// need window creation. HCBT_CREATEWND also fires for the #32768 popups the
// kernel creates inside TrackPopupMenu, which NtUserCreateWindowEx_hook never
// sees. The window exists at that point but hasn't received WM_NCCREATE yet.
static LRESULT CALLBACK CbtProc(INT nCode, WPARAM wParam, LPARAM lParam)
{
    if (nCode == HCBT_CREATEWND)
    {
        const HWND hwnd = reinterpret_cast<HWND>(wParam);
        const CREATESTRUCTW* cs =
            reinterpret_cast<const CBT_CREATEWNDW*>(lParam)->lpcs;
        wchar_t cls[32] = {};
        GetClassNameW(hwnd, cls, ARRAYSIZE(cls));

        // ── Acrylic context menus ──────────────────────────────────────────
        // Everything MenuTryInstallAcrylic does (DWM attributes, composition
        // attribute, subclass) only needs the HWND; MN_SIZEWINDOW re-applies
        // once the popup has its size.
        if (g_settings.ModernContextMenus
            && (_wcsicmp(cls, MENUPOPUP_CLASS) == 0
                || _wcsicmp(cls, L"DropDown") == 0
                || _wcsicmp(cls, L"ViewControlClass") == 0)) {
            MenuTryInstallAcrylic(hwnd);
        }

        // ── Checkbox animation subclass ────────────────────────────────────
        // The check state isn't known yet (dialogs set it after creation);
        // CheckBoxSubclassProc reads it on the first WM_PAINT.
        if (g_settings.RoundedButtons && cs && _wcsicmp(cls, L"Button") == 0 &&
            !g_checkBoxAnimUnloading.load(std::memory_order_acquire))
        {
            const LONG style = cs->style & 0xFL;
            const bool isChk = (style == BS_CHECKBOX   || style == BS_AUTOCHECKBOX ||
                                style == BS_3STATE     || style == BS_AUTO3STATE);
            if (isChk)
            {
                bool hasSubclass;
                {
                    std::lock_guard<std::recursive_mutex> lk(g_checkAnimsMutex);
                    hasSubclass = g_checkAnims.find((ULONG_PTR)hwnd) != g_checkAnims.end();
                }
                if (!hasSubclass &&
                    WindhawkUtils::SetWindowSubclassFromAnyThread(
                        hwnd, CheckBoxSubclassProc, 0))
                {
                    CheckAnim ca;
                    ca.fromState = -1;
                    ca.progress  = 1.f;
                    ca.lastTick  = GetTickCount();
                    std::lock_guard<std::recursive_mutex> lk(g_checkAnimsMutex);
                    g_checkAnims[(ULONG_PTR)hwnd] = ca;
                }
            }
        }
    }
    return CallNextHookEx(nullptr, nCode, wParam, lParam);
}

// ── TrackPopupMenuEx hook — installs per-thread WH_CBT before the menu ──────
// The #32768 window is created INSIDE TrackPopupMenuEx. Our WH_CBT must be
// installed on the thread BEFORE this call, or HCBT_CREATEWND won't be seen.
static void InstallCbtHookForThread(DWORD tid = 0); // forward decl
static decltype(&TrackPopupMenuEx) TrackPopupMenuEx_orig = nullptr;
static BOOL WINAPI TrackPopupMenuEx_hook(HMENU hMenu, UINT uFlags, int x, int y,
    HWND hWnd, LPTPMPARAMS lptpm)
{
    if (g_settings.ModernContextMenus) {
        // A shell component can arrive after Wh_ModInit (notably in XAML
        // hosts). Only post the deferred symbol work here; never resolve or
        // apply hooks from inside TrackPopupMenuEx itself.
        MenuImmersiveRequestPendingHooks();
        InstallCbtHookForThread();
    }
    [[clang::musttail]] return TrackPopupMenuEx_orig(hMenu, uFlags, x, y, hWnd, lptpm);
}

static decltype(&TrackPopupMenu) TrackPopupMenu_orig = nullptr;
static BOOL WINAPI TrackPopupMenu_hook(HMENU hMenu, UINT uFlags, int x, int y,
    int nReserved, HWND hWnd, const RECT* prcRect)
{
    if (g_settings.ModernContextMenus) {
        MenuImmersiveRequestPendingHooks();
        InstallCbtHookForThread();
    }
    [[clang::musttail]] return TrackPopupMenu_orig(hMenu, uFlags, x, y, nReserved, hWnd, prcRect);
}


// Called from NtUserCreateWindowEx_hook to install a per-thread hook.
// Can install on ANY thread (not just the calling thread) by passing a
// thread ID.
// Creation time of a live thread, or false once it has exited.
static bool CbtThreadCreationTime(DWORD tid, FILETIME* created)
{
    HANDLE thread = OpenThread(THREAD_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION, FALSE, tid);
    if (!thread)
        return false;
    FILETIME exited, kernel, user;
    DWORD exitCode = 0;
    const bool alive =
        GetThreadTimes(thread, created, &exited, &kernel, &user) &&
        GetExitCodeThread(thread, &exitCode) && exitCode == STILL_ACTIVE;
    CloseHandle(thread);
    return alive;
}

static void InstallCbtHookForThread(DWORD tid)
{
    if (!g_settings.RoundedButtons && !g_settings.ModernContextMenus) return;
    const bool currentThread = tid == 0 || tid == GetCurrentThreadId();
    const unsigned generation =
        g_cbtHooksGeneration.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
    if (currentThread) {
        if (t_cbtHookInstalled && t_cbtHookGeneration == generation)
            return;
        tid = GetCurrentThreadId();
    }
    FILETIME created = {};
    if (!CbtThreadCreationTime(tid, &created))
        return;

    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(g_cbtHooksMutex);
    auto it = g_cbtHooks.find(tid);
    if (it != g_cbtHooks.end()) {
        if (CompareFileTime(&it->second.created, &created) == 0) {
            if (currentThread) {
                t_cbtHookInstalled = true;
                t_cbtHookGeneration = generation;
            }
            return;
        }
        // The ID now belongs to a newer thread; the old hook ended with the
        // thread it was installed on.
        g_cbtHooks.erase(it);
    }
    HHOOK h = SetWindowsHookExW(WH_CBT, CbtProc, nullptr, tid);
    if (!h)
        return;
    // Entries of exited threads are otherwise only replaced on ID reuse.
    if (g_cbtHooks.size() >= 256) {
        std::erase_if(g_cbtHooks, [](const auto& entry) {
            FILETIME alive = {};
            return !CbtThreadCreationTime(entry.first, &alive) ||
                CompareFileTime(&alive, &entry.second.created) != 0;
        });
    }
    g_cbtHooks[tid] = { h, created };
    if (currentThread) {
        t_cbtHookInstalled = true;
        t_cbtHookGeneration = generation;
    }
}

// EnumWindows callback for mod init: install CbtProc hooks on all
// existing top-level window threads. This catches processes/threads that
// were already running before the mod was loaded into them — their menus
// would otherwise never be detected because no new top-level window
// creation triggers InstallCbtHookForThread on those threads.
static BOOL CALLBACK MenuInitEnumProc(HWND hwnd, LPARAM)
{
    DWORD pid = 0;
    DWORD tid = GetWindowThreadProcessId(hwnd, &pid);
    if (pid != GetCurrentProcessId()) return TRUE;
    InstallCbtHookForThread(tid);
    return TRUE;
}

// ============================================================================
// Indeterminate progress bar detection
// OpenThemeData intercepts "Indeterminate::Progress" class to tag those hTheme
// handles. WindowFromDC on memory DCs returns NULL so we can't check at draw time.
// ============================================================================

static std::unordered_map<HTHEME, bool> g_indeterminateThemes; // used as set
static SRWLOCK                    g_indeterminateThemesLock = SRWLOCK_INIT;
static std::unordered_set<HTHEME> g_dragDropThemes;
static SRWLOCK                    g_dragDropThemesLock = SRWLOCK_INIT;

static decltype(&OpenThemeData)  OpenThemeData_orig  = nullptr;
static decltype(&CloseThemeData) CloseThemeData_orig = nullptr;

// Classes this mod has zero custom paint for (native rendering today, at
// most a GetThemeColor_hook text-color patch) get redirected to their real
// Microsoft-shipped DarkMode_DarkTheme:: counterpart -- full, pixel-correct
// dark art confirmed via the shipped theme data (same MINSIZE/
// SIZINGMARGINS/CONTENTMARGINS as the light class; only the bitmap resource
// and colors differ), with zero involvement from GetSysColor/SetSysColors.
// Rebar is deliberately NOT included here -- it's handled by
// PaintExplorerRebarMicaTintRect's own dark-literal fallback instead, kept
// separate to avoid re-touching the exact area a prior color regression was
// traced to.
// Tab is conditional: PaintTab already fully owns Tab rendering whenever
// IsWinUiTabStyleActive() (RoundedTabPane) is on, so redirecting then would
// just be redundant with (and risk diverging from) that custom paint. Only
// redirect when that setting is off, so a user who never turns on tab
// modernization still gets a properly dark tab strip instead of relying on
// the raw system color table.
//
// Header/ListView deliberately not redirected here: dui70.dll resolves its
// "Header"/"ListView" open to the real ItemsView:: light-theme classes,
// whose backgrounds are baked BGTYPE=IMAGEFILE bitmap art -- there's no
// FILLCOLOR property to redirect toward or recolor via GetThemeColor_hook
// for those parts. The native ItemsView::Header/ListView TEXTCOLOR values
// (e.g. RGB(76,96,122) for header column titles) already read fine as-is;
// only the baked-white background needs forcing dark, which the existing
// DrawThemeBackground(Ex)_hook FillRect patches below already do -- now
// scoped via IsPropertyDirectUIScope.
static LPCWSTR GetDarkThemeClassRedirect(LPCWSTR pszClassList, HWND hwnd)
{
    if (!pszClassList) return nullptr;
    if (_wcsicmp(pszClassList, L"Static") == 0) return L"DarkMode_DarkTheme::Static";
    if (_wcsicmp(pszClassList, L"Link") == 0)   return L"DarkMode_DarkTheme::Link";
    if (_wcsicmp(pszClassList, L"Tab") == 0 && !IsWinUiTabStyleActive())
        return L"DarkMode_DarkTheme::Tab";
    // Toolbar is deliberately NOT redirected here, unlike Static/Link/Tab:
    // GetThemeClass(hTheme) reflects whatever class string OpenThemeData was
    // actually called with, so redirecting to "DarkMode_DarkTheme::Toolbar"
    // would make every downstream `cls == L"Toolbar"` check in
    // HandleThemeDraw/DrawThemeBackground_hook (button hover-pressed fill,
    // mica tint, TravelBand dropdown glyph, ...) silently stop matching --
    // this class fails the "zero custom paint" precondition the other three
    // redirects rely on.
    (void)hwnd;
    return nullptr;
}

HTHEME WINAPI OpenThemeData_hook(HWND hwnd, LPCWSTR pszClassList)
{
    // Thread-local guard: OpenThemeData_orig can call OpenThemeData recursively
    // (for sub-themes). Without this guard, recursive calls would re-enter this
    // hook, causing infinite recursion and a stack-overflow crash.
    static thread_local bool s_running = false;
    if (s_running) {
        HTHEME hThemeRecursive = OpenThemeData_orig(hwnd, pszClassList);
        RecordThemeOpenerHwnd(hThemeRecursive, hwnd);
        return hThemeRecursive;
    }
    s_running = true;
    LPCWSTR effectiveClassList = pszClassList;
    if (hwnd) {
        if (LPCWSTR redirect = GetDarkThemeClassRedirect(pszClassList, hwnd)) {
            // g_darkModeActive, not IsHwndDarkMode(hwnd): these theme
            // requests (Static above all) fire constantly -- every label/
            // group box on every dialog paint -- and IsHwndDarkMode walks to
            // the top-level ancestor and calls DwmGetWindowAttribute, a real
            // dwm.exe RPC round trip, on every single call. Paying that on
            // this hot a path already caused one real UI-thread freeze
            // earlier on this branch (the pill/glyph recursion fix); this
            // mirrors that fix's safe pattern instead of repeating it.
            bool dark = g_darkModeExcluded
                ? (IsInsideExcludedFilePicker(hwnd) && IsSystemDarkMode())
                : g_darkModeActive.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
            if (dark)
                effectiveClassList = redirect;
        }
    }
    HTHEME hTheme = OpenThemeData_orig(hwnd, effectiveClassList);
    s_running = false;
    RecordThemeOpenerHwnd(hTheme, hwnd);
    if (hTheme && pszClassList && wcsstr(pszClassList, L"Indeterminate") != nullptr)
    {
        AcquireSRWLockExclusive(&g_indeterminateThemesLock);
        g_indeterminateThemes[hTheme] = true;
        ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&g_indeterminateThemesLock);
    }
    if (hTheme && pszClassList && wcsstr(pszClassList, L"DragDrop") != nullptr)
    {
        AcquireSRWLockExclusive(&g_dragDropThemesLock);
        g_dragDropThemes.insert(hTheme);
        ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&g_dragDropThemesLock);
    }
    return hTheme;
}

// ── OpenNcThemeData (uxtheme ordinal 49, undocumented) ──────────────────────
// Non-client-area theme data has its own separate entry point -- scrollbars
// specifically resolve their theme through this, not OpenThemeData, so the
// hook above never sees "ScrollBar" requests at all. This mod already paints
// its own WinUI-style scrollbar via HandleThemeDraw/D2D, so this redirect is
// deliberately just a fallback per the linked gist's technique: if that
// custom paint doesn't apply for some reason (an edge case not yet hit, a
// class this mod doesn't own), the scrollbar still comes out dark natively
// instead of falling back to whatever the live GetSysColor table currently
// holds. Redirects "ScrollBar" to "Explorer::ScrollBar" (hwnd=nullptr for
// that call, matching the well-known public dark-scrollbar trick) --
// uxtheme's own SetPreferredAppMode(AllowDark)-aware resolution (already
// active via g_setAppMode) then serves the dark variant on its own.
using OpenNcThemeData_t = HTHEME(WINAPI*)(HWND, LPCWSTR);
static OpenNcThemeData_t OpenNcThemeData_orig = nullptr;

static bool IsScrollbarThemeClassList(LPCWSTR classList)
{
    if (!classList) return false;
    const wchar_t* leaf = wcsrchr(classList, L':');
    return _wcsicmp(leaf ? leaf + 1 : classList, L"ScrollBar") == 0;
}

static void RecordNcThemeContext(
    HTHEME hTheme, HWND hwnd, LPCWSTR classList)
{
    RecordThemeOpenerHwnd(hTheme, hwnd);
    if (hTheme && IsScrollbarThemeClassList(classList) &&
        IsInsideExplorer(hwnd)) {
        MarkThemeAsExplorerScrollbar(hTheme);
    }
}

// DirectUI opens its themes through these (logged: HTHEMEs with no
// recorded opener); only the opener is recorded, the class list is not
// rewritten here.
static decltype(&OpenThemeDataEx) OpenThemeDataEx_orig = nullptr;
HTHEME WINAPI OpenThemeDataEx_hook(HWND hwnd, LPCWSTR pszClassList, DWORD dwFlags)
{
    HTHEME hTheme = OpenThemeDataEx_orig(hwnd, pszClassList, dwFlags);
    RecordThemeOpenerHwnd(hTheme, hwnd);
    return hTheme;
}

// Not in the import library: resolved by name at hook time.
using OpenThemeDataForDpi_t = HTHEME(WINAPI*)(HWND, LPCWSTR, UINT);
static OpenThemeDataForDpi_t OpenThemeDataForDpi_orig = nullptr;
HTHEME WINAPI OpenThemeDataForDpi_hook(HWND hwnd, LPCWSTR pszClassList, UINT dpi)
{
    HTHEME hTheme = OpenThemeDataForDpi_orig(hwnd, pszClassList, dpi);
    RecordThemeOpenerHwnd(hTheme, hwnd);
    return hTheme;
}

HTHEME WINAPI OpenNcThemeData_hook(HWND hwnd, LPCWSTR pszClassList)
{
    static thread_local bool s_running = false;
    if (s_running) {
        HTHEME hThemeRecursive = OpenNcThemeData_orig(hwnd, pszClassList);
        RecordNcThemeContext(hThemeRecursive, hwnd, pszClassList);
        return hThemeRecursive;
    }
    s_running = true;
    // g_darkModeActive, not a per-hwnd IsHwndDarkMode() walk: scrollbar NC
    // theme requests fire on every scroll tick, and IsHwndDarkMode's
    // DwmGetWindowAttribute RPC round trip on that hot a path already caused
    // a real UI-thread freeze once (see the pill/glyph recursion fix
    // earlier on this branch) -- this mirrors that fix's safe pattern.
    bool dark = g_darkModeExcluded
        ? (IsInsideExcludedFilePicker(hwnd) && IsSystemDarkMode())
        : g_darkModeActive.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
    HTHEME hTheme;
    if (hwnd && pszClassList && _wcsicmp(pszClassList, L"ScrollBar") == 0 && dark) {
        hTheme = OpenNcThemeData_orig(nullptr, L"Explorer::ScrollBar");
    } else {
        hTheme = OpenNcThemeData_orig(hwnd, pszClassList);
    }
    s_running = false;
    // Scrollbars obtain their theme through OpenNcThemeData, so recording
    // only OpenThemeData leaves their first buffered paints with no stable
    // HWND while WindowFromDC is still null. Preserve the original opener
    // even when the dark redirect deliberately calls uxtheme with nullptr.
    RecordNcThemeContext(hTheme, hwnd, pszClassList);
    return hTheme;
}

HRESULT WINAPI CloseThemeData_hook(HTHEME hTheme)
{
    static thread_local bool s_running = false;
    if (s_running) return CloseThemeData_orig(hTheme);
    s_running = true;
    HRESULT hr = CloseThemeData_orig(hTheme);
    s_running = false;
    if (hTheme)
    {
        {
            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(g_themeClassCacheMutex);
            g_themeClassCache.erase(hTheme);
        }
        ThemeClassCacheBump();
        {
            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(g_themeOpenerHwndMutex);
            g_themeOpenerHwnd.erase(hTheme);
            g_explorerScrollbarThemes.erase(hTheme);
        }

        AcquireSRWLockExclusive(&g_indeterminateThemesLock);
        g_indeterminateThemes.erase(hTheme);
        ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&g_indeterminateThemesLock);

        bool clearDragDropCache = false;
        AcquireSRWLockExclusive(&g_dragDropThemesLock);
        if (g_dragDropThemes.erase(hTheme) != 0 && g_dragDropThemes.empty())
            clearDragDropCache = true;
        ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&g_dragDropThemesLock);
        if (clearDragDropCache)
            DragDropBadgeCacheClear();
    }
    return hr;
}

static D2D1_COLOR_F ColorFAlpha(COLORREF c, float alpha = 1.f)
{
    return D2D1::ColorF(
        GetRValue(c) / 255.f,
        GetGValue(c) / 255.f,
        GetBValue(c) / 255.f,
        alpha);
}

// ============================================================================
// Disk chart accent color (ExplorerSection.DiskChartAccentColor)
// ============================================================================
// Recolors the disk usage chart and its legend swatches in drive Properties
// dialogs to the system accent color, with rounded swatch corners. Reuses
// this mod's own accent palette (GetAccentFromPalette) and per-window dark
// mode detection (IsWindowDarkMode) above instead of duplicating that logic
// — this also means the CustomAccentColor override applies here for free.
//
// The chart renders through GDI+, and its brushes may be cached between
// repaints, so hook the GDI+ fill calls and inspect the brush in hand.

#ifdef _WIN64
#   define DISKPIE_SSTDCALL           L"__cdecl"
#   define DISKPIE_SHELL32_DRAWPIE    L"DrawPie"
#   define DISKPIE_WPDSHEXT_DRAWPIE   L"void __cdecl _DrawPie(struct HDC__ *,struct tagRECT const *,unsigned int,unsigned int,unsigned long const *)"
#else
#   define DISKPIE_SSTDCALL           L"__stdcall"
#   define DISKPIE_SHELL32_DRAWPIE    L"_DrawPie@20"
#   define DISKPIE_WPDSHEXT_DRAWPIE   L"void __stdcall _DrawPie(struct HDC__ *,struct tagRECT const *,unsigned int,unsigned int,unsigned long const *)"
#endif

// Legend swatch control IDs on the drive properties page, relative to
// IDC_DRV_FIRST (0x3840).
constexpr int IDC_DRV_USEDCOLOR  = 0x3843;
constexpr int IDC_DRV_FREECOLOR  = 0x3844;
constexpr int IDC_DRV_CACHECOLOR = 697;

// Set for the duration of the original chart-drawing call so the GDI+ fill
// hooks below know it's safe to inspect/swap the requested color, and what
// HDC/usage fraction triggered it (per-window dark mode + full-disk bypass).
thread_local struct
{
    bool  active = false;
    HDC   hdc = nullptr;
    DWORD usagePer1000 = 0;
} g_diskPieState;

static bool DiskPieIsFull()
{
    return g_diskPieState.usagePer1000 >= 1000;
}

// The "used" slice's color, confirmed by on-screen inspection: #26A0DA.
static constexpr COLORREF kDiskPieUsedColor = RGB(0x26, 0xA0, 0xDA);

// The "free" slice's light-mode color, confirmed via probing: #ACACAC.
// Light mode keeps this as-is; dark mode swaps it for a color that actually
// reads well against a dark surface instead of looking washed out.
static constexpr COLORREF kDiskPieFreeColorLight = RGB(0xAC, 0xAC, 0xAC);
static constexpr COLORREF kDiskPieFreeColorDark  = RGB(0x37, 0x37, 0x37);

static bool DiskPieColorCloseTo(COLORREF c, COLORREF target, int tolerance)
{
    return abs((int)GetRValue(c) - (int)GetRValue(target)) <= tolerance &&
           abs((int)GetGValue(c) - (int)GetGValue(target)) <= tolerance &&
           abs((int)GetBValue(c) - (int)GetBValue(target)) <= tolerance;
}

static bool DiskPieIsUsedSliceColor(COLORREF c)
{
    // Small tolerance to absorb rounding/blending noise without being loose
    // enough to catch unrelated colors used elsewhere in the same call.
    return DiskPieColorCloseTo(c, kDiskPieUsedColor, 6);
}

static bool DiskPieIsFreeSliceColor(COLORREF c)
{
    return DiskPieColorCloseTo(c, kDiskPieFreeColorLight, 6);
}

// The donut's center hole isn't drawn with a color this mod picks -- it's
// native shell32/wpdshext code reading GetSysColor(COLOR_BTNFACE), which
// ApplyDarkSysColors has remapped process-wide to Win32MainDark (needed for the
// countless other unrelated consumers of that system color). That's the
// right shade for most contexts, but wrong specifically when the chart sits
// on a property-sheet page: those pages paint their own actual background
// as the lighter kElevatedPaneDark (see IsInsidePropSheetPage/DarkBgForPaint), so
// a hole filled with the darker global BTNFACE shade reads as a mismatched
// dark circle instead of blending in. Can't fix this by changing what
// COLOR_BTNFACE maps to (that would wrongly recolor everything else that
// reads it) -- has to be caught and swapped here, the same way the slice
// colors already are, scoped to just this one draw call.
static bool DiskPieIsHoleColor(COLORREF c)
{
    return DiskPieColorCloseTo(c, Win32MainDark, 4);
}

static UINT32 DiskPieColorRefToOpaqueArgb(COLORREF color)
{
    return 0xFF000000 |
        ((UINT32)GetRValue(color) << 16) |
        ((UINT32)GetGValue(color) << 8) |
        (UINT32)GetBValue(color);
}

// Shared by every fill-color hook below, regardless of which GDI+ call
// caught it. Returns the color unchanged if it isn't one of the two slices
// this mod cares about. No explicit "disk full" check is needed here: if
// the OS switches the chart to a warning color in that state, that color
// won't be within tolerance of either pattern below, so it already passes
// through untouched (unlike the legend's full-takeover swatch further
// down, which has no color check of its own and does need one).
static COLORREF DiskPieResolveColor(COLORREF color)
{
    if (DiskPieIsUsedSliceColor(color))
    {
        bool dark = IsWindowDarkMode(g_diskPieState.hdc);
        return GetAccentFillDefault(dark);
    }
    if (DiskPieIsFreeSliceColor(color) && IsWindowDarkMode(g_diskPieState.hdc))
    {
        return kDiskPieFreeColorDark; // Light mode keeps the original as-is.
    }
    if (DiskPieIsHoleColor(color) && IsWindowDarkMode(g_diskPieState.hdc))
    {
        HWND pieHwnd = g_tlsPaintHwnd ? g_tlsPaintHwnd : WindowFromDC(g_diskPieState.hdc);
        if (IsInsidePropSheetPage(pieHwnd))
            return kElevatedPaneDark;
    }
    return color;
}

// Resolved dynamically since gdiplus.dll's flat C exports aren't declared
// by any header included here.
using DiskPieGdipCreateSolidFill_t = int(WINAPI*)(UINT32, void**);
using DiskPieGdipGetBrushType_t = int(WINAPI*)(void*, int*);
using DiskPieGdipGetSolidFillColor_t = int(WINAPI*)(void*, UINT32*);
using DiskPieGdipDeleteBrush_t = int(WINAPI*)(void*);

static DiskPieGdipCreateSolidFill_t   g_pDiskPieGdipCreateSolidFill;
static DiskPieGdipGetBrushType_t      g_pDiskPieGdipGetBrushType;
static DiskPieGdipGetSolidFillColor_t g_pDiskPieGdipGetSolidFillColor;
static DiskPieGdipDeleteBrush_t       g_pDiskPieGdipDeleteBrush;

// Inspect the brush at GDI+ fill time, not creation time: the chart's fill
// brushes aren't necessarily (re)created on every repaint, but every
// repaint must call one of the Fill* functions below, so inspecting the
// brush there always sees the real color in use.
static void* DiskPieMaybeSwapGdipBrush(void* brush, bool* outOwned)
{
    *outOwned = false;
    if (!g_diskPieState.active || !brush || !g_pDiskPieGdipGetBrushType)
    {
        return brush;
    }

    int type = -1;
    if (g_pDiskPieGdipGetBrushType(brush, &type) != 0 /* Ok */)
    {
        return brush;
    }

    if (type != 0 /* BrushTypeSolidColor */ ||
        !g_pDiskPieGdipGetSolidFillColor || !g_pDiskPieGdipCreateSolidFill)
    {
        return brush;
    }

    UINT32 argb = 0;
    if (g_pDiskPieGdipGetSolidFillColor(brush, &argb) != 0)
    {
        return brush;
    }

    COLORREF color = RGB((argb >> 16) & 0xFF, (argb >> 8) & 0xFF, argb & 0xFF);
    COLORREF newColor = DiskPieResolveColor(color);
    if (newColor == color)
    {
        return brush;
    }

    void* newBrush = nullptr;
    if (g_pDiskPieGdipCreateSolidFill(DiskPieColorRefToOpaqueArgb(newColor), &newBrush) == 0 && newBrush)
    {
        *outOwned = true;
        return newBrush;
    }

    return brush;
}
