            const bool hotkey = editPaint.kind == LegacyRebarTextKind::DialogHotkey;
            if (search || hotkey || (options & ETO_GLYPH_INDEX)) {
                // Hosted edits can receive the same translated DirectUI DC.
                // Restore it before native fallback as well as after success.
                LegacyDialogTextDcScope dcScope(hdc, editPaint.kind, true);
                if (dcScope.ready) {
                    drawn = search ? DrawSearchEditTextDWrite(
                        hdc, x, y, options, lprect, lpString, c, lpDx)
                        : hotkey ? DrawHotkeyTextDWrite(
                            hdc, x, y, options, lprect, lpString, c, lpDx)
                        : DrawEditableGlyphTextDWrite(
                            hdc, x, y, options, lprect, lpString, c, lpDx);
                }
            }
            if (drawn)
                return TRUE;
            // Complex Search Unicode reaches GDI's shaping stage, whose
            // nested glyph call comes back here. Placeholder DrawText/DTT
            // callbacks keep their own path.
            // Measurements, unsupported fonts and opaque-only draws must not
            // enter a second caption/Mica renderer or change native advances.
            return ExtTextOutW_orig(hdc, x, y, options, lprect, lpString, c, lpDx);
        }
    }
    const bool legacyDrawn = TryDrawLegacyRebarExtText(
        hdc, x, y, options, lprect, lpString, c, lpDx);
    if (legacyDrawn)
        return TRUE;
    // Other DirectUI text elements can bypass DrawTextW. This caption path
    // accepts only simple clipped Unicode; glyphs/custom advances and opaque
    // backgrounds require the native contracts handled above or native GDI.
    constexpr UINT kSupportedExplorerEtoOptions = ETO_CLIPPED | ETO_RTLREADING;
    if (g_settings.ShellTextDirectWrite &&
        !IsTextPipelineDisabled() && g_duiExplorerTextPaintElement && hdc &&
        lpString && c > 0 && lprect && !lpDx &&
        (options & ETO_CLIPPED) &&
        !(GetTextAlign(hdc) & TA_UPDATECP) &&
        !(options & ~kSupportedExplorerEtoOptions)) {
        UINT format = DT_SINGLELINE | DT_TOP | DT_LEFT | DT_NOPREFIX;
        const UINT textAlign = GetTextAlign(hdc);
        if ((options & ETO_RTLREADING) || (textAlign & TA_RTLREADING))
            format |= DT_RTLREADING;

        const ShellTextExtPlacement placement = {
            x, y, textAlign};
        INT result = 0;
        if (DrawShellItemTextDWrite(
                hdc, lpString, static_cast<int>(c), lprect, format, 2,
                &result, g_duiExplorerTextWeightBoost, 0.0f, &placement)) {
            return TRUE;
        }
    }

    // ComboLBox's shaped runs are intercepted before glyph-index output in
    // NavTV_ScriptStringOut_hook. Unsupported glyph/advance contracts stay native.

    // ReBar search box: see IsInsideSearchEditBoxWrapper's own comment.
    // micaLightPath widens just the !g_darkModeActive term below for
    // ExplorerMicaBackdrop's light-mode text fix, reusing this whole
    // pipeline (simpleSafe, then DIB+AlphaBlend) instead of duplicating
    // it -- safe because micaNeedsGlow only goes true inside
    // MicaLightTextNeedsGlow's own narrow class scope, and the
    // very next check bails to ExtTextOutW_orig otherwise, so every other
    // light-mode caller is unaffected.
    bool micaLightPath = (ExplorerMicaActive() || RgMicaActive()) &&
        !g_darkModeActive;
    if (IsTextPipelineDisabled() || !hdc ||
        g_tlsIsAccentButton || g_glowEntry ||
        (!g_darkModeActive && !micaLightPath)) {
        [[clang::musttail]] return ExtTextOutW_orig(hdc, x, y, options, lprect, lpString, c, lpDx);
    }

    HWND dcHwnd = nullptr;
    HWND paintHwnd = g_tlsPaintHwnd;
    if (!paintHwnd) {
        dcHwnd = WindowFromDC(hdc);
        paintHwnd = dcHwnd;
    }
    if (IsAeroWizardRawWindow(paintHwnd) ||
        IsTaskbarThumbnailWindow(paintHwnd) ||
        IsInsideSearchEditBoxWrapper(paintHwnd)) {
        [[clang::musttail]] return ExtTextOutW_orig(hdc, x, y, options, lprect, lpString, c, lpDx);
    }

    HWND renamePaintHwnd = nullptr;
    if (micaLightPath && ListRenameHasActiveEdit()) {
        if (g_listRenameInHwndHostPaint && g_listRenamePaintEdit) {
            renamePaintHwnd = g_listRenamePaintEdit;
        } else {
            if (!dcHwnd)
                dcHwnd = WindowFromDC(hdc);
            renamePaintHwnd = dcHwnd ? dcHwnd : paintHwnd;
        }
    }
    if (renamePaintHwnd &&
        ListRenameGetKind(renamePaintHwnd) ==
            ListRenameKind::DirectUiDefView &&
        GetPropW(renamePaintHwnd, kListRenameActiveProp) &&
        ListRenameIsExactEdit(renamePaintHwnd)) {
        return ExtTextOutW_orig(
            hdc, x, y, options, lprect, lpString, c, lpDx);
    }
    const bool navigationRenamePaint = renamePaintHwnd &&
        ListRenameIsNativeControlKind(ListRenameGetKind(renamePaintHwnd)) &&
        GetPropW(renamePaintHwnd, kListRenameActiveProp) &&
        ListRenameIsExactEdit(renamePaintHwnd) &&
        ListRenameIsMicaNativeControlEdit(renamePaintHwnd);

    // The native Edit completes its Uniscribe draw before that hook
    // repairs alpha. Preserve every inner erase/glyph operation here so the
    // copied RGB contains the actual text and selection background.
    if (navigationRenamePaint) {
        return ExtTextOutW_orig(
            hdc, x, y, options, lprect, lpString, c, lpDx);
    }

    // Only the desktop ListView keeps custom label-edit rendering. It uses
    // the classic BeginPaint path and must not enter the DirectUI/Mica text
    // replacement below.
    renamePaintHwnd = nullptr;

    if (!lpString && !(options & ETO_GLYPH_INDEX))
        return ExtTextOutW_orig(hdc, x, y, options, lprect, lpString, c, lpDx);

    // c==0 with ETO_OPAQUE is the common GDI idiom for "fill lprect with the
    // current bk color", not a text draw -- no glyphs means no text-pipeline
    // work is needed here.
    if (c == 0)
        return ExtTextOutW_orig(hdc, x, y, options, lprect, lpString, c, lpDx);

    // Check text color — only process dark text (dark mode), or route a
    // genuine ExplorerMicaBackdrop light-mode match through unchanged --
    // see MicaLightTextNeedsGlow's own comment for why forcing a
    // different color there is wrong; only the pipeline routing changes.
    COLORREF origColor = GetTextColor(hdc);
    bool micaNeedsGlow =
        micaLightPath && MicaLightTextNeedsGlow(paintHwnd);
    COLORREF newClr = g_darkModeActive ? FixDarkTextColor(origColor) : origColor;
    // Same decisions as FixDarkTextColorForDc.
    if (g_darkModeActive) {
        COLORREF background;
        const bool opaque = (options & ETO_OPAQUE) || GetBkMode(hdc) == OPAQUE;
        if (opaque)
            background = GetBkColor(hdc);
        if (opaque || KnownCtlColorBackground(hdc, &background)) {
            newClr = newClr != origColor
                ? ReadableTextColorOn(newClr, origColor, background)
                : KeepVisibleOn(origColor, background);
        } else if (newClr != origColor) {
            // Bounds only for a DC whose pixels will be read.
            RECT drawRect = {};
            if (lprect)
                drawRect = *lprect;
            if (GetObjectType(hdc) == OBJ_MEMDC &&
                (lprect || ExtTextOutTextBounds(hdc, x, y, options,
                    lpString, c, lpDx, &drawRect, false)) &&
                MemoryDcTextBackground(hdc, drawRect, &background))
                newClr = ReadableTextColorOn(newClr, origColor, background);
        }
    }
    if (newClr == origColor && !micaNeedsGlow) {
        return ExtTextOutW_orig(hdc, x, y, options, lprect, lpString, c, lpDx);
    }

    // Known non-composited controls: simple SetTextColor (old method,
    // proven) -- skipped for micaNeedsGlow even when the class would
    // otherwise match (e.g. SysTreeView32): confirmed the nav pane also
    // renders over the real DWM-composited surface here, so it needs the
    // alpha-safe DIB+AlphaBlend pipeline below like DirectUIHWND does,
    // not this plain-SetTextColor shortcut.
    if (paintHwnd && !micaNeedsGlow) {
        wchar_t wc[64] = {};
        GetClassNameW(paintHwnd, wc, ARRAYSIZE(wc));
        bool simpleSafe = (_wcsicmp(wc, L"msctls_statusbar32") == 0 ||
                           _wcsicmp(wc, L"ComboBox") == 0 ||
                           _wcsicmp(wc, L"ComboLBox") == 0 ||
                           _wcsicmp(wc, L"ListBox") == 0 ||
                           _wcsicmp(wc, L"Static") == 0 ||
                           _wcsicmp(wc, L"SysListView32") == 0 ||
                           _wcsicmp(wc, L"SysTreeView32") == 0 ||
                           _wcsicmp(wc, L"SysHeader32") == 0 ||
                           wcsstr(wc, L"SysTabCtl") != nullptr);
        // ComboBox/ComboLBox: the DirectWrite attempt already ran above,
        // before the g_darkModeActive gate -- reaching here means it failed.

        if (simpleSafe) {
            SetTextColor(hdc, newClr);
            BOOL ret = ExtTextOutW_orig(hdc, x, y, options, lprect, lpString, c, lpDx);
            SetTextColor(hdc, origColor);
            return ret;
        }
    }

    // ETO_CLIPPED|ETO_OPAQUE with text → redirect to DrawTextW, only where
    // DrawTextW can keep the call's contract: default alignment (left, top,
    // no current position or RTL) and no custom spacing. The redirect fills
    // the opaque background itself, starts the text at (x, y) clipped to
    // lprect, and draws '&' literally. Anything else takes the generic
    // pipeline below, which keeps x/y, alignment, lpDx and the fill.
    if (options == (ETO_CLIPPED | ETO_OPAQUE) && lprect && lpString) {
        const UINT align = GetTextAlign(hdc);
        const bool plainPlacement = !lpDx &&
            !(align & (TA_RIGHT | TA_CENTER | TA_BOTTOM | TA_BASELINE |
                       TA_UPDATECP | TA_RTLREADING));
        if (DrawTextW_orig && plainPlacement) {
            ExtTextOutW_orig(hdc, 0, 0, ETO_OPAQUE, lprect, nullptr, 0, nullptr);
            const int savedDc = SaveDC(hdc);
            IntersectClipRect(hdc, lprect->left, lprect->top,
                              lprect->right, lprect->bottom);
            const int oldBkMode = SetBkMode(hdc, TRANSPARENT);
            RECT rect = { x, y, std::max<LONG>(lprect->right, x),
                          std::max<LONG>(lprect->bottom, y) };
            const BOOL result = (BOOL)DrawTextW_hook(hdc, lpString, c, &rect,
                DT_LEFT | DT_TOP | DT_SINGLELINE | DT_NOPREFIX | DT_NOCLIP);
            if (oldBkMode)
                SetBkMode(hdc, oldBkMode);
            if (savedDc)
                RestoreDC(hdc, savedDc);
            return result;
        }
    }

    if (options & ETO_OPAQUE && !lprect)
        return ExtTextOutW_orig(hdc, x, y, options, lprect, lpString, c, lpDx);

    // DIB + AlphaBlend pipeline (GLOBAL — no class filter)

    RECT textRect = {};
    if (lprect && !(options == ETO_OPAQUE && ((lprect->right - lprect->left) == 1 || (lprect->bottom - lprect->top) == 1))) {
        textRect = *lprect;
    } else if (options) {
        if (!ExtTextOutTextBounds(hdc, x, y, options, lpString, c, lpDx, &textRect))
            return ExtTextOutW_orig(hdc, x, y, options, lprect, lpString, c, lpDx);
    } else {
        return ExtTextOutW_orig(hdc, x, y, options, lprect, lpString, c, lpDx);
    }

    INT tw = textRect.right - textRect.left;
    INT th = textRect.bottom - textRect.top;
    if (tw <= 0 || th <= 0)
        return ExtTextOutW_orig(hdc, x, y, options, lprect, lpString, c, lpDx);

    // OS-pooled DIB via the buffered-paint API instead of a fresh
    // CreateCompatibleDC+CreateDIBSection every call -- this fires on nearly
    // every text draw in the process (PROF_ExtTextOutW). Its memDC uses the
    // same coordinate space as hdc/textRect (see DrawTextW_hook's own use of
    // it above), so draw at absolute coordinates, not origin-relative.
    // BPPF_NOCLIP: don't inherit hdc's clip region, or the mask can get cut off.
    BP_PAINTPARAMS bpParams = { sizeof(BP_PAINTPARAMS) };
    bpParams.dwFlags = BPPF_ERASE | BPPF_NOCLIP;
    HDC memDC = nullptr;
    HPAINTBUFFER hpb = BeginBufferedPaint(hdc, &textRect, BPBF_TOPDOWNDIB, &bpParams, &memDC);
    if (!hpb || !memDC)
        return ExtTextOutW_orig(hdc, x, y, options, lprect, lpString, c, lpDx);

    RGBQUAD* pPixels = nullptr;
    int rowWidth = 0; // stride in RGBQUADs, not bytes -- may exceed tw
    if (FAILED(GetBufferedPaintBits(hpb, &pPixels, &rowWidth))) {
        EndBufferedPaint(hpb, FALSE);
        return ExtTextOutW_orig(hdc, x, y, options, lprect, lpString, c, lpDx);
    }

    SelectObject(memDC, GetCurrentObject(hdc, OBJ_FONT));
    const UINT textAlign = GetTextAlign(hdc);
    SetTextAlign(memDC, textAlign);
    // TA_UPDATECP draws at the current position and advances it: carried
    // into the buffer, and the advanced one back to the caller's DC.
    POINT currentPosition = {};
    const bool updatesPosition = (textAlign & TA_UPDATECP) &&
        GetCurrentPositionEx(hdc, &currentPosition);
    if (updatesPosition)
        MoveToEx(memDC, currentPosition.x, currentPosition.y, nullptr);

    COLORREF origBkColor = GetBkColor(hdc);
    COLORREF highlightClr = GetSysColor(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT);
    // The opaque fill goes to hdc only: in the mask buffer the background's
    // luminance would turn into text alpha over the whole rectangle.
    if (options & ETO_OPAQUE && lprect) {
        HBRUSH bkBr = CreateSolidBrush(origBkColor);
        if (bkBr) {
            FillRect_orig(hdc, lprect, bkBr);
            DeleteObject(bkBr);
        }
    }

    SetBkMode(memDC, TRANSPARENT);
    SetTextColor(memDC, RGB(255, 255, 255)); // white mask

    g_glowEntry = true;
    BOOL res = ExtTextOutW_orig(memDC, x, y, options & ~ETO_OPAQUE, lprect, lpString, c, lpDx);
    g_glowEntry = false;
    if (updatesPosition && GetCurrentPositionEx(memDC, &currentPosition))
        MoveToEx(hdc, currentPosition.x, currentPosition.y, nullptr);
    // Colorize: gamma-corrected white-mask luminance as alpha. AC_SRC_ALPHA
    // needs a premultiplied source (rgb = color*alpha/255, dst stays 0) --
    // only highlighted/selected text bakes origBkColor in, forcing alpha=255
    // so AlphaBlend copies it straight instead of blending twice.
    const auto& gammaLUT = TextAlphaGammaLUT();
    BYTE txtR = GetRValue(newClr), txtG = GetGValue(newClr), txtB = GetBValue(newClr);
    bool highlightedText = (options & ETO_OPAQUE) &&
        origBkColor == highlightClr;
    BYTE dstR = highlightedText ? GetRValue(origBkColor) : 0;
    BYTE dstG = highlightedText ? GetGValue(origBkColor) : 0;
    BYTE dstB = highlightedText ? GetBValue(origBkColor) : 0;

    for (INT cy = 0; cy < th; ++cy) {
        RGBQUAD* row = pPixels + (size_t)cy * rowWidth;
        for (INT cx = 0; cx < tw; ++cx) {
            RGBQUAD& p = row[cx];
            BYTE luma = (BYTE)((p.rgbRed * 54 + p.rgbGreen * 183 + p.rgbBlue * 19) >> 8);
            BYTE alpha = gammaLUT[luma];
            if (!alpha) continue;
            p.rgbBlue = (BYTE)((txtB * alpha +
                dstB * (255 - alpha)) >> 8);
            p.rgbGreen = (BYTE)((txtG * alpha +
                dstG * (255 - alpha)) >> 8);
            p.rgbRed = (BYTE)((txtR * alpha +
                dstR * (255 - alpha)) >> 8);
            p.rgbReserved = highlightedText ? 255 : alpha;
        }
    }

    BLENDFUNCTION blend = { AC_SRC_OVER, 0, 255, AC_SRC_ALPHA };
    AlphaBlend(
        hdc, textRect.left, textRect.top, tw, th,
        memDC, textRect.left, textRect.top, tw, th, blend);
    EndBufferedPaint(hpb, FALSE);
    return res;
}
HRESULT WINAPI GetThemeColor_hook(HTHEME hTheme, int iPartId, int iStateId,
    int iPropId, COLORREF* pColor)
{
    HRESULT hr = GetThemeColor_orig(hTheme, iPartId, iStateId, iPropId, pColor);

    // ListView group header text -> GroupHeaderTextColor, checked before the FAILED(hr)
    // bailout below. Live logging showed the two hosts query DIFFERENT
    // color properties: DirectUI (modern Explorer) asks for
    // TMT_HEADING1TEXTCOLOR (3825) and succeeds; classic comctl32
    // ListViews (e.g. a common-dialog file picker) ask for plain
    // TMT_TEXTCOLOR (3803) and the theme has no such value for this part,
    // so GetThemeColor_orig fails outright (0x80070490, "not found") --
    // bailing out on FAILED(hr) as usual meant this branch could never
    // even be reached for the classic path. Own settings gate (not tied
    // to dark mode/AccentColorize) since this is RoundedButtons-
    // specific, and forced regardless of hr since we don't need the
    // original value either way.
    if (pColor && g_settings.RoundedButtons && iPartId == LVP_GROUPHEADER &&
        (iPropId == TMT_TEXTCOLOR || iPropId == TMT_HEADING1TEXTCOLOR) &&
        IsListViewThemeClass(GetCachedThemeClass(hTheme))) {
        // LVP_GROUPHEADER on a real ListView/ItemsView theme class only ever
        // means genuine shell UI, never a host app's own control -- this
        // call fires once, early, during DirectUI's style-resolution pass,
        // well before the group header's first real WM_PAINT, so
        // g_tlsPaintHwnd here can be a stale or already-destroyed handle
        // from an unrelated window. Narrowing by
        // IsInsideExcludedFilePicker(g_tlsPaintHwnd), like every other
        // exclusion check in this file, isn't safe here since that stale
        // hwnd fails the file-picker match even while genuinely inside
        // one. Key off g_darkModeExcluded instead of any hwnd: an excluded
        // host's own picker still follows the real system dark-mode
        // setting no matter which window hosts it.
        bool ghDark;
        if (g_darkModeExcluded) {
            ghDark = IsSystemDarkMode();
        } else {
            HWND ghPaintHwnd = g_tlsPaintHwnd;
            ghDark = ghPaintHwnd ? IsHwndDarkMode(ghPaintHwnd) : IsSystemDarkMode();
        }
        *pColor = GroupHeaderTextColor(ghDark);
        return S_OK;
    }

    // Tab control text, same "not found" case as LVP_GROUPHEADER above --
    // GetThemeColor_orig fails outright for TABP_TOPTABITEM(_*EDGE) +
    // TMT_TEXTCOLOR (confirmed via live logging: 0x80070490), so this can't
    // wait for the FAILED(hr) bailout below either. Real DrawThemeTextEx
    // masks this by ignoring the caller's DTT_TEXTCOLOR for this part and
    // using its own internal dark color -- fine for that GDI path, but
    // DrawWinUiStyledTextDWrite draws independently of DrawThemeTextEx and
    // needs a real value from this call, not whatever uxtheme silently
    // substitutes later.
    if (pColor && iPropId == TMT_TEXTCOLOR &&
        GetCachedThemeClass(hTheme) == L"Tab") {
        const bool tabDark = g_darkModeActive;
        if (iStateId == 3 /*CSTB_SELECTED*/)
            *pColor = tabDark ? RGB(255, 255, 255) : RGB(0, 0, 0);
        else // CSTB_HOT and normal share the same dimmed shade
            *pColor = tabDark ? RGB(0xCC, 0xCC, 0xCC) : RGB(0x5C, 0x5C, 0x5C);
        return S_OK;
    }

    // TreeView item text in dark mode, the same "not found" case as the two
    // branches above: the dark tree theme defines no TMT_TEXTCOLOR for
    // TREIS_HOT, so GetThemeColor_orig fails (0x80070490, measured live) and
    // leaves *pColor at zero -- which is the black a hovered item renders.
    // The TreeView branch further down never sees this, because the FAILED(hr)
    // bailout right below returns first; widening that branch's black test
    // would have changed nothing, since it is never reached. Only the failing
    // states are answered here, so every state the theme does define (normal
    // already answers white) keeps coming from the theme. Dark only: light
    // mode has no such gap, the fallback black being correct there anyway.
    if (pColor && FAILED(hr) && g_darkModeActive &&
        iPropId == TMT_TEXTCOLOR &&
        GetCachedThemeClass(hTheme).find(L"TreeView") != std::wstring::npos) {
        *pColor = RGB(255, 255, 255);
        return S_OK;
    }

    if (!pColor || FAILED(hr)) return hr;

    const std::wstring& cls = GetCachedThemeClass(hTheme);
    HWND themePaintHwnd = g_tlsPaintHwnd;

    // The visible preview/reading pane surface comes from ReadingPane part 1
    // (BACKGROUNDCOLORS), not PreviewPane's image-backed PREVIEWBACKGROUND:
    // Tema.txt exposes this part's FILLCOLOR as white in light mode and #202020
    // in dark mode. DirectUI queries the color independently of its eventual
    // paint DC, so override the theme property itself, as with ItemsView and
    // ProperTree below. The class is shell-specific and shared by Explorer and
    // Common Item Dialogs; accept both the plain and sub-app-prefixed names.
    if (ExplorerBackdropMode() && iPartId == 1 &&
        iPropId == TMT_FILLCOLOR &&
        (cls == L"ReadingPane" || cls.ends_with(L"::ReadingPane"))) {
        *pColor = FilePickerPaneColor(g_darkModeActive);
        return S_OK;
    }

    // Tema.txt confirms TEXTCOLOR on the common properties of both
    // ExplorerStatusBar and DarkMode::ExplorerStatusBar. COLORREF carries no
    // alpha, so use the WinUI foregrounds flattened against this bar's known
    // secondary-Mica base instead of losing #9E/#C5 in the theme pipeline.
    if (ExplorerBackdropMode() && iPropId == TMT_TEXTCOLOR &&
        IsCurrentProcessExplorer() &&
        cls.find(L"ExplorerStatusBar") != std::wstring::npos) {
        *pColor = ExplorerMicaStatusBarTextColor(g_darkModeActive);
        return S_OK;
    }

    // The picker's file list background: DirectUI fills the list host's
    // root with ItemsView's FILLCOLOR (#FFFFFF, DarkMode:: #191919 -- Tema
    // Msstyles.txt), resolved at the view's creation through a theme opened
    // on the view host / DefView (OpenThemeDataForDpi, logged), and again
    // from the list host's own paints; the bracket and the painting window
    // cover the latter. In explorer.exe (pickers of its own dialogs, e.g.
    // Extract) its file list shares that HTHEME, so only the two per-window
    // signals count there, never the opener.
    if (FilePickerListShaded() && iPropId == TMT_FILLCOLOR &&
        cls.find(L"ItemsView") != std::wstring::npos &&
        (t_filePickerListHostDepth > 0 ||
         IsFilePickerListWindow(themePaintHwnd) ||
         (!IsCurrentProcessExplorer() &&
          IsFilePickerViewThemeOpener(GetThemeOpenerHwnd(hTheme))))) {
        *pColor = FilePickerListColor(g_darkModeActive);
        return S_OK;
    }


    bool accentDark = false;
    bool accentDarkResolved = false;
    auto isAccentDark = [&]() -> bool {
        if (!accentDarkResolved) {
            accentDark = themePaintHwnd ? IsHwndDarkMode(themePaintHwnd)
                                        : IsSystemDarkMode();
            accentDarkResolved = true;
        }
        return accentDark;
    };
    // Link text: AccentTextFillColor Primary / Secondary (hover) / Tertiary
    // (pressed), as HyperlinkButton uses them (Common_themeresources_any.xaml):
    // Light3 / Light3 / Light2 dark, Dark2 / Dark3 / Dark1 light.
    auto accentNormal = [&]() -> COLORREF {
        return GetAccentFromPalette(isAccentDark() ? 0 : 20);
    };
    auto accentHot = [&]() -> COLORREF {
        return GetAccentFromPalette(isAccentDark() ? 0 : 24);
    };
    auto accentPressed = [&]() -> COLORREF {
        return GetAccentFromPalette(isAccentDark() ? 4 : 16);
    };

    // Explorer first: isAccentDark() resolves the window's mode.
    if (pColor && iPropId == TMT_TEXTCOLOR && IsCurrentProcessExplorer() &&
        ControlPanelTextRecolorActive(isAccentDark())) {
        // Control Panel's page title takes the color of Explorer's group
        // headers, in both themes.
        if (iPartId == CPANEL_TITLE && cls == L"ControlPanelStyle") {
            *pColor = GroupHeaderTextColor(isAccentDark());
            return S_OK;
        }
        // The view button beside it (CommandModule's library-pane top view)
        // carries a native link blue: the accent replaces it in both themes.
        if (iPartId == 9 && cls == L"CommandModule" && SUCCEEDED(hr)) {
            const BYTE b2 = GetBValue(*pColor), r2 = GetRValue(*pColor);
            if ((b2 > 100 && r2 < 128 && b2 > r2 + 30) || g_settings.AccentColorize) {
                *pColor = (iStateId == 1) ? accentNormal() :
                          (iStateId == 2) ? accentHot() :
                          (iStateId == 3) ? accentPressed() : RGB(96, 96, 96);
                return S_OK;
            }
        }
    }

    // DarkMode_DarkTheme::Link's HyperLink part (confirmed via the shipped
    // theme dump: Part "HyperLink", part id 1) bakes a fixed RGB(68,101,162)
    // dark blue TEXTCOLOR -- identical to plain "Link"'s own value, i.e.
    // genuinely not accent-aware, same fixed-color category already
    // documented for DarkMode_Explorer's ComboBox/ProperTree parts below.
    // This class only reaches here via OpenThemeData_hook's Tier 1b
    // redirect (real "Link" never resolves to this class name), so no
    // extra dark-mode gate is needed -- the redirect itself already only
    // fires when dark.
    if (cls == L"DarkMode_DarkTheme::Link" && iPartId == LP_HYPERLINK &&
        iPropId == TMT_TEXTCOLOR) {
        *pColor = accentNormal();
        return S_OK;
    }

    // DarkMode_Explorer returns #383838 (normal) / #0078D4 (hot) for
    // CP_DROPDOWNITEM fill. Replace the dark background, and recolor the
    // hover accent in light mode only when AccentColorize is enabled.
    // Uses GetSystemAccentColor() -- the plain, non-indicator-specific
    // accent already used for AccentColorize/AccentMarquee elsewhere --
    // instead of a combobox-only light/dark-tuned pair (accentHot's
    // offsets 0/12) picked just for this one item.
    if ((cls == L"ComboBox" || cls == L"Combobox") &&
        iPartId == 9 /*CP_DROPDOWNITEM*/ && iPropId == TMT_FILLCOLOR &&
        (g_darkModeActive || g_settings.AccentColorize)) {
        if (g_darkModeActive && iStateId == 1) {
            *pColor = Win32MainDark;
        } else if (iStateId == 2) {
            *pColor = GetSystemAccentColor();
        } else {
            return hr;
        }
        return S_OK;
    }

    // ExplorerMicaBackdrop: force literal black for the fills DWM needs
    // unpainted/black to reveal a real Mica backdrop through (confirmed
    // against the live theme dump and a throwaway test mod). Both modes --
    // Mica requires black regardless of light/dark. Independent of and
    // takes priority over the
    // ProperTree branch below.
    // Gated by process, not per-call hwnd: GetThemeColor has no HWND/HDC
    // parameter, so any per-call resolution (GetThemeOpenerHwnd, TLS) is a
    // best-effort cache that goes stale or empty for calls outside a live
    // paint bracket (confirmed empirically -- real Explorer nav pane/status
    // bar/ItemsView coverage was consistently partial with that gate, and
    // went to fully correct the moment it was removed). IsCurrentProcessMMC
    // is the established precedent for this same tradeoff elsewhere in this
    // file. Residual scope risk: a file Properties dialog's Previous
    // Versions tab (ItemsView Common Properties, see IsPropertyDirectUIScope
    // below) can host in-process with real Explorer windows rather than
    // rundll32.exe, so its list background would go black here too even
    // without a real Mica backdrop behind it -- narrowed below.
    if (ExplorerBackdropMode() && iPropId == TMT_FILLCOLOR &&
        IsCurrentProcessExplorer() &&
        (cls.find(L"ProperTree") != std::wstring::npos ||
         cls.find(L"ItemsView") != std::wstring::npos ||
         cls.find(L"ExplorerNavPane") != std::wstring::npos ||
         cls.find(L"ExplorerStatusBar") != std::wstring::npos)) {
        // Best-effort ADDITIONAL exclusion, never the primary gate: only
        // skips the black fill when a real Explorer/#32770 dialog window can
        // actually be resolved for THIS call. When resolution fails (the
        // common case that broke the old per-call hwnd gate above), this
        // simply falls through to black same as before -- it can narrow the
        // Properties-dialog leak, never reopen the nav-pane/status-bar bug,
        // since neither of those is ever #32770-rooted.
        HWND drawHwnd = g_tlsThemeDrawHwnd;
        if (!drawHwnd) drawHwnd = GetThemeOpenerHwnd(hTheme);
        if (!drawHwnd) drawHwnd = themePaintHwnd;
        HWND excludeRoot = drawHwnd ? GetAncestor(drawHwnd, GA_ROOT) : nullptr;
        wchar_t excludeCls[16] = {};
        bool isDialogHost = excludeRoot &&
            GetClassNameW(excludeRoot, excludeCls, ARRAYSIZE(excludeCls)) &&
            _wcsicmp(excludeCls, L"#32770") == 0;
        if (!isDialogHost) {
            // Status bar specifically uses a slightly lighter near-black
            // instead of literal black -- pure black under Mica's own
            // reveal came out noticeably more purple/saturated (~#383744
            // against real wallpaper testing) than WinUI's own lighter Mica
            // base shade (~#2c2a32 on the same wallpaper). #0C0C0C (dark
            // mode) and #080808 (light mode) are linear estimates of how
            // much lighter WinUI's own secondary Mica base shade (#2c2c2c
            // dark / #fbfbfb light) is than Mica's primary base (#202020
            // dark / #f3f3f3 light), reapplied from pure black -- confirmed
            // against real wallpaper testing in dark mode; light mode
            // follows the same method but is unverified so far.
            if (ExplorerOpaqueMode()) {
                // Opaque shades: status bar on the chrome, list on the
                // lifted pane color, nav pane (ProperTree/ExplorerNavPane)
                // on the pane shade.
                if (cls.find(L"ExplorerStatusBar") != std::wstring::npos)
                    *pColor = FilePickerChromeColor(g_darkModeActive);
                else if (cls.find(L"ItemsView") != std::wstring::npos)
                    *pColor = ExplorerMicaPaneSolidColor(g_darkModeActive);
                else
                    *pColor = FilePickerPaneColor(g_darkModeActive);
            } else if (cls.find(L"ExplorerStatusBar") != std::wstring::npos) {
                *pColor = ExplorerMicaSecondaryRevealColor(g_darkModeActive);
            } else if (ExplorerMicaPaneMode() &&
                       cls.find(L"ItemsView") != std::wstring::npos) {
                *pColor = ExplorerMicaPaneRevealColor(g_darkModeActive);
            } else {
                *pColor = RGB(0, 0, 0);
            }
            return S_OK;
        }
    }

    // DarkMode_Explorer hardcodes "ProperTree" (nav-pane TreeView) fill to
    // #131313/#121212 instead of the shell shade -- shows as a seam against
    // the adjacent native file list.
    if (cls == L"ProperTree" && iPropId == TMT_FILLCOLOR && g_darkModeActive) {
        *pColor = ExplorerDarkColor;
        return S_OK;
    }

    // ListView/ItemsView Common Properties FILLCOLOR — the DUI-hosted
    // Previous Versions tab list opens its theme through a multi-class
    // fallback list (e.g. "ItemsView::ListView;ItemsView;ListView"); its
    // primary ItemsView::ListView class declares no FILLCOLOR at all for
    // this part, so uxtheme falls through to whichever later class in the
    // list does — plain "ItemsView" and plain "ListView" both declare a
    // real (255,255,255) FILLCOLOR here (confirmed in the shipped theme
    // dump), so GetCachedThemeClass can come back as either depending on
    // which one actually supplied it. Unlike Header's Common Properties/
    // HEADERITEM background (baked BGTYPE=IMAGEFILE bitmap art, no
    // FILLCOLOR to redirect at all), these really are plain recolorable
    // fills. Scoped to the property-dialog DUI list only — real Explorer
    // SysListView32 controls get their dark background through
    // SetExplorerFamilyTheme/DarkMode_Explorer instead, not this hook.
    // Scope via the hwnd this HTHEME was actually opened with (reliable at
    // any time), not themePaintHwnd/g_tlsPaintHwnd alone -- that TLS value
    // is only meaningful inside a BeginPaint bracket, and DUI's very first
    // FILLCOLOR resolution for a freshly created list (e.g. first time the
    // Previous Versions tab is ever activated in a dialog) can happen
    // during style/layout setup, outside any paint call, when
    // g_tlsPaintHwnd may still hold a stale hwnd from unrelated painting
    // elsewhere in the process. That mismatch made IsPropertyDirectUIScope
    // fail on that one query, producing a native white flash that only
    // cleared once a real WM_PAINT re-resolved the color correctly -- and
    // never recurred on tab switches after that, since the list's style is
    // cached from then on. Falls back to themePaintHwnd if the opener
    // wasn't recorded (e.g. hwnd was null at OpenThemeData time).
    HWND fillColorHwnd = GetThemeOpenerHwnd(hTheme);
    if (!fillColorHwnd) fillColorHwnd = themePaintHwnd;
    if (iPartId == 0 /*COMMONPROPS*/ && iPropId == TMT_FILLCOLOR &&
            (cls.find(L"ListView") != std::wstring::npos ||
             cls.find(L"ItemsView") != std::wstring::npos) &&
            IsPropertyDirectUIScope(fillColorHwnd)) {
        *pColor = Win32MainDark;
        return S_OK;
    }

    // Tooltip text color — check owner window's dark mode (not tooltip's own)
    if (g_settings.ModernTooltips && cls == L"Tooltip" && iPropId == TMT_TEXTCOLOR) {
        if (iPartId == TTP_STANDARD || iPartId == TTP_BALLOON) {
            HWND hTT = g_tlsPaintHwnd;
            HWND owner = hTT ? GetWindow(hTT, GW_OWNER) : nullptr;
            bool dark = owner ? IsHwndDarkMode(owner)
                              : (hTT ? IsHwndDarkMode(hTT) : IsSystemDarkMode());
            // ToolTipForeground: TextFillColorPrimary over the tooltip's
            // AcrylicInAppFillColorDefault surface (#FFFFFF dark, #1A1A1A light).
            *pColor = WinUI::FlattenOver(WinUI::TextFillColorPrimary(dark),
                WinUiFloatingSurfaceColor(dark));
        }
    }

    // ── Acrylic context menus: force theme fill colors ──────────────────
    // The system reads TMT_FILLCOLOR from the Menu theme to fill the entire
    // client before drawing items via DrawThemeBackground -- a shade that
    // would sit visibly on top of the backdrop in either theme. Black only
    // for DWM-transparent menus; with transparency off, the surface's own
    // opaque shade, so the menu does not become flat black.
    //
    // This is the query with no DC at all, which is why the popup has to be
    // named from the subclass bracket; see MenuPopupBeingPainted.
    if (g_settings.ModernContextMenus && cls == L"Menu" &&
        (iPropId == TMT_FILLCOLOR || iPropId == TMT_FILLCOLORHINT) &&
        !IsLegacyShellDropdownRoot(g_tlsPaintHwnd) &&
        MenuSurfaceIsOwned(MenuPopupBeingPainted(nullptr),
                           /*answerWhenUnnamed=*/g_darkModeActive))
    {
        *pColor = MenuUseTransparentBackdrop()
            ? RGB(0, 0, 0)
            : MenuSurfaceSolidColor(g_darkModeActive);
        return S_OK;
    }

    if (g_settings.ModernContextMenus && cls == L"Menu"
        && g_darkModeActive)
    {
        if (IsLegacyShellDropdownRoot(g_tlsPaintHwnd))
            return hr;

        // Text color: white for non-disabled items (disabled = state 3 or 4).
        if (iPropId == TMT_TEXTCOLOR) {
            if ((iPartId == 14 /*MENU_POPUPITEM*/ || iPartId == 27)
                && iStateId != 3 && iStateId != 4) {
                if (*pColor == RGB(0, 0, 0)) *pColor = RGB(255, 255, 255);
            }
            else if (iPartId == 8 /*MENU_BARITEM*/
                && iStateId != 3 /*MBI_DISABLED*/ && iStateId != 6 /*MBI_DISABLEDPUSHED*/) {
                if (*pColor == RGB(0, 0, 0)) *pColor = RGB(255, 255, 255);
            }
        }
    }

    // Dark mode text colors — force white/accent in OUR dark windows only.
    // Explorer's XAML/DirectUI manages its own dark text. Overriding it causes
    // font/color resets and white-flash glitches in the content area.
    if (g_darkModeActive && iPropId == TMT_TEXTCOLOR) {
        // Header/ItemsView: only override in property windows we darkened
        HWND hWnd = g_tlsPaintHwnd;
        bool isOurDark = false;
        if (hWnd) {
            HWND anc = GetAncestor(hWnd, GA_ROOT);
            if (anc && GetPropW(anc, kPropertyDialogDarkModeMarker))
                isOurDark = true;
        }
        if (isOurDark) {
            // Header's own background is force-filled dark above (baked
            // bitmap art, no FILLCOLOR to recolor instead) -- its native
            // text needs forcing to white to stay legible against that.
            if (cls == L"Header" || cls.find(L"Header") != std::wstring::npos) {
                *pColor = RGB(255, 255, 255); return S_OK;
            }
        }
        // ItemsView/ListView row text stays native against the patched FILLCOLOR.
        // TaskDialog main instruction → accent light2
        if (cls == L"TaskDialogStyle") {
            if (iPartId == TDLG_MAININSTRUCTIONPANE) {
                *pColor = GetAccentFromPalette(4);
                return S_OK;
            }
            if (iPartId == TDLG_CONTENTPANE || iPartId == TDLG_VERIFICATIONTEXT) {
                if (*pColor == RGB(0, 0, 0)) *pColor = RGB(255, 255, 255);
                return S_OK;
            }
        }
        // Tab control text: handled earlier (before the FAILED(hr) bailout
        // above), since GetThemeColor_orig fails outright for this part.
        // Toolbar text → white (breadcrumb dropdowns, ViewControlClass
        // buttons, classic dialog "Organize"/"New Folder" split buttons).
        // Luma threshold instead of an exact RGB(0,0,0) match: this
        // experiment's shrunk kDarkSysColorElems no longer forces the
        // underlying system-color-mapped theme property to pure black the
        // way the old 30-entry array incidentally did, so the live raw
        // value can be some other dark shade (e.g. a dark blue) that the
        // exact-match check would silently stop catching.
        if (cls == L"Toolbar" || cls.find(L"Toolbar") != std::wstring::npos) {
            int luma = (GetRValue(*pColor) * 54 + GetGValue(*pColor) * 183 +
                        GetBValue(*pColor) * 19) >> 8;
            if (luma < 128) *pColor = RGB(255, 255, 255);
            return S_OK;
        }
        // Status bar text → white in dark mode.
        if (cls == L"Status") {
            if (*pColor == RGB(0, 0, 0)) *pColor = RGB(255, 255, 255);
            return S_OK;
        }
        // Combobox text → white in dark mode
        if (cls == L"Combobox" || cls == L"ComboBox") {
            if (iStateId != 4 /*CBXS_DISABLED*/)
                if (*pColor == RGB(0, 0, 0)) *pColor = RGB(255, 255, 255);
            return S_OK;
        }
        // Edit text → white in dark mode
        if (cls == L"Edit") {
            if (*pColor == RGB(0, 0, 0)) *pColor = RGB(255, 255, 255);
            return S_OK;
        }
        // Static text → white
        if (cls == L"Static") {
            if (*pColor < RGB(16, 16, 16)) *pColor = RGB(255, 255, 255);
            return S_OK;
        }
        // Context menu text — POPUPITEM/27: black→white in dark mode.
        // Removed earlier with menu cleanup but still needed — system draws
        // text separately and the Menu theme returns black for POPUPITEM.
        if (cls == L"Menu" && (iPartId == 14 /*MENU_POPUPITEM*/ || iPartId == 27)
            && iStateId != 3 && iStateId != 4) {
            if (*pColor == RGB(0, 0, 0)) *pColor = RGB(255, 255, 255);
            return S_OK;
        }
        // ControlPanelStyle: dark-only overrides (white text, task links)
        // Links and accent-colored items moved to accent-applicable block below.
        if (cls == L"ControlPanelStyle") {
            // Section title link (e.g. "Hardware e Sons" in category view) is
            // kept neutral instead of accent-colored like the sublinks below
            // it -- it reads as a heading first, a link second.
            if (iPartId == CPANEL_BODYTITLE || iPartId == CPANEL_GROUPTEXT ||
                iPartId == CPANEL_MESSAGETEXT || iPartId == CPANEL_BODYTEXT ||
                iPartId == CPANEL_TITLE || iPartId == CPANEL_CONTENTPANELABEL ||
                iPartId == CPANEL_SECTIONTITLELINK) {
                *pColor = RGB(255, 255, 255);
                return S_OK;
            }
            if (iPartId == CPANEL_TASKLINK) {
                *pColor = (iStateId == CPTL_HOT) ? RGB(255, 255, 255) :
                          (iStateId == CPTL_PRESSED) ? RGB(160, 160, 160) :
                          (iStateId == CPTL_DISABLED) ? RGB(96, 96, 96) :
                          RGB(190, 190, 190);
                return S_OK;
            }
        }
        // CommandModule: dark-only (black→white task button)
        if (cls == L"CommandModule" && iPartId == 3 && iStateId == 1
            && *pColor == RGB(0, 0, 0)) {
            *pColor = RGB(255, 255, 255); return S_OK;
        }
        // TreeView text
        if ((cls == L"TreeView" || cls.find(L"TreeView") != std::wstring::npos)
            && *pColor == RGB(0, 0, 0)) {
            *pColor = RGB(255, 255, 255); return S_OK;
        }
        // AeroWizardStyle text → white
        if (cls == L"AeroWizardStyle") {
            *pColor = RGB(255, 255, 255); return S_OK;
        }
        // AeroWizard title text (part=1/AW_TITLEBAR) queries this class/part
        // combo directly (not "AeroWizardStyle") and defaults to black.
        if (cls == L"AeroWizard" && iPartId == 1 /*AW_TITLEBAR*/) {
            *pColor = RGB(255, 255, 255); return S_OK;
        }
        // Button disabled → gray
        if (cls == L"Button" && iPartId == BP_PUSHBUTTON && iStateId == PBS_DISABLED
            && *pColor == RGB(0, 0, 0)) {
            *pColor = RGB(192, 192, 192); return S_OK;
        }
    }

    // Accent-applicable overrides — blue system links → user accent color.
    // Active with EITHER dark mode OR AccentColorize.
    if ((g_darkModeActive || g_settings.AccentColorize)
        && iPropId == TMT_TEXTCOLOR) {
        // Link text → accent shades
        if (cls == L"Link") {
            *pColor = (iStateId == 2) ? accentHot() :
                      (iStateId == 3) ? accentPressed() :
                      (iStateId == 4) ? RGB(96, 96, 96) : accentNormal();
            return S_OK;
        }
        // Button CommandLink (part 6) — text-only links with default blue
        if (cls == L"Button" && iPartId == 6 /*BP_COMMANDLINK*/) {
            BYTE b2 = GetBValue(*pColor), r2 = GetRValue(*pColor);
            if (b2 > 100 && r2 < 128 && b2 > r2 + 30) {
                *pColor = accentNormal();
                return S_OK;
            }
        }
        // TextStyle → accent for blue text
        if (cls == L"TextStyle") {
            BYTE b2 = GetBValue(*pColor), r2 = GetRValue(*pColor);
            if (b2 > 100 && r2 < 128 && b2 > r2 + 30) {
                *pColor = accentNormal();
                return S_OK;
            }
            if (g_darkModeActive && *pColor < RGB(16, 16, 16)) {
                *pColor = RGB(255, 255, 255);
                return S_OK;
            }
        }
        // ControlPanelStyle links → accent
        if (cls == L"ControlPanelStyle") {
            if (iPartId == CPANEL_TITLE) {
                *pColor = accentNormal();
                return S_OK;
            }
            if (iPartId == CPANEL_SECTIONTITLELINK) {
                *pColor = RGB(0, 0, 0);
                return S_OK;
            }
            if (iPartId == CPANEL_CONTENTLINK || iPartId == CPANEL_HELPLINK) {
                *pColor = (iStateId == CPHL_HOT) ? accentHot() :
                          (iStateId == CPHL_PRESSED) ? accentPressed() : accentNormal();
                return S_OK;
            }
        }
        // CommandModule library pane → accent
        if (cls == L"CommandModule" && iPartId == 9) {
            BYTE b2 = GetBValue(*pColor), r2 = GetRValue(*pColor);
            bool nativeBlue = (b2 > 100 && r2 < 128 && b2 > r2 + 30);
            if (nativeBlue || g_settings.AccentColorize) {
                *pColor = (iStateId == 1) ? accentNormal() :
                          (iStateId == 2) ? accentHot() :
                          (iStateId == 3) ? accentPressed() : RGB(96, 96, 96);
                return S_OK;
            }
            if (g_darkModeActive) {
                *pColor = (iStateId == 4) ? RGB(96, 96, 96) : RGB(255, 255, 255);
                return S_OK;
            }
        }
    }

    // Fill color overrides (outside TMT_TEXTCOLOR block)
    if (g_darkModeActive) {
        if (cls == L"ControlPanelStyle" && iPropId == TMT_FILLCOLORHINT
            && iPartId == CPANEL_CONTENTPANELINE && iStateId == 0) {
            *pColor = RGB(64, 64, 64); return S_OK;
        }
    }

    // Context menu fill colors — tell system to use dark bg for all menu parts
    if (g_darkModeActive && cls == L"Menu"
        && (iPropId == TMT_FILLCOLOR || iPropId == TMT_FILLCOLORHINT)) {
        *pColor = RGB(0x2E, 0x2E, 0x2E);
        return S_OK;
    }


    // Button text color — detect accent and dark mode directly
    // (GetThemeColor may be called BEFORE DrawThemeBackground, so thread-local
    // Button non-pushbutton parts (GroupBox, CheckBox, RadioButton labels → white)
    if (g_darkModeActive && cls == L"Button" && iPropId == TMT_TEXTCOLOR
        && iPartId != BP_PUSHBUTTON) {
        if (*pColor == RGB(0, 0, 0)) *pColor = RGB(255, 255, 255);
        return hr;
    }
    // Button pushbutton: the color PaintPushButton resolved for this state,
    // else the accent/dark contrast fallback.
    if (g_settings.RoundedButtons && cls == L"Button"
        && iPartId == BP_PUSHBUTTON && iPropId == TMT_TEXTCOLOR
        && g_tlsButtonTextColor != CLR_INVALID) {
        *pColor = g_tlsButtonTextColor;
        return S_OK;
    }
    if (g_settings.RoundedButtons && cls == L"Button"
        && iPartId == BP_PUSHBUTTON && iPropId == TMT_TEXTCOLOR
        && iStateId != PBS_DISABLED) {
        const bool isAccent = g_tlsIsAccentButton;
        const bool dark = g_tlsButtonDark;
        if (isAccent)
            *pColor = dark ? RGB(0, 0, 0) : RGB(255, 255, 255);
        else if (dark)
            *pColor = RGB(255, 255, 255);
    }
    return hr;
}

HRESULT WINAPI GetThemeMargins_hook(HTHEME hTheme, HDC hdc, int iPartId,
    int iStateId, int iPropId, LPRECT prc, MARGINS* pMargins)
{
    HRESULT hr = GetThemeMargins_orig(hTheme, hdc, iPartId, iStateId,
                                      iPropId, prc, pMargins);
    if (!g_settings.ModernTooltips || !pMargins || FAILED(hr)) return hr;

    const std::wstring& cls = GetCachedThemeClass(hTheme);
    if (cls == L"Tooltip" && iPartId == TTP_STANDARD) {
        if (iPropId == TMT_CONTENTMARGINS) {
            // Comctl32 and the offscreen native DrawText pass use the same
            // selected HFONT. Base values are divided by the 125% reference
            // scale and scaled back for the paint DPI.
            const float dpiScale = DpiForPaintHdc(hdc) / 96.0f;
            pMargins->cxLeftWidth = (LONG)std::lround(6.4f * dpiScale);
            pMargins->cxRightWidth = (LONG)std::lround(6.4f * dpiScale);
            pMargins->cyTopHeight = (LONG)std::lround(5.6f * dpiScale);
            pMargins->cyBottomHeight = (LONG)std::lround(5.6f * dpiScale);
        }
    }
    return hr;
}

// ============================================================================
// Registry Editor modernization (RegeditSection)
// ============================================================================
// TryApplyToWindow_Regedit() styles each control (TV/LV/Header/Search) via a
// dedicated subclass, installed on window creation. TreeView rendering uses
// D2D via BindDC; horizontal scroll artifacts are prevented by WM_HSCROLL in
// RgTVSubclassProc forcing a full RedrawWindow after every ScrollWindowEx
// BitBlt.
// ============================================================================

static bool IsCurrentProcessRegedit()
{
    static std::atomic<int> cached{ -1 };
    int val = cached.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
    if (val == -1)
    {
        wchar_t path[MAX_PATH] = {};
        GetModuleFileNameW(nullptr, path, MAX_PATH);
        wchar_t* name = wcsrchr(path, L'\\');
        val = (name && _wcsicmp(name + 1, L"regedit.exe") == 0) ? 1 : 0;
        cached.store(val, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    }
    return val == 1;
}

// Whole-subsystem gate for every dark/light decision below. Regedit is
// always a single top-level process, so exclusion here always means "this
// process" -- no per-hwnd/file-picker narrowing needed like the shared
// hooks elsewhere. RegeditSection has its own complete light-mode
// rendering at every call site, so this safely routes an excluded

// Declared here (ahead of its "real" neighbors further down, alongside
// rg_hwndMain/rg_hwndTV) because RgHoverFadeEnabled below needs it and this
// file has no header -- declaration order is compile order.
static std::atomic<bool> rg_unloading{ false };

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Regedit tree hover fade (UI-thread only, no lock)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Mirrors NavHoverFadeState's design exactly -- same struct type and fade
// curve/constants (kNavHoverFadeDurationSeconds, kNavHoverFadeTimerIntervalMs,
// NavHoverFadeProgress, all pure functions with no hidden state) -- but stored
// as a plain global instead of a window prop.
// NavHoverFadeGetState's GetPropW-based lookup elsewhere (DrawRoundedItemBg's
// isNavPaneTree) treats that prop's mere presence on a window as "this is
// the nav pane", so this must never touch that storage. A plain global is
// also simpler here: regedit has exactly one tree (rg_hwndTV), unlike
// Explorer's multiple nav panes across windows.
static NavHoverFadeState rg_hoverFade;

static bool RgHoverFadeGetPaintRect(
    HWND hwnd, HTREEITEM item, RECT* rect)
{
    return hwnd && item && rect &&
        TreeView_GetItemRect(hwnd, item, rect, FALSE) &&
        rect->right > rect->left && rect->bottom > rect->top;
}

static void RgHoverFadeStopTimer(HWND hwnd)
{
    if (!rg_hoverFade.timerActive)
        return;
    KillTimer(hwnd, kRgHoverFadeTimerId);
    rg_hoverFade.timerActive = false;
}

static void RgHoverFadeClear(HWND hwnd, bool invalidate)
{
    RgHoverFadeStopTimer(hwnd);
    if (invalidate && rg_hoverFade.hotItem)
        InvalidateRect(hwnd, &rg_hoverFade.rect, FALSE);
    rg_hoverFade = NavHoverFadeState{};
}

static bool RgHoverFadeEnabled()
{
    return !rg_unloading.load(std::memory_order_acquire) &&
        g_settings.RegeditSection;
}

// Fades in on hover and out on leave, same bidirectional curve as
// NavHoverFadeRetarget/NavHoverFadeProgress (fadingOut reverses the curve).
// Re-targeting the item currently fading out reverses back into a fade-in
// instead of no-op'ing, same as NavHoverFadeRetarget.
static void RgHoverFadeRetarget(HWND hwnd, HTREEITEM hotItem)
{
    if (rg_hoverFade.hotItem == hotItem && !rg_hoverFade.fadingOut)
        return;
    if (!hotItem) {
        if (rg_hoverFade.fadingOut || !rg_hoverFade.hotItem)
            return;
        if (!SysAnimationsEnabled() || (TreeView_GetItemState(
                hwnd, rg_hoverFade.hotItem, TVIS_SELECTED) & TVIS_SELECTED)) {
            RgHoverFadeClear(hwnd, true);
            return;
        }
        RgHoverFadeStopTimer(hwnd);
        rg_hoverFade.fadingOut = true;
        rg_hoverFade.startTime = TimerGetSeconds();
        if (SetTimer(hwnd, kRgHoverFadeTimerId, kNavHoverFadeTimerIntervalMs, nullptr))
            rg_hoverFade.timerActive = true;
        else
            RgHoverFadeClear(hwnd, true);
        return;
    }

    const bool selected =
        (TreeView_GetItemState(hwnd, hotItem, TVIS_SELECTED) & TVIS_SELECTED);

    if (rg_hoverFade.hotItem)
        InvalidateRect(hwnd, &rg_hoverFade.rect, FALSE);
    RgHoverFadeStopTimer(hwnd);
    rg_hoverFade.fadingOut = false;

    rg_hoverFade.hotItem = hotItem;
    rg_hoverFade.startTime = 0.0;
    if (!RgHoverFadeGetPaintRect(hwnd, hotItem, &rg_hoverFade.rect)) {
        rg_hoverFade = NavHoverFadeState{};
        return;
    }

    // Selected or physically pressed: show the highlight immediately, same
    // as NavHoverFadeRetarget -- no fade racing a click or a state the
    // background tint already renders at full strength.
    const bool animate = SysAnimationsEnabled() && !selected &&
        !IsTreeItemPressed(hwnd, &rg_hoverFade.rect);
    if (animate)
        rg_hoverFade.startTime = TimerGetSeconds();

    InvalidateRect(hwnd, &rg_hoverFade.rect, FALSE);
    if (animate) {
        if (SetTimer(hwnd, kRgHoverFadeTimerId, kNavHoverFadeTimerIntervalMs, nullptr))
            rg_hoverFade.timerActive = true;
        else
            rg_hoverFade.startTime = 0.0;
    }
}

static void RgHoverFadeHandleMouseMove(HWND hwnd, LPARAM lParam)
{
    if (!RgHoverFadeEnabled()) {
        RgHoverFadeClear(hwnd, true);
        return;
    }

    TVHITTESTINFO hit = {};
    hit.pt.x = static_cast<SHORT>(LOWORD(lParam));
    hit.pt.y = static_cast<SHORT>(HIWORD(lParam));
    HTREEITEM item = TreeView_HitTest(hwnd, &hit);
    if (rg_hoverFade.hotItem == item && !rg_hoverFade.fadingOut) {
        if (!rg_hoverFade.trackingLeave) {
            TRACKMOUSEEVENT tme = { sizeof(tme), TME_LEAVE, hwnd, 0 };
            rg_hoverFade.trackingLeave = TrackMouseEvent(&tme) != FALSE;
        }
        return;
    }
    RgHoverFadeRetarget(hwnd, item);
    if (!rg_hoverFade.trackingLeave) {
        TRACKMOUSEEVENT tme = { sizeof(tme), TME_LEAVE, hwnd, 0 };
        rg_hoverFade.trackingLeave = TrackMouseEvent(&tme) != FALSE;
    }
}

static void RgHoverFadeSyncCursor(HWND hwnd, bool rearmLeave)
{
    if (!rg_hoverFade.hotItem)
        return;
    if (rearmLeave)
        rg_hoverFade.trackingLeave = false;
    POINT point = {};
    if (!TreeHoverCursorClientPoint(hwnd, &point)) {
        RgHoverFadeRetarget(hwnd, nullptr);
        return;
    }
    const RECT previousRect = rg_hoverFade.rect;
    RECT currentRect = {};
    if (RgHoverFadeGetPaintRect(hwnd, rg_hoverFade.hotItem, &currentRect) &&
        !EqualRect(&previousRect, &currentRect)) {
        InvalidateRect(hwnd, &previousRect, FALSE);
        InvalidateRect(hwnd, &currentRect, FALSE);
        rg_hoverFade.rect = currentRect;
    }
    RgHoverFadeHandleMouseMove(hwnd, MAKELPARAM(point.x, point.y));
}

static void RgHoverFadeTimerTick(HWND hwnd)
{
    if (!rg_hoverFade.timerActive)
        return;
    if (!RgHoverFadeEnabled()) {
        RgHoverFadeClear(hwnd, !rg_unloading.load(std::memory_order_acquire));
        return;
    }
    if (!SysAnimationsEnabled()) {
        if (rg_hoverFade.fadingOut) {
            RgHoverFadeClear(hwnd, true);
        } else {
            rg_hoverFade.startTime = 0.0;
            RgHoverFadeStopTimer(hwnd);
            InvalidateRect(hwnd, &rg_hoverFade.rect, FALSE);
        }
        return;
    }

    const DOUBLE now = TimerGetSeconds();
    RECT previousRect = rg_hoverFade.rect;
    if (!RgHoverFadeGetPaintRect(hwnd, rg_hoverFade.hotItem, &rg_hoverFade.rect)) {
        RgHoverFadeClear(hwnd, true);
        return;
    }
    if (!EqualRect(&previousRect, &rg_hoverFade.rect))
        InvalidateRect(hwnd, &previousRect, FALSE);
    InvalidateRect(hwnd, &rg_hoverFade.rect, FALSE);

    // Fading out runs kNavHoverFadeOutHoldSeconds longer than fading in
    // (see NavHoverFadeProgress) -- without adding it here too, this would
    // clear rg_hoverFade (and stop painting it) partway through its own
    // held-then-fading curve, popping it off mid-animation.
    const DOUBLE totalDuration = rg_hoverFade.fadingOut
        ? kNavHoverFadeDurationSeconds + kNavHoverFadeOutHoldSeconds
        : kNavHoverFadeDurationSeconds;
    if (now - rg_hoverFade.startTime >= totalDuration) {
        if (rg_hoverFade.fadingOut) {
            RgHoverFadeClear(hwnd, false);
            return;
        }
        rg_hoverFade.startTime = 0.0;
        RgHoverFadeStopTimer(hwnd);
    }
}

static void RgHoverFadeClearAfterGeometryChange(HWND hwnd)
{
    if (!rg_hoverFade.fadingOut || !rg_hoverFade.hotItem)
        return;

    const RECT previousRect = rg_hoverFade.rect;
    RECT currentRect = {};
    const bool currentRectValid =
        RgHoverFadeGetPaintRect(hwnd, rg_hoverFade.hotItem, &currentRect);
    InvalidateRect(hwnd, &previousRect, FALSE);
    if (currentRectValid) {
        if (!EqualRect(&previousRect, &currentRect))
            InvalidateRect(hwnd, &currentRect, FALSE);
    } else {
        InvalidateRect(hwnd, nullptr, FALSE);
    }
    RgHoverFadeClear(hwnd, false);
}

static bool RgUnionTreeItemRect(HWND tv, HTREEITEM item, RECT* inOut, bool* hasRect)
{
    if (!tv || !item || !inOut || !hasRect)
        return false;

    RECT rc = {};
    *reinterpret_cast<HTREEITEM*>(&rc) = item;
    if (!SendMessage(tv, TVM_GETITEMRECT, FALSE, reinterpret_cast<LPARAM>(&rc)))
        return false;

    if (!*hasRect) {
        *inOut = rc;
        *hasRect = true;
    } else {
        UnionRect(inOut, inOut, &rc);
    }
    return true;
}

static void RgInvalidatePillItems(HWND tv)
{
    if (!tv || !IsWindow(tv)) return;

    RECT dirty = {};
    bool hasRect = false;
    RgUnionTreeItemRect(tv, rg_pillAnimPrevItem, &dirty, &hasRect);
    RgUnionTreeItemRect(tv, rg_pillAnimItem, &dirty, &hasRect);
    if (hasRect)
        InvalidateRect(tv, &dirty, FALSE);
    // Neither item resolved a rect (scrolled off-screen, collapsed away, or
    // removed by a tree rebuild mid-animation) -- nothing to redraw, and a
    // WM_TIMER tick must never fall back to invalidating the whole HWND.
}

static ID2D1SolidColorBrush* rg_tvPillSolidBrush = nullptr;
static ID2D1GradientStopCollection* rg_tvPillGradientStops = nullptr;
static ID2D1LinearGradientBrush* rg_tvPillGradientBrush = nullptr;

static PillListViewIndicatorState RgSamplePillAnimation(DOUBLE now)

static void RgReleaseTreePillBrushes()
{
    if (rg_tvPillGradientBrush) {
        rg_tvPillGradientBrush->Release();
        rg_tvPillGradientBrush = nullptr;
    }
    if (rg_tvPillGradientStops) {
        rg_tvPillGradientStops->Release();
        rg_tvPillGradientStops = nullptr;
    }
    if (rg_tvPillSolidBrush) {
        rg_tvPillSolidBrush->Release();
        rg_tvPillSolidBrush = nullptr;
    }
    rg_tvPillGradientAccent = CLR_INVALID;
    rg_tvPillGradientBase = CLR_INVALID;
}

static ID2D1Brush* RgGetTreePillBrush(
    COLORREF accent, COLORREF base, bool gradient,
    float left, float top, float bottom, float opacity)
{
    if (!rg_tvCachedRT)
        return nullptr;

    if (gradient) {
        if (!rg_tvPillGradientBrush ||
            rg_tvPillGradientAccent != accent ||
            rg_tvPillGradientBase != base) {
            if (rg_tvPillGradientBrush) {
                rg_tvPillGradientBrush->Release();
                rg_tvPillGradientBrush = nullptr;
            }
            if (rg_tvPillGradientStops) {
                rg_tvPillGradientStops->Release();
                rg_tvPillGradientStops = nullptr;
            }

            const D2D1_GRADIENT_STOP stops[2] = {
                { 0.0f, D2D1::ColorF(GetRValue(accent) / 255.0f,
                                     GetGValue(accent) / 255.0f,
                                     GetBValue(accent) / 255.0f) },
                { 1.0f, D2D1::ColorF(GetRValue(base) / 255.0f,
                                     GetGValue(base) / 255.0f,
                                     GetBValue(base) / 255.0f) }
            };
            HRESULT hr = rg_tvCachedRT->CreateGradientStopCollection(
                stops, ARRAYSIZE(stops), &rg_tvPillGradientStops);
            if (SUCCEEDED(hr)) {
                hr = rg_tvCachedRT->CreateLinearGradientBrush(
                    D2D1::LinearGradientBrushProperties(
                        D2D1::Point2F(left, top),
                        D2D1::Point2F(left, bottom)),
                    rg_tvPillGradientStops, &rg_tvPillGradientBrush);
            }
            if (FAILED(hr)) {
                if (rg_tvPillGradientBrush) {
                    rg_tvPillGradientBrush->Release();
                    rg_tvPillGradientBrush = nullptr;
                }
                if (rg_tvPillGradientStops) {
                    rg_tvPillGradientStops->Release();
                    rg_tvPillGradientStops = nullptr;
                }
            } else {
                rg_tvPillGradientAccent = accent;
                rg_tvPillGradientBase = base;
            }
        }

        if (rg_tvPillGradientBrush) {
            rg_tvPillGradientBrush->SetStartPoint(D2D1::Point2F(left, top));
            rg_tvPillGradientBrush->SetEndPoint(D2D1::Point2F(left, bottom));
            rg_tvPillGradientBrush->SetOpacity(opacity);
            return rg_tvPillGradientBrush;
        }
    }

    if (!rg_tvPillSolidBrush) {
        const D2D1_COLOR_F color = D2D1::ColorF(
            GetRValue(accent) / 255.0f,
            GetGValue(accent) / 255.0f,
            GetBValue(accent) / 255.0f);
        if (FAILED(rg_tvCachedRT->CreateSolidColorBrush(
                color, &rg_tvPillSolidBrush))) {
            return nullptr;
        }
    }
    rg_tvPillSolidBrush->SetColor(D2D1::ColorF(
        GetRValue(accent) / 255.0f,
        GetGValue(accent) / 255.0f,
        GetBValue(accent) / 255.0f));
    rg_tvPillSolidBrush->SetOpacity(opacity);
    return rg_tvPillSolidBrush;
}

// DPI/dark-mode snapshot for the current TV paint pass, set once at
// CDDS_PREPAINT and reused by every CDDS_ITEMPREPAINT until the next one
// (UI-thread only, same as the rest of this file's paint-time state).
static UINT s_rgTvPaintDpi  = 96;
static bool s_rgTvPaintDark = false;
// The tree font with the WinUI face the D2D text uses; valid only when read.
static LOGFONTW s_rgTvPaintFont = {};
static bool s_rgTvPaintFontValid = false;

// A plain tree row (no tint, pill or turning chevron) draws its chevron and
// name from the raster cache, where the row's D2D session would draw them:
// `glyphX` and `textLeft` are relative to rcFull, as in that session. Returns
// false, with nothing drawn, when the row can't use the cache; *textDrawn
// says whether the name was drawn.
static bool RgTreeRowDrawCached(HDC hdc, const RECT& rcFull, bool hasChildren,
    int glyphX, int glyphW, float chevronAngle, int textLeft, int textRight,
    LPCWSTR text, bool dark, UINT dpi, bool* textDrawn)
{
    *textDrawn = false;
    if (!s_rgTvPaintFontValid || GetMapMode(hdc) != MM_TEXT)
        return false;
    const LONG rowH = rcFull.bottom - rcFull.top;
    const int textLen = (int)wcslen(text);
    const bool hasText = textLen > 0 && textRight > textLeft;
    // The session clips at the row, not the text rect: keep a margin so glyph
    // overhang past the rect's edges isn't cut.
    const int margin = MulDiv(kRgTVHMargin, (int)dpi, 96);
    const int padLeft = std::min(margin, std::max(0, textLeft));
    const int padRight = margin;
    const RECT area = {rcFull.left + textLeft - padLeft, rcFull.top,
        rcFull.left + textRight + padRight, rcFull.bottom};
    const LONG width = area.right - area.left;
    if (hasText && !ShellTextRasterUsable(hdc, width, rowH))
        return false;

    if (hasChildren) {
        const RECT cell = {rcFull.left + glyphX, rcFull.top,
            rcFull.left + glyphX + glyphW, rcFull.bottom};
        const int fontSizePx = std::max(1, (int)std::lround(
            kTreeViewChevronGlyphDip * (float)dpi / 96.f));
        if (!DrawChevronGlyphCached(hdc, cell, kChevronGlyphRight, chevronAngle,
                fontSizePx, dark))
            return false;
    }
    if (!hasText) {
        *textDrawn = true;
        return true;
    }
    const WinUI::Color foreground = NavigationItemForegroundColor(dark,
        g_settings.NeutralSelection, dark ? kRgDkTVText : kRgLtTVText, false);
    const COLORREF color = foreground.rgb;
    const UINT flags = DT_LEFT | DT_VCENTER | DT_SINGLELINE | DT_END_ELLIPSIS;
    const LOGFONTW& font = s_rgTvPaintFont;
    ShellTextRasterKey key;
    key.text = std::wstring_view(text, textLen);
    key.face = std::wstring_view(font.lfFaceName, wcsnlen(font.lfFaceName, LF_FACESIZE));
    key.values = {static_cast<uint32_t>(font.lfHeight), static_cast<uint32_t>(font.lfWidth),
        static_cast<uint32_t>(font.lfWeight), font.lfItalic, font.lfUnderline,
        font.lfStrikeOut, font.lfCharSet, font.lfQuality, dpi, flags,
        static_cast<uint32_t>(width), static_cast<uint32_t>(rowH),
        static_cast<uint32_t>(padLeft), static_cast<uint32_t>(padRight), foreground.alpha};
    key.color = color;
    key.generation = ShellTextRasterGeneration();
    key.rendererKind = 4;
    const uint64_t hash = key.Hash();
    ShellTextRaster* raster = ShellTextRasterLoad(width, rowH, key, hash, nullptr);
    if (!raster) {
        raster = ShellTextRasterRender(width, rowH, color, key, hash, 0,
            [&](ID2D1RenderTarget* target, ID2D1SolidColorBrush*) {
                const RECT local = {padLeft, 0, width - padRight, rowH};
                return DrawWinUiStyledTextDWriteInSession(target, &local, text,
                    textLen, font, color, flags, dpi, foreground.alpha / 255.f);
            });
    }
    *textDrawn = raster && ShellTextRasterBlend(hdc, area, *raster);
    return true;
}

// Regedit globals
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Set once (first-writer-wins via compare_exchange) at control creation and
// only cleared on teardown -- plain atomics instead of rg_srw (a SRWLOCK)
// since every access is just a single pointer read/write/CAS, and the only
// real cross-thread case is Wh_ModAfterInit's late-attach scan racing the
// UI thread's own window-creation dispatch.
static std::atomic<HWND> rg_hwndMain{ nullptr };

static bool RgListTextDWrite(HDC hdc, LPCWSTR text, INT count, LPRECT rect,
    UINT format, INT* result)

    if (!t_rgListPaintHwnd || !text || !g_settings.RegeditSection ||
        !IsCurrentProcessRegedit() || GetBkMode(hdc) != TRANSPARENT) {

    const COLORREF original = GetTextColor(hdc);

        hdc, text, count, rect, format, 2, result, 0, 0.0f);

        SetTextColor(hdc, original);

// D2D blend: accent at opacity over dark/light base (opaque, non-layered window)
static D2D1_COLOR_F RgBlendAccent(COLORREF accent, float opacity)
{
    // Premultiplied tree target (Mica): let the render target compose it.
    if (rg_tvCachedRTPremultiplied)
        return { GetRValue(accent) / 255.f, GetGValue(accent) / 255.f,
                 GetBValue(accent) / 255.f, opacity };
    const bool dark = RgIsDarkMode();
    const float base = dark ? kRgDkMicaBase : kRgLtMicaBase;
    const float ar = GetRValue(accent) / 255.f;
    const float ag = GetGValue(accent) / 255.f;
    const float ab = GetBValue(accent) / 255.f;
    return { base + (ar - base) * opacity,
             base + (ag - base) * opacity,
             base + (ab - base) * opacity, 1.0f };
}

static bool RgEnsureGdipLocked()
{
    if (rg_gdip.ready)
        return true;
    if (rg_gdip.startupAttempted ||
        g_gdipUnloading.load(std::memory_order_acquire))
        return false;

    rg_gdip.startupAttempted = true;
    Gdiplus::GdiplusStartupInput input;
    if (Gdiplus::GdiplusStartup(&rg_gdip.token, &input, nullptr) !=
        Gdiplus::Ok) {
        rg_gdip.token = 0;
        return false;
    }

    rg_gdip.ready = true;
    return true;
}

static void RgClearGdipLocked()
{
    if (rg_gdip.token) {
        Gdiplus::GdiplusShutdown(rg_gdip.token);
        rg_gdip.token = 0;
    }
    rg_gdip.ready = false;
    rg_gdip.startupAttempted = false;
}
