// SetSysColors changes one session-wide table. A named mutex and process
// list ensure only the final participating process restores the trusted
// baseline; exited processes are pruned so abnormal exits cannot pin the
// palette. Each entry carries the process creation time, so a PID reused by
// an unrelated process doesn't count as a participant.
struct DarkSysColorsProcess {
    DWORD pid;
    FILETIME created;
};
struct SharedDarkSysColorsState {
    static constexpr int kMaxTrackedProcesses = 64;
    LONG originalSaved;
    COLORREF originalCols[kDarkSysColorCount];
    DarkSysColorsProcess active[kMaxTrackedProcesses];
};
// Named v2: the layout differs from the PID-only table of earlier builds.
static constexpr wchar_t kDarkSysColorsMutexName[] =
    L"Local\\Win32UIModernizer.DarkSysColorsMutex2";
static constexpr wchar_t kDarkSysColorsMapName[] =
    L"Local\\Win32UIModernizer.DarkSysColorsShared2";
static HANDLE g_darkSysColsMutex = nullptr;
static HANDLE g_darkSysColsMap = nullptr;
// A tagged value distinguishes a trusted SysMetrics baseline from snapshots
// written by older builds while keeping the shared mapping layout compatible.
static constexpr LONG kDarkSysColorsSysMetricsBaseline = 0x574D5301;

// Creation time of a live process, or false once it has exited or can't be
// opened. PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION is granted across integrity
// levels, so an elevated Explorer peer is still checkable from a normal one.
static bool DarkSysColsProcessCreationTime(DWORD pid, FILETIME* created)
{
    HANDLE h = OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION, FALSE, pid);
    if (!h)
        return false;
    FILETIME exited, kernel, user;
    DWORD exitCode = 0;
    const bool alive =
        GetProcessTimes(h, created, &exited, &kernel, &user) &&
        GetExitCodeProcess(h, &exitCode) && exitCode == STILL_ACTIVE;
    CloseHandle(h);
    return alive;
}

// Drops entries whose process has exited, or whose PID now belongs to a
// different process, and returns how many remain.
static int DarkSysColsPruneAndCountLocked(SharedDarkSysColorsState* shared)
{
    int count = 0;
    for (DarkSysColorsProcess& entry : shared->active) {
        if (!entry.pid)
            continue;
        FILETIME created = {};
        if (DarkSysColsProcessCreationTime(entry.pid, &created) &&
            CompareFileTime(&created, &entry.created) == 0) {
            count++;
        } else {
            entry = {};
        }
    }
    return count;
}

// Acquires the cross-process lock and maps the shared section. Returns
// false (nothing locked) if the kernel objects were never created --
// Wh_ModInit failure, a sandboxed/AppContainer host, etc. -- or the mutex
// wait times out; callers use only an independently validated SysMetrics
// baseline. WAIT_ABANDONED (a previous
// owner died while holding it) is treated as a normal acquire -- the
// critical sections below are a few plain assignments, nothing that can be
// left half-done in a way that corrupts a later reader.
static bool DarkSysColsLockShared(SharedDarkSysColorsState** outShared)
{
    *outShared = nullptr;
    if (!g_darkSysColsMutex || !g_darkSysColsMap)
        return false;
    DWORD wait = WaitForSingleObject(g_darkSysColsMutex, 2000);
    if (wait != WAIT_OBJECT_0 && wait != WAIT_ABANDONED)
        return false;
    SharedDarkSysColorsState* shared = (SharedDarkSysColorsState*)MapViewOfFile(
        g_darkSysColsMap, FILE_MAP_WRITE, 0, 0,
        sizeof(SharedDarkSysColorsState));
    if (!shared) {
        ReleaseMutex(g_darkSysColsMutex);
        return false;
    }
    *outShared = shared;
    return true;
}

static void DarkSysColsUnlockShared(SharedDarkSysColorsState* shared)
{
    if (shared) UnmapViewOfFile(shared);
    ReleaseMutex(g_darkSysColsMutex);
}

// The current user and SYSTEM, full access, with a medium integrity label
// (see Wh_ModInit). LocalFree the result.
static PSECURITY_DESCRIPTOR DarkSysColsCreateSecurityDescriptor()
{
    HANDLE token = nullptr;
    if (!OpenProcessToken(GetCurrentProcess(), TOKEN_QUERY, &token))
        return nullptr;
    DWORD size = 0;
    GetTokenInformation(token, TokenUser, nullptr, 0, &size);
    std::vector<BYTE> buffer(size);
    LPWSTR userSid = nullptr;
    if (size && GetTokenInformation(token, TokenUser, buffer.data(), size, &size)) {
        ConvertSidToStringSidW(
            reinterpret_cast<TOKEN_USER*>(buffer.data())->User.Sid, &userSid);
    }
    CloseHandle(token);
    if (!userSid)
        return nullptr;

    const std::wstring sddl = std::wstring(L"D:P(A;;GA;;;") + userSid +
        L")(A;;GA;;;SY)S:(ML;;NW;;;ME)";
    LocalFree(userSid);
    PSECURITY_DESCRIPTOR descriptor = nullptr;
    if (!ConvertStringSecurityDescriptorToSecurityDescriptorW(
            sddl.c_str(), SDDL_REVISION_1, &descriptor, nullptr)) {
        return nullptr;
    }
    return descriptor;
}

static bool DarkSysColsTrackCurrentProcessLocked(
    SharedDarkSysColorsState* shared)
{
    const DWORD pid = GetCurrentProcessId();
    for (const DarkSysColorsProcess& entry : shared->active) {
        if (entry.pid == pid)
            return true;
    }
    FILETIME created, exited, kernel, user;
    if (!GetProcessTimes(GetCurrentProcess(), &created, &exited, &kernel, &user))
        return false;
    for (DarkSysColorsProcess& entry : shared->active) {
        if (!entry.pid) {
            entry = { pid, created };
            return true;
        }
    }
    return false;
}

static void DarkSysColsUntrackCurrentProcessLocked(
    SharedDarkSysColorsState* shared)
{
    const DWORD pid = GetCurrentProcessId();
    for (DarkSysColorsProcess& entry : shared->active) {
        if (entry.pid == pid) {
            entry = {};
            return;
        }
    }
}

static COLORREF g_origDarkSysCols[kDarkSysColorCount] = {};
static bool g_darkSysColsSaved = false;

static bool QueryThemeSysMetricsColors(
    COLORREF (&colors)[kLegacyDarkSysColorCount])
{
    if (!OpenThemeData_orig || !CloseThemeData_orig)
        return false;

    HTHEME theme = OpenThemeData_orig(nullptr, L"SysMetrics");
    if (!theme)
        return false;

    bool valid = true;
    for (int i = 0; i < kLegacyDarkSysColorCount; ++i) {
        colors[i] = GetThemeSysColor(theme, kLegacyDarkSysColorElems[i]);
        if (colors[i] == CLR_INVALID)
            valid = false;
    }

    HRESULT closeHr = CloseThemeData_orig(theme);
    if (FAILED(closeHr))
        Wh_Log(L"CloseThemeData(SysMetrics) failed: 0x%08X", closeHr);
    return valid;
}

static COLORREF ThemeSysMetricsColorFor(
    const COLORREF (&colors)[kLegacyDarkSysColorCount], int element)
{
    for (int i = 0; i < kLegacyDarkSysColorCount; ++i) {
        if (kLegacyDarkSysColorElems[i] == element)
            return colors[i];
    }
    return CLR_INVALID;
}

static void CopyCurrentDarkSysColorsFromThemeMetrics(
    const COLORREF (&colors)[kLegacyDarkSysColorCount],
    COLORREF (&current)[kDarkSysColorCount])
{
    for (int i = 0; i < kDarkSysColorCount; ++i)
        current[i] = ThemeSysMetricsColorFor(colors, kDarkSysColorElems[i]);
}

static bool IsCurrentDarkSysColorElement(int element)
{
    for (int current : kDarkSysColorElems) {
        if (current == element)
            return true;
    }
    return false;
}

// The dark base older releases wrote, before Win32MainDark became
// SolidBackgroundFillColorBase. Independent of both current constants.
static constexpr COLORREF kLegacyModernizerDarkBase = RGB(0x19, 0x19, 0x19);

static bool IsLegacyModernizerDarkSysColor(int element, COLORREF color)
{
    switch (element) {
    case COLOR_SCROLLBAR:
    case COLOR_BACKGROUND:
    case COLOR_INACTIVECAPTION:
    case COLOR_WINDOW:
    case COLOR_INACTIVEBORDER:
    case COLOR_INFOBK:
        return color == kLegacyModernizerDarkBase;
    case COLOR_MENUBAR:
        return color == RGB(0, 0, 0) || color == kLegacyModernizerDarkBase;
    case COLOR_WINDOWTEXT:
        return color == RGB(0xE6, 0xE6, 0xE6);
    case COLOR_MENUTEXT:
    case COLOR_CAPTIONTEXT:
    case COLOR_HIGHLIGHTTEXT:
    case COLOR_BTNTEXT:
    case COLOR_INFOTEXT:
        return color == WinUI::Dark::TextFillColorPrimary;
    case COLOR_ACTIVECAPTION:
    case COLOR_ACTIVEBORDER:
    case COLOR_BTNSHADOW:
    case COLOR_GRADIENTACTIVECAPTION:
    case COLOR_GRADIENTINACTIVECAPTION:
        return color == RGB(0x20, 0x20, 0x20);
    case COLOR_WINDOWFRAME:
    case COLOR_BTNHIGHLIGHT:
        return color == RGB(0x40, 0x40, 0x40);
    case COLOR_APPWORKSPACE:
        return color == RGB(0x08, 0x08, 0x08);
    case COLOR_GRAYTEXT:
        return color == RGB(0x80, 0x80, 0x80);
    case COLOR_INACTIVECAPTIONTEXT:
        return color == RGB(0xA0, 0xA0, 0xA0);
    case COLOR_3DDKSHADOW:
        return color == RGB(0x10, 0x10, 0x10);
    case COLOR_3DLIGHT:
        return color == RGB(0x04, 0x04, 0x04);
    default:
        return false;
    }
}

static void ReadLiveSysColors(
    COLORREF (&colors)[kLegacyDarkSysColorCount])
{
    for (int i = 0; i < kLegacyDarkSysColorCount; ++i)
        colors[i] = GetSysColor_orig(kLegacyDarkSysColorElems[i]);
}

static bool RestoreThemeSysMetricsColors(
    const COLORREF (&themeColors)[kLegacyDarkSysColorCount],
    const COLORREF (&liveColors)[kLegacyDarkSysColorCount])
{
    if (!GetSysColor_orig)
        return false;

    INT restoreElems[kLegacyDarkSysColorCount];
    COLORREF restoreColors[kLegacyDarkSysColorCount];
    int restoreCount = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < kLegacyDarkSysColorCount; ++i) {
        const int element = kLegacyDarkSysColorElems[i];
        if (liveColors[i] == themeColors[i] ||
            (!IsCurrentDarkSysColorElement(element) &&
             !IsLegacyModernizerDarkSysColor(element, liveColors[i]))) {
            continue;
        }
        restoreElems[restoreCount] = element;
        restoreColors[restoreCount] = themeColors[i];
        ++restoreCount;
    }

    if (!restoreCount)
        return true;
    if (!SetSysColors(restoreCount, restoreElems, restoreColors)) {
        Wh_Log(L"SetSysColors SysMetrics restore failed: %u",
               GetLastError());
        return false;
    }
    return true;
}

static COLORREF GetRestorableSysColor(int index);

static COLORREF AccentBaselineSysColor(int index)
{
    COLORREF themeColors[kLegacyDarkSysColorCount];
    if (QueryThemeSysMetricsColors(themeColors)) {
        const COLORREF color = ThemeSysMetricsColorFor(themeColors, index);
        if (color != CLR_INVALID)
            return color;
    }
    return GetRestorableSysColor(index);
}

static COLORREF GetRestorableSysColor(int index)
{
    if (g_darkSysColsSaved) {
        for (int i = 0; i < kDarkSysColorCount; ++i) {
            if (kDarkSysColorElems[i] == index)
                return g_origDarkSysCols[i];
        }
    }
    return GetSysColor_orig ? GetSysColor_orig(index) : GetSysColor(index);
}

static void ApplyDarkSysColors()
{
    // Explorer owns the session-wide table. Other processes receive these
    // colors globally and keep only their local theme/paint hooks active.
    if (!IsCurrentProcessExplorer())
        return;
    // Never over a contrast theme's colors, whatever order the toggle's
    // WM_SYSCOLORCHANGE and WM_SETTINGCHANGE arrive in.
    if (SysHighContrastEnabled())
        return;

    // The baseline must come from a real theme handle; a null handle would
    // fall back to the live system-color table that this mod changes.
    if (!GetSysColor_orig)
        return;

    COLORREF accent = GetSystemAccentColor();
    COLORREF menuBg = (g_settings.ModernContextMenus && MenuUseTransparentBackdrop())
        ? RGB(0, 0, 0)
        : Win32MainDark;

    // Register this process only after a trusted SysMetrics baseline exists.
    // The tagged shared value also upgrades a mapping left by an older build.
    if (!g_darkSysColsSaved) {
        COLORREF freshThemeColors[kLegacyDarkSysColorCount];
        const bool freshThemeMetrics =
            QueryThemeSysMetricsColors(freshThemeColors);
        SharedDarkSysColorsState* shared = nullptr;
        if (DarkSysColsLockShared(&shared)) {
            DarkSysColsPruneAndCountLocked(shared);
            if (freshThemeMetrics) {
                CopyCurrentDarkSysColorsFromThemeMetrics(
                    freshThemeColors, shared->originalCols);
                shared->originalSaved = kDarkSysColorsSysMetricsBaseline;
            } else if (shared->originalSaved !=
                       kDarkSysColorsSysMetricsBaseline) {
                DarkSysColsUnlockShared(shared);
                Wh_Log(L"SetSysColors dark palette skipped: no trusted baseline");
                return;
            }
            memcpy(g_origDarkSysCols, shared->originalCols, sizeof(g_origDarkSysCols));
            if (!DarkSysColsTrackCurrentProcessLocked(shared)) {
                DarkSysColsUnlockShared(shared);
                Wh_Log(L"SetSysColors dark palette skipped: tracking table full");
                return;
            }
            DarkSysColsUnlockShared(shared);
        } else {
            // Without shared coordination, apply only when this process has
            // independently obtained a trusted SysMetrics baseline.
            if (!freshThemeMetrics) {
                Wh_Log(L"SetSysColors dark palette skipped: no trusted baseline");
                return;
            }
            CopyCurrentDarkSysColorsFromThemeMetrics(
                freshThemeColors, g_origDarkSysCols);
        }
        g_darkSysColsSaved = true;
    }

    // Guard: if colors already applied, skip. SetSysColors broadcasts
    // WM_SYSCOLORCHANGE which redraws all top-level windows → flickering.
    // CRITICAL: use GetSysColor_orig (bypasses our hook) to check the REAL
    // system color database. Only checks indices still in the shrunk array
    // above (COLOR_MENUBAR is no longer touched, so checking it here would
    // always read light and defeat the guard).
    if (GetSysColor_orig(COLOR_BTNFACE) == Win32MainDark
        && GetSysColor_orig(COLOR_MENU) == menuBg
        && GetSysColor_orig(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT) == accent
        && GetSysColor_orig(COLOR_BTNTEXT) == WinUI::Dark::TextFillColorPrimary)
        return;

    COLORREF darkCols[kDarkSysColorCount] = {
        Win32MainDark,  // COLOR_BTNFACE      dialog/window bg
        menuBg,     // COLOR_MENU         popup menu bg
        accent,     // COLOR_HIGHLIGHT    selection/hover bg
        accent,     // COLOR_HOTLIGHT     hyperlinks
        accent,     // COLOR_MENUHILIGHT  menu item hover
        WinUI::Dark::TextFillColorPrimary,  // COLOR_BTNTEXT
        WinUI::Dark::TextFillColorPrimary,  // COLOR_MENUTEXT
    };
    if (!SetSysColors(kDarkSysColorCount, kDarkSysColorElems, darkCols))
        Wh_Log(L"SetSysColors dark palette apply failed: %u", GetLastError());
}

static void RestoreDarkSysColors()
{
    if (!IsCurrentProcessExplorer() || !g_darkSysColsSaved)
        return;

    COLORREF freshThemeColors[kLegacyDarkSysColorCount];
    const bool freshThemeMetrics =
        QueryThemeSysMetricsColors(freshThemeColors);
    bool releaseComplete = false;

    // Only the last tracked participant restores the session-wide table.
    SharedDarkSysColorsState* shared = nullptr;
    if (DarkSysColsLockShared(&shared)) {
        DarkSysColsUntrackCurrentProcessLocked(shared);
        int remaining = DarkSysColsPruneAndCountLocked(shared);
        if (remaining <= 0) {
            bool restored = false;
            // A contrast theme has already written its own colors.
            if (SysHighContrastEnabled()) {
                restored = true;
            } else if (freshThemeMetrics) {
                COLORREF liveColors[kLegacyDarkSysColorCount];
                ReadLiveSysColors(liveColors);
                restored = RestoreThemeSysMetricsColors(
                    freshThemeColors, liveColors);
            } else if (shared->originalSaved ==
                       kDarkSysColorsSysMetricsBaseline) {
                restored = !!SetSysColors(
                    kDarkSysColorCount, kDarkSysColorElems,
                    shared->originalCols);
                if (!restored) {
                    Wh_Log(L"SetSysColors shared baseline restore failed: %u",
                           GetLastError());
                }
            } else {
                Wh_Log(L"SetSysColors restore skipped: no trusted baseline");
            }
            if (restored) {
                shared->originalSaved = FALSE;
                releaseComplete = true;
            } else if (!DarkSysColsTrackCurrentProcessLocked(shared)) {
                Wh_Log(L"SetSysColors restore retry tracking failed: table full");
            }
        } else {
            releaseComplete = true;
        }
        // else: other processes still count on dark colors staying applied
        // -- leave the live system table alone.
        DarkSysColsUnlockShared(shared);
    } else {
        // A contrast theme has already written its own colors.
        if (SysHighContrastEnabled()) {
            releaseComplete = true;
        } else if (freshThemeMetrics) {
            COLORREF liveColors[kLegacyDarkSysColorCount];
            ReadLiveSysColors(liveColors);
            releaseComplete = RestoreThemeSysMetricsColors(
                freshThemeColors, liveColors);
        } else {
            releaseComplete = !!SetSysColors(
                kDarkSysColorCount, kDarkSysColorElems, g_origDarkSysCols);
            if (!releaseComplete) {
                Wh_Log(L"SetSysColors local baseline restore failed: %u",
                       GetLastError());
            }
        }
    }
    if (releaseComplete)
        g_darkSysColsSaved = false;
}

// Classic Open/Save places bar: a transparent/customer-erase toolbar whose
// parent must handle CDDS_PREERASE or it falls back to a light erase. Match the
// full stable style word so modern picker breadcrumb toolbars are excluded.
static bool IsClassicPlacesBarToolbar(HWND hwndFrom)
{
    if (!hwndFrom)
        return false;
    wchar_t cls[32] = {};
    if (!GetClassNameW(hwndFrom, cls, ARRAYSIZE(cls)) || _wcsicmp(cls, L"ToolbarWindow32") != 0)
        return false;
    constexpr LONG_PTR kNeeded =
        WS_CHILD | WS_VISIBLE | WS_TABSTOP |
        TBSTYLE_TOOLTIPS | TBSTYLE_WRAPABLE | TBSTYLE_FLAT |
        TBSTYLE_CUSTOMERASE | TBSTYLE_TRANSPARENT |
        CCS_TOP | CCS_NORESIZE | CCS_NOPARENTALIGN | CCS_NODIVIDER;
    LONG_PTR style = GetWindowLongPtrW(hwndFrom, GWL_STYLE);
    if ((style & kNeeded) != kNeeded)
        return false;
    HWND root = GetAncestor(hwndFrom, GA_ROOT);
    wchar_t rootCls[32] = {};
    return root && GetClassNameW(root, rootCls, ARRAYSIZE(rootCls)) &&
           _wcsicmp(rootCls, L"#32770") == 0 && GetPropW(root, kPropertyDialogDarkModeMarker);
}

// A WM_CTLCOLOR* answer the dialog chose itself, as opposed to the defaults
// the dark subclass replaces: null, a system-color brush, the stock white
// or hollow brush, uxtheme's dialog texture (a pattern brush), or one of
// the mod's own dark shades (what DefWindowProc hands back through the
// mod's hook once the dialog procedure declines). Such a dialog paints its
// own background, so it keeps it in dark mode. Not applied inside
// explorer.exe, whose property sheets are the mod's own dark surfaces.
static bool IsAppOwnedCtlColorBrush(HBRUSH br)
{
    if (IsCurrentProcessExplorer())
        return false;
    if (!br || reinterpret_cast<ULONG_PTR>(br) <= 31)
        return false;
    if (br == GetStockObject(WHITE_BRUSH) || br == GetStockObject(HOLLOW_BRUSH))
        return false;
    for (int sys : { COLOR_BTNFACE, COLOR_WINDOW, COLOR_SCROLLBAR, COLOR_MENU })
        if (br == GetSysColorBrush(sys))
            return false;
    LOGBRUSH lb = {};
    if (!GetObject(br, sizeof(lb), &lb))
        return false;
    return lb.lbStyle == BS_SOLID &&
           lb.lbColor != Win32MainDark && lb.lbColor != ExplorerDarkColor &&
           lb.lbColor != kElevatedPaneDark &&
           lb.lbColor != kNativeExcludedPickerDarkBg &&
           lb.lbColor != kFilePickerChromeDark && lb.lbColor != kFilePickerChromeLight &&
           lb.lbColor != GetSysColor(COLOR_BTNFACE);
}

// The dialog's own WM_CTLCOLORDLG brush, or null when it takes the default.
static HBRUSH AppOwnedDialogBrush(HWND hwnd, HDC hdc)
{
    const COLORREF savedBk = GetBkColor(hdc);
    const COLORREF savedText = GetTextColor(hdc);
    const int savedMode = GetBkMode(hdc);
    HBRUSH br = (HBRUSH)DefSubclassProc(hwnd, WM_CTLCOLORDLG, (WPARAM)hdc, (LPARAM)hwnd);
    SetBkColor(hdc, savedBk);
    SetTextColor(hdc, savedText);
    SetBkMode(hdc, savedMode);
    return IsAppOwnedCtlColorBrush(br) ? br : nullptr;
}

// The ContentDialog colors PaintTaskDialogPanel gives the two panels.
static COLORREF TaskDialogPanelColor(bool content)
{
    const COLORREF base = WinUI::SolidBackgroundFillColorBase(true);
    return content ? WinUI::FlattenOver(WinUI::Dark::LayerFillColorAlt, base) : base;
}

// Where the command band starts in the dialog's client area, or -1 when the
// dialog doesn't draw TaskDialog panels.
static int TaskDialogBandTop(HWND dialog)
{
    const INT_PTR stored = reinterpret_cast<INT_PTR>(
        GetPropW(dialog, kPropTaskDialogBandTop));
    return stored > 0 ? static_cast<int>(stored - 1) : -1;
}

// WM_CTLCOLOR* for a control of such a dialog: the color of the panel it
// sits on, whatever the dialog answered (its own brush matches the native
// light panel, which this mod repaints). Null when the dialog has no panels.
static HBRUSH TaskDialogBandCtlColor(HWND dialog, HWND control, HDC hdc)
{
    const int bandTop = TaskDialogBandTop(dialog);
    if (bandTop < 0 || !control || !hdc)
        return nullptr;
    RECT rc = {};
    if (!GetWindowRect(control, &rc))
        return nullptr;
    MapWindowPoints(nullptr, dialog, reinterpret_cast<POINT*>(&rc), 2);
    const COLORREF bg = TaskDialogPanelColor(rc.bottom <= bandTop);
    HBRUSH br = GetCachedSolidBrush(bg);
    if (!br)
        return nullptr;
    SetTextColor(hdc, WinUI::Dark::TextFillColorPrimary);
    SetBkColor(hdc, bg);
    SetBkMode(hdc, TRANSPARENT);
    return br;
}

static LRESULT CALLBACK PropertyDialogSubclassProc(
    HWND hwnd, UINT msg, WPARAM wp, LPARAM lp, DWORD_PTR dwRefData)
{
    if (msg == WM_NCDESTROY) {
        WindhawkUtils::RemoveWindowSubclassFromAnyThread(hwnd, PropertyDialogSubclassProc);
        RemovePropW(hwnd, kPropertyDialogDarkModeMarker);
        RemovePropW(hwnd, kDarkWindowAppliedMarker);
        RemovePropW(hwnd, kPropDuiListPrimed);
        RemovePropW(hwnd, kFilePickerBottomRuleMarker);
        RemovePropW(hwnd, kFilePickerMicaTopMarker);
        RemovePropW(hwnd, kPropTaskDialogBandTop);
        return DefSubclassProc(hwnd, msg, wp, lp);
    }

    switch (msg) {
    case WM_CTLCOLORDLG:
    case WM_CTLCOLORSTATIC:
    case WM_CTLCOLORBTN:
    case WM_CTLCOLORSCROLLBAR: {
        // A dialog answering with its own brush keeps it (and the DC colors
        // it set along with it), unless its controls sit on TaskDialog
        // panels this mod repaints.
        const LRESULT own = DefSubclassProc(hwnd, msg, wp, lp);
        if (msg != WM_CTLCOLORDLG) {
            if (HBRUSH panel = TaskDialogBandCtlColor(
                    hwnd, reinterpret_cast<HWND>(lp), reinterpret_cast<HDC>(wp)))
                return reinterpret_cast<LRESULT>(panel);
        }
        if (IsAppOwnedCtlColorBrush((HBRUSH)own)) {
            RememberCtlColorBackground(reinterpret_cast<HDC>(wp),
                reinterpret_cast<HWND>(lp), (HBRUSH)own);
            return own;
        }
        // Tab pages (inside pane) use pane color; main dialog uses outer color
        bool isPage = (dwRefData == kPropertyPageSubclassId);
        COLORREF bg = isPage ? kElevatedPaneDark : Win32MainDark;
        HBRUSH br = isPage
            ? (g_elevatedPaneDarkBrush ? g_elevatedPaneDarkBrush : (g_elevatedPaneDarkBrush = CreateSolidBrush(kElevatedPaneDark)))
            : (g_win32MainDarkBrush   ? g_win32MainDarkBrush   : (g_win32MainDarkBrush   = CreateSolidBrush(Win32MainDark)));
        if (!isPage && FilePickerChromeRoot(hwnd)) {
            bg = FilePickerControlBackground(true);
            br = GetCachedSolidBrush(bg);
        }
        SetTextColor((HDC)wp, WinUI::Dark::TextFillColorPrimary);
        SetBkColor((HDC)wp, bg);
        SetBkMode((HDC)wp, TRANSPARENT);
        return (LRESULT)br;
    }

    case WM_CTLCOLOREDIT:
    case WM_CTLCOLORLISTBOX: {
        LRESULT orig = DefSubclassProc(hwnd, msg, wp, lp);
        HBRUSH origBr = (HBRUSH)orig;
        bool isGenericBrush = (orig == 0 ||
            origBr == GetSysColorBrush(COLOR_WINDOW) ||
            origBr == GetSysColorBrush(COLOR_BTNFACE) ||
            origBr == GetSysColorBrush(COLOR_SCROLLBAR) ||
            origBr == (HBRUSH)GetStockObject(WHITE_BRUSH) ||
            origBr == (HBRUSH)GetStockObject(HOLLOW_BRUSH));
        if (!isGenericBrush)
            return orig;
        if (!g_elevatedPaneDarkBrush)
            g_elevatedPaneDarkBrush = CreateSolidBrush(kElevatedPaneDark);
        SetTextColor((HDC)wp, WinUI::Dark::TextFillColorPrimary);
        SetBkColor((HDC)wp, kElevatedPaneDark);
        return (LRESULT)g_elevatedPaneDarkBrush;
    }

    // DrawThemeParentBackground sends WM_PRINTCLIENT to the parent. The tab
    // control (parent == root dialog) uses this to get the strip
    // background; a themed child control -- a checkbox's box glyph, a
    // static label with a transparent theme part, etc. (parent == the page
    // dialog) -- uses the exact same message to get ITS backdrop. Same
    // isPage split as the WM_CTLCOLORSTATIC/BTN case above: without it,
    // every one of those child-control backdrops came out Win32MainDark (the
    // darker strip shade) even on a page, showing as a mismatched rectangle
    // against the lighter kElevatedPaneDark page background around it.
    case WM_PRINTCLIENT: {
        bool isPage = (dwRefData == kPropertyPageSubclassId);
        HDC hdc = (HDC)wp;
        RECT rc;
        GetClientRect(hwnd, &rc);
        // A themed child's backdrop on a dialog with TaskDialog panels: each
        // part of the client in its panel's color.
        if (const int bandTop = TaskDialogBandTop(hwnd); bandTop >= 0) {
            RECT content = rc;
            content.bottom = std::clamp<LONG>(bandTop, rc.top, rc.bottom);
            RECT band = rc;
            band.top = content.bottom;
            if (HBRUSH br = GetCachedSolidBrush(TaskDialogPanelColor(true)))
                FillRect(hdc, &content, br);
            if (HBRUSH br = GetCachedSolidBrush(TaskDialogPanelColor(false)))
                FillRect(hdc, &band, br);
            return 0;
        }
        if (HBRUSH own = AppOwnedDialogBrush(hwnd, hdc)) {
            FillRect(hdc, &rc, own);
            return 0;
        }
        HBRUSH br = isPage
            ? (g_elevatedPaneDarkBrush ? g_elevatedPaneDarkBrush : (g_elevatedPaneDarkBrush = CreateSolidBrush(kElevatedPaneDark)))
            : (g_win32MainDarkBrush   ? g_win32MainDarkBrush   : (g_win32MainDarkBrush   = CreateSolidBrush(Win32MainDark)));
        if (!isPage && FilePickerChromeRoot(hwnd)) {
            FilePickerEraseChrome(hdc, rc, true);
            return 0;
        }
        FillRect(hdc, &rc, br);
        return 0;
    }

    // Tab selection change: SetSysColors handles colors for new controls
    case WM_NOTIFY: {
        const NMHDR* nm = reinterpret_cast<const NMHDR*>(lp);
        if (!nm) break;

        if (nm->code == NM_CUSTOMDRAW) {
            const NMCUSTOMDRAW* ncd = reinterpret_cast<const NMCUSTOMDRAW*>(lp);

            // Classic places bar: answer its pre-erase notification with our
            // dark background instead of letting it fall back to its own
            // default (light) erase, then also request per-item notify at
            // paint time so item labels get our text color instead of the
            // system default (black) -- CDRF_SKIPDEFAULT at PREERASE only
            // answers the erase stage, it says nothing about how item text
            // gets drawn later. See IsClassicPlacesBarToolbar.
            if (IsClassicPlacesBarToolbar(nm->hwndFrom)) {
                if (ncd->dwDrawStage == CDDS_PREERASE) {
                    if (!g_win32MainDarkBrush)
                        g_win32MainDarkBrush = CreateSolidBrush(Win32MainDark);
                    if (g_win32MainDarkBrush)
                        FillRect(ncd->hdc, &ncd->rc, g_win32MainDarkBrush);
                    return CDRF_SKIPDEFAULT;
                }
                if (ncd->dwDrawStage == CDDS_PREPAINT)
                    return CDRF_NOTIFYITEMDRAW;
                if (ncd->dwDrawStage == CDDS_ITEMPREPAINT) {
                    // Icon/pill modernization rides on LegacyRebarControls,
                    // same as its light-mode counterpart in
                    // ClassicDlgToolbarSubclassProc. The PREERASE dark fill
                    // above stays unconditional either way -- without it the
                    // strip would show as a light hole in a dark dialog.
                    if (g_settings.LegacyRebarControls &&
                        PaintClassicPlacesBarItem(nm->hwndFrom, ncd))
                        return CDRF_SKIPDEFAULT;
                    // Unrecognized command, or LegacyRebarControls off --
                    // preserve the original dark-mode text legibility fix as
                    // a fallback instead of drawing nothing.
                    SetTextColor(ncd->hdc, WinUI::Dark::TextFillColorPrimary);
                    SetBkMode(ncd->hdc, TRANSPARENT);
                    return CDRF_DODEFAULT;
                }
            }
        }
        break;
    }

    case WM_ERASEBKGND: {
        bool isPage = (dwRefData == kPropertyPageSubclassId);
        COLORREF bg = isPage ? kElevatedPaneDark : Win32MainDark;
        HDC hdc = (HDC)wp;
        RECT rc;
        GetClientRect(hwnd, &rc);
        // What DefDlgProc does with a dialog's own WM_CTLCOLORDLG brush.
        if (HBRUSH own = AppOwnedDialogBrush(hwnd, hdc)) {
            FillRect_orig(hdc, &rc, own);
            return 1;
        }
        if (!isPage && FilePickerChromeRoot(hwnd)) {
            FilePickerEraseChrome(hdc, rc, true);
        } else {
            HBRUSH hBr = CreateSolidBrush(bg);
            if (hBr) { FillRect_orig(hdc, &rc, hBr); DeleteObject(hBr); }
        }
        if (!isPage)
            FilePickerBottomRule(hwnd, hdc);

        // Experiment: extend the flat content-pane fill out to the real
        // window edges. HandleThemeDraw's own TABP_PANE paint can't do this
        // itself -- its hdc belongs to the tab control, whose DC is clipped
        // to its own bounds no matter what rect we hand FillRect. This hdc
        // is the root dialog's own, unclipped, so the side margins can
        // actually be reached from here, drawn underneath where the tab
        // control then paints its own (correctly clipped) matching fill on
        // top. No rounding/border -- two independently-drawn shapes never
        // lined up pixel-perfectly, so just the plain color, which needs no
        // alignment at all.
        if (!isPage && g_settings.RoundedTabPane) {
            HWND hwndTab = FindWindowExW(hwnd, nullptr, L"SysTabControl32", nullptr);
            RECT rcContent;
            if (hwndTab &&
                GetExtendedTabPaneRect(hwnd, hwndTab, rc, &rcContent)) {
                if (HBRUSH hPaneBr = CreateSolidBrush(kElevatedPaneDark)) {
                    FillRect_orig(hdc, &rcContent, hPaneBr);
                    DeleteObject(hPaneBr);
                }
            }
        }
        return 1;
    }
    }
    return DefSubclassProc(hwnd, msg, wp, lp);
}

// Light mode's counterpart to PropertyDialogSubclassProc's WM_ERASEBKGND pane
// extension -- installed independently of the whole dark-mode subclass/
// color-override system (ApplyPropertyDialogDarkMode et al.), since none of that is
// needed here: native light-theme colors are already correct everywhere
// else in the dialog. The one gap is the margin between the tab control's
// own edges and the real dialog edges, which natively erases to the
// dialog's own COLOR_BTNFACE-ish class brush -- this fills just that
// margin white afterward, so it reads as the same elevated white surface
// HandleThemeDraw's TABP_PANE paints inside the tab control itself, instead
// of a mismatched gray band around it.
static LRESULT CALLBACK PropertySheetLightPaneSubclassProc(
    HWND hwnd, UINT msg, WPARAM wp, LPARAM lp, DWORD_PTR)
{
    if (msg == WM_NCDESTROY) {
        WindhawkUtils::RemoveWindowSubclassFromAnyThread(hwnd, PropertySheetLightPaneSubclassProc);
        RemovePropW(hwnd, kPropertySheetLightPaneSubclassMarker);
        return DefSubclassProc(hwnd, msg, wp, lp);
    }

    if (msg == WM_ERASEBKGND) {
        // Let native erase happen first (fills the dialog's real class
        // brush) -- this only adds a patch on top, it never replaces the
        // dialog's own background the way the dark version's handler does.
        LRESULT res = DefSubclassProc(hwnd, msg, wp, lp);
        if (!g_settings.RoundedTabPane)
            return res;

        HWND hwndTab = FindWindowExW(hwnd, nullptr, L"SysTabControl32", nullptr);
        RECT rc;
        RECT rcContent;
        if (hwndTab && GetClientRect(hwnd, &rc) &&
            GetExtendedTabPaneRect(hwnd, hwndTab, rc, &rcContent)) {
            if (HBRUSH hPaneBr = GetCachedSolidBrush(WinUI::Light::SolidBackgroundFillColorTertiary))
                FillRect_orig((HDC)wp, &rcContent, hPaneBr);
        }
        return res;
    }

    return DefSubclassProc(hwnd, msg, wp, lp);
}

// Light file picker chrome: the erase, WM_CTLCOLOR* and WM_PRINTCLIENT of
// the picker dialog and its nested template dialog in the light chrome shade,
// plus the rule above the file-name area on the root. The dialog's own
// erase asks WM_CTLCOLORDLG inside user32, which no SendMessageW hook sees,
// hence a subclass. Installed on every light #32770 at creation -- the
// picker can't be told apart before its children exist -- with
// FilePickerChromeRoot deciding per message; other dialogs pass through.
// Dark pickers get the same shade from PropertyDialogSubclassProc.
static LRESULT CALLBACK FilePickerLightSubclassProc(
    HWND hwnd, UINT msg, WPARAM wp, LPARAM lp, DWORD_PTR)
{
    if (msg == WM_NCDESTROY) {
        WindhawkUtils::RemoveWindowSubclassFromAnyThread(hwnd, FilePickerLightSubclassProc);
        RemovePropW(hwnd, kFilePickerLightSubclassMarker);
        RemovePropW(hwnd, kFilePickerBottomRuleMarker);
        RemovePropW(hwnd, kFilePickerMicaTopMarker);
        return DefSubclassProc(hwnd, msg, wp, lp);
    }

    switch (msg) {
    case WM_CTLCOLORDLG:
    case WM_CTLCOLORSTATIC:
    case WM_CTLCOLORBTN: {
        if (g_darkModeActive || !FilePickerChromeRoot(hwnd))
            break;
        const LRESULT own = DefSubclassProc(hwnd, msg, wp, lp);
        if (IsAppOwnedCtlColorBrush((HBRUSH)own))
            return own;
        const COLORREF chrome = FilePickerControlBackground(false);
        HBRUSH br = GetCachedSolidBrush(chrome);
        if (!br)
            return own;
        SetBkColor((HDC)wp, chrome);
        return (LRESULT)br;
    }

    case WM_ERASEBKGND:
    case WM_PRINTCLIENT: {
        if (g_darkModeActive)
            break;
        HWND root = FilePickerChromeRoot(hwnd);
        if (!root)
            break;
        HDC hdc = (HDC)wp;
        RECT rc;
        GetClientRect(hwnd, &rc);
        if (HBRUSH own = AppOwnedDialogBrush(hwnd, hdc)) {
            FillRect_orig(hdc, &rc, own);
        } else {
            FilePickerEraseChrome(hdc, rc, false);
            if (hwnd == root && msg == WM_ERASEBKGND)
                FilePickerBottomRule(hwnd, hdc);
        }
        return msg == WM_ERASEBKGND ? 1 : 0;
    }
    }
    return DefSubclassProc(hwnd, msg, wp, lp);
}

static void ApplyPropertyDialogDarkMode(HWND hwnd)
{
    if (g_darkModeUnloading.load(std::memory_order_acquire) || !IsSystemDarkMode()) return;
    if (!IsCustomDarkModeAllowed()) return;
    if (GetPropW(hwnd, kPropertyDialogDarkModeMarker)) return;
    // #32770 pages inside an AeroWizard still need this: a page created
    // before the wizard's own kPropAeroWizardCaption prop
    // existed (its first page) got this normally via the branch below and
    // rendered correctly, while a page created after that prop existed
    // (any later page) hit this exclusion and never got its WM_CTLCOLORDLG
    // answered, staying white -- a creation-order race, not an AeroWizard
    // compatibility issue. Only the wizard's own non-#32770 windows still
    // need to be left alone here.
    wchar_t propDlgCls[16] = {};
    bool propDlgIs32770 = GetClassNameW(hwnd, propDlgCls, ARRAYSIZE(propDlgCls)) &&
        wcscmp(propDlgCls, L"#32770") == 0;
    if (!propDlgIs32770 && IsAeroWizardRawWindow(hwnd)) return;
    SetPropW(hwnd, kPropertyDialogDarkModeMarker, (HANDLE)1);
    SetPropW(hwnd, kDarkWindowAppliedMarker, (HANDLE)1);

    BOOL darkAttr = TRUE;
    DwmSetWindowAttribute(hwnd, DWMWA_USE_IMMERSIVE_DARK_MODE, &darkAttr, sizeof(darkAttr));
    COLORREF borderClr = RGB(32, 32, 32);
    DwmSetWindowAttribute(hwnd, 34, &borderClr, sizeof(borderClr));
    if (g_cbdAllowDark) g_cbdAllowDark(hwnd, true);

    // DarkMode_Explorer: tells DefDlgProc to use dark theme for WM_CTLCOLOR*.
    // Without this, the dialog returns GetSysColorBrush(COLOR_3DFACE) which
    // may be a cached light brush depending on timing.
    if (IsCurrentProcessExplorer())
        SetWindowTheme(hwnd, L"DarkMode_Explorer", nullptr);

    // Nested child dialogs inherit the elevated pane shade; unrelated WS_CHILD
    // dialogs remain on the base background.
    const DWORD_PTR subclassKind =
        IsInTabbedPropertyPane(hwnd)
            ? kPropertyPageSubclassId
            : kPropertyDialogSubclassId;
    if (!WindhawkUtils::SetWindowSubclassFromAnyThread(
            hwnd, PropertyDialogSubclassProc, subclassKind)) {
        RemovePropW(hwnd, kPropertyDialogDarkModeMarker);
        RemovePropW(hwnd, kDarkWindowAppliedMarker);
        return;
    }

    SetWindowPos(hwnd, nullptr, 0, 0, 0, 0,
        SWP_NOMOVE | SWP_NOSIZE | SWP_NOZORDER | SWP_NOACTIVATE | SWP_FRAMECHANGED);
}

// FindWindowExW(nullptr, ...) enumerates every top-level window on the
// desktop across ALL processes -- filter by PID before using a match, same
// as MenuDetectPopupFromUAH's #32768 lookup above. Without this, a
// class-brush helper called with no sample (from Wh_ModUninit/
// Wh_ModSettingsChanged, where there genuinely is none) can grab a foreign
// process's window of the same class, cache ITS class brush as "the
// original to restore later", write this mod's own brush handle into a
// class it doesn't own, and force a RedrawWindow on an unrelated app --
// while never actually themeing anything in this process.
static HWND FindWindowInCurrentProcess(LPCWSTR className)
{
    const DWORD myPid = GetCurrentProcessId();
    HWND hwnd = nullptr;
    while ((hwnd = FindWindowExW(nullptr, hwnd, className, nullptr)) != nullptr) {
        DWORD pid = 0;
        GetWindowThreadProcessId(hwnd, &pid);
        if (pid == myPid)
            return hwnd;
    }
    return nullptr;
}

static void SetPropertyDialogClassBrush(bool dark, HWND sample)
{
    HWND hwnd = sample;
    bool destroySample = false;
    if (!hwnd || !IsWindow(hwnd)) {
        hwnd = FindWindowInCurrentProcess(L"#32770");
        if (!hwnd) {
            hwnd = CreateWindowExW(0, L"#32770", nullptr, WS_POPUP,
                0, 0, 0, 0, nullptr, nullptr, nullptr, nullptr);
            destroySample = hwnd != nullptr;
        }
    }
    if (!hwnd)
        return;

    if (!g_propertyDialogOriginalClassBrushSaved) {
        g_propertyDialogOriginalClassBrush = reinterpret_cast<HBRUSH>(
            GetClassLongPtrW(hwnd, GCLP_HBRBACKGROUND));
        g_propertyDialogOriginalClassBrushSaved = true;
    }

    HBRUSH brush = dark ? g_win32MainDarkBrush : g_propertyDialogOriginalClassBrush;
    if (!brush && !dark)
        brush = GetSysColorBrush(COLOR_3DFACE);
    if (brush)
        SetClassLongPtrW(hwnd, GCLP_HBRBACKGROUND, reinterpret_cast<LONG_PTR>(brush));

    if (destroySample)
        DestroyWindow(hwnd);
}

static HBRUSH g_fontViewOriginalClassBrush = nullptr;
static bool g_fontViewOriginalClassBrushSaved = false;

// Same save-once/restore pattern as SetPropertyDialogClassBrush, but never
// spins up a throwaway FontViewWClass window -- unlike #32770 it's a
// specialized host, not a generic dialog class safe to instantiate blindly.
// If no live instance exists, this is a no-op: the next window of this
// class is created via NtUserCreateWindowEx_hook, which always re-applies
// the brush for the current mode, so there's nothing stale left dangling.
static void SetFontViewClassBrush(bool dark, HWND sample)
{
    HWND hwnd = (sample && IsWindow(sample))
        ? sample
        : FindWindowInCurrentProcess(L"FontViewWClass");
    if (!hwnd)
        return;

    if (!g_fontViewOriginalClassBrushSaved) {
        g_fontViewOriginalClassBrush = reinterpret_cast<HBRUSH>(
            GetClassLongPtrW(hwnd, GCLP_HBRBACKGROUND));
        g_fontViewOriginalClassBrushSaved = true;
    }

    HBRUSH brush = dark ? g_win32MainDarkBrush : g_fontViewOriginalClassBrush;
    if (!brush && !dark)
        brush = GetSysColorBrush(COLOR_3DFACE);
    if (brush)
        SetClassLongPtrW(hwnd, GCLP_HBRBACKGROUND, reinterpret_cast<LONG_PTR>(brush));

    RedrawWindow(hwnd, nullptr, nullptr,
        RDW_INVALIDATE | RDW_ERASE | RDW_FRAME | RDW_ALLCHILDREN);
}

static void ApplyCustomDarkModeToExistingWindow(HWND hwnd)
{
    if (!hwnd || !IsWindow(hwnd) || !IsCustomDarkModeAllowed() ||
        g_darkModeUnloading.load(std::memory_order_acquire))
        return;

    wchar_t cls[64] = {};
    GetClassNameW(hwnd, cls, ARRAYSIZE(cls));
    if (_wcsicmp(cls, L"#32770") == 0) {
        if (!g_win32MainDarkBrush)
            g_win32MainDarkBrush = CreateSolidBrush(Win32MainDark);
        SetPropertyDialogClassBrush(true, hwnd);
        ApplyPropertyDialogDarkMode(hwnd);
        return;
    }

    if (GetWindowLongPtrW(hwnd, GWL_STYLE) & WS_CHILD)
        return;
    if (IsCurrentProcessExplorer() &&
        (_wcsicmp(cls, L"CabinetWClass") == 0 ||
         _wcsicmp(cls, L"ExploreWClass") == 0))
        return;
    if (_wcsicmp(cls, L"ComboLBox") == 0 || IsAeroWizardRawWindow(hwnd))
        return;

    const BOOL dark = TRUE;
    DwmSetWindowAttribute(hwnd, DWMWA_USE_IMMERSIVE_DARK_MODE, &dark, sizeof(dark));
    if (g_cbdAllowDark)
        g_cbdAllowDark(hwnd, true);
    SetPropW(hwnd, L"UseImmersiveDarkModeColors", (HANDLE)1);
    SetPropW(hwnd, kDarkWindowAppliedMarker, (HANDLE)1);
    HwndDarkCacheInvalidate();
}

static void RemoveCustomDarkModeFromWindow(HWND hwnd)
{
    if (!hwnd || !IsWindow(hwnd))
        return;

    const bool wasDialog = GetPropW(hwnd, kPropertyDialogDarkModeMarker) != nullptr;
    const bool wasWindow = GetPropW(hwnd, kDarkWindowAppliedMarker) != nullptr;
    if (!wasDialog && !wasWindow)
        return;

    if (wasDialog)
        WindhawkUtils::RemoveWindowSubclassFromAnyThread(hwnd, PropertyDialogSubclassProc);

    RemovePropW(hwnd, kPropertyDialogDarkModeMarker);
    RemovePropW(hwnd, kPropTaskDialogBandTop);
    RemovePropW(hwnd, L"_PropDkCounterApplied");
    RemovePropW(hwnd, L"UseImmersiveDarkModeColors");
    RemovePropW(hwnd, kDarkWindowAppliedMarker);
    HwndDarkCacheInvalidate();

    const BOOL dark = FALSE;
    const COLORREF defaultColor = DWMWA_COLOR_DEFAULT;
    DwmSetWindowAttribute(hwnd, DWMWA_USE_IMMERSIVE_DARK_MODE, &dark, sizeof(dark));
    DwmSetWindowAttribute(hwnd, kDwmwaBorderColor,
        &defaultColor, sizeof(defaultColor));
    if (g_cbdAllowDark)
        g_cbdAllowDark(hwnd, false);
    if (wasDialog && IsCurrentProcessExplorer())
        SetWindowTheme(hwnd, nullptr, nullptr);

    SetWindowPos(hwnd, nullptr, 0, 0, 0, 0,
        SWP_NOMOVE | SWP_NOSIZE | SWP_NOZORDER |
        SWP_NOACTIVATE | SWP_FRAMECHANGED);
}

// ── Classic dialog top toolbar: Fluent glyph icons ──────────────────────────
// Cosmetic-only glyph swap on the classic Open/Save dialog toolbar. Must
// render correctly in light mode too, so (unlike the places bar) this needs
// no kPropertyDialogDarkModeMarker gate and installs unconditionally.

// Distinguished from the places bar by NOT having TBSTYLE_CUSTOMERASE/
// TBSTYLE_WRAPABLE -- full style word confirmed via WinSpy on the real
// control (same "match everything, it's all creation-time and stable"
// reasoning as IsClassicPlacesBarToolbar).
static bool IsClassicDialogTopToolbar(HWND hwndFrom)
{
    if (!hwndFrom)
        return false;
    wchar_t cls[32] = {};
    if (!GetClassNameW(hwndFrom, cls, ARRAYSIZE(cls)) || _wcsicmp(cls, L"ToolbarWindow32") != 0)
        return false;
    constexpr LONG_PTR kNeeded =
        WS_CHILD | WS_VISIBLE | WS_TABSTOP |
        TBSTYLE_TOOLTIPS | TBSTYLE_FLAT | TBSTYLE_TRANSPARENT |
        CCS_TOP | CCS_NORESIZE | CCS_NODIVIDER;
    LONG_PTR style = GetWindowLongPtrW(hwndFrom, GWL_STYLE);
    if ((style & kNeeded) != kNeeded)
        return false;
    // Explicit exclusion, not just a missing-bit gap: the places bar also
    // has TRANSPARENT, and the two lists were derived from separate WinSpy
    // dumps -- guard against them ever partially overlapping on some other
    // Windows build.
    if (style & (TBSTYLE_CUSTOMERASE | TBSTYLE_WRAPABLE))
        return false;
    HWND root = GetAncestor(hwndFrom, GA_ROOT);
    wchar_t rootCls[32] = {};
    return root && GetClassNameW(root, rootCls, ARRAYSIZE(rootCls)) &&
           _wcsicmp(rootCls, L"#32770") == 0;
}

// idCommand values observed via the diagnostic probe on this dialog's
// toolbar -- comdlg32-internal, undocumented, but stable in practice (the
// bitmaps behind them still carry XP/Vista-era art, meaning this part of
// comdlg32 hasn't changed in a very long time). Unrecognized commands
// (separators, anything added by a future build) fall through to the
// control's own default icon untouched.
static constexpr UINT_PTR kClassicDlgViewCommand = 40970; // Exibir -- BTNS_WHOLEDROPDOWN

static const wchar_t* ClassicDialogToolbarGlyphForCommand(UINT_PTR idCommand)
{
    switch (idCommand) {
    case 40971:                   return GLYPH_NAV_BACK;      // Voltar
    case 40961:                   return GLYPH_NAV_UP;        // Subir um nivel
    case 40962:                   return GLYPH_DLG_NEWFOLDER; // Nova pasta
    case kClassicDlgViewCommand:  return GLYPH_DLG_VIEW;      // Exibir
    default:                      return nullptr;
    }
}

// ── Classic places bar: animated SVG glyph icons ────────────────────────────
// Same idCommand->shortcut mapping confirmed via the diagnostic probe
// (consecutive 41060-41064, unlike the top toolbar's scattered IDs) --
// comdlg32-internal, undocumented, but stable in practice.
static const wchar_t* PlacesBarGlyphForCommand(UINT_PTR idCommand)
{
    switch (idCommand) {
    case 41060: return GLYPH_HOME;      // Inicio
    case 41061: return GLYPH_DESKTOP;   // Area de Trabalho
    case 41062: return GLYPH_LIBRARY;   // Bibliotecas
    case 41063: return GLYPH_THISPC;    // Este Computador
    case 41064: return GLYPH_NETWORK;   // Rede
    default:    return nullptr;
    }
}

// Same bespoke wipe-to-Filled durations already used by the Explorer nav
// pane for these exact 5 glyphs (see ICON_POP_WIPE_DUR_* above).
static DOUBLE PlacesBarWipeDuration(wchar_t glyphCh)
{
    if (glyphCh == GLYPH_HOME[0])    return ICON_POP_WIPE_DUR_HOME;
    if (glyphCh == GLYPH_DESKTOP[0]) return ICON_POP_DESKTOP_FADE_DUR + ICON_POP_DESKTOP_BLOOM_DUR;
    if (glyphCh == GLYPH_THISPC[0])  return ICON_POP_WIPE_DUR_THISPC;
    if (glyphCh == GLYPH_LIBRARY[0]) return ICON_POP_WIPE_DUR_LIBRARY;
    if (glyphCh == GLYPH_NETWORK[0]) return ICON_POP_WIPE_DUR_NETWORK;
    return 0.0;
}

// Dispatches to the same bespoke intro-animation functions the Explorer nav
// pane uses on genuine selection change (DrawHomeDoorFillIn, DrawThisPcCrtOn,
// etc.) -- all take a plain hdc/rc/color/t, no TreeView/HTREEITEM dependency,
// so they're reused verbatim here for the places bar's "this is now the
// current location" transition.
static void PlacesBarDrawWipe(HDC hdc, const RECT& rc, COLORREF color,
    wchar_t glyphCh, float wipeElapsedSec, bool inCabinet)
{
    if (glyphCh == GLYPH_HOME[0]) {
        FLOAT t = wipeElapsedSec / (FLOAT)ICON_POP_WIPE_DUR_HOME;
        DrawHomeDoorFillIn(hdc, rc, color, t, inCabinet);
    } else if (glyphCh == GLYPH_DESKTOP[0]) {
        if (wipeElapsedSec < (FLOAT)ICON_POP_DESKTOP_FADE_DUR) {
            FLOAT t = EaseOutCubic(wipeElapsedSec / (FLOAT)ICON_POP_DESKTOP_FADE_DUR);
            DrawCrossfadeSingle(hdc, rc, color, GLYPH_DESKTOP[0], t, inCabinet);
        } else {
            FLOAT t = (wipeElapsedSec - (FLOAT)ICON_POP_DESKTOP_FADE_DUR) / (FLOAT)ICON_POP_DESKTOP_BLOOM_DUR;
            DrawDesktopBloomRise(hdc, rc, color, t, inCabinet);
        }
    } else if (glyphCh == GLYPH_THISPC[0]) {
        FLOAT t = wipeElapsedSec / (FLOAT)ICON_POP_WIPE_DUR_THISPC;
        DrawThisPcCrtOn(hdc, rc, color, t, inCabinet);
    } else if (glyphCh == GLYPH_LIBRARY[0]) {
        FLOAT t = wipeElapsedSec / (FLOAT)ICON_POP_WIPE_DUR_LIBRARY;
        DrawLibraryBooksIn(hdc, rc, color, t, inCabinet);
    } else if (glyphCh == GLYPH_NETWORK[0]) {
        FLOAT t = wipeElapsedSec / (FLOAT)ICON_POP_WIPE_DUR_NETWORK;
        DrawNetworkScanIn(hdc, rc, color, t, inCabinet);
    }
}

// Buttons are tiny (16px icons in a 28px-tall strip): fill, glyph and the
// Exibir chevron all come from one render target and coordinate system, so
// the hover/press scale pivots exactly where the fill sits.
static void PaintClassicDlgToolbarItem(const NMCUSTOMDRAW* cd, const wchar_t* glyphStr)
{
    if (!cd || !cd->hdc || !glyphStr)
        return;

    RECT rc = cd->rc;
    if (rc.right <= rc.left || rc.bottom <= rc.top)
        return;

    const bool hot      = (cd->uItemState & CDIS_HOT) != 0;
    const bool pressed  = (cd->uItemState & CDIS_SELECTED) != 0;
    const bool disabled = (cd->uItemState & CDIS_DISABLED) != 0;

    HWND ctxHwnd = g_tlsPaintHwnd ? g_tlsPaintHwnd : WindowFromDC(cd->hdc);
    const bool dark = IsDarkForExcludedAwarePaint(ctxHwnd);
    COLORREF textClr = disabled
        ? (dark ? RGB(120, 120, 120) : RGB(160, 160, 160))
        : (dark ? RGB(255, 255, 255) : RGB(25, 26, 26));

    const float w = (float)(rc.right - rc.left);
    const float h = (float)(rc.bottom - rc.top);
    const float dpiScale = (float)DpiForPaintHdc(cd->hdc) / 96.f;
    // Less travel reads as snappier for an immediate state switch (not a
    // timed animation).
    const float scale = disabled ? 1.0f : pressed ? 0.93f : hot ? 1.08f : 1.0f;
    // Font sized so the glyph's bounding box stays clear of the rounded
    // fill's edges.
    const int fontSize = std::max(9, (int)(std::min(w, h) * 0.56f + 0.5f));
    const bool showFill = !disabled && (hot || pressed);
    // Exibir is BTNS_WHOLEDROPDOWN -- comctl32 would normally draw its own
    // dropdown arrow, but CDRF_SKIPDEFAULT suppresses that along with the
    // icon, so we draw a small fixed chevron ourselves. Always-on regardless
    // of hot/pressed (it's a state indicator, not part of the hover
    // feedback), so this button always needs the D2D path even at rest.
    const bool needsChevron = !disabled && (UINT_PTR)cd->dwItemSpec == kClassicDlgViewCommand;
    const float pairOffset = needsChevron ? w * 0.16f : 0.f;
    const float glyphCenterX = w * 0.5f - pairOffset;
    const float centerY = h * 0.5f;

    // Only when no render target can be bound at all.
    auto drawGdiFallback = [&]() {
        RECT glyphRc = rc;
        if (needsChevron)
            glyphRc.right = rc.left + (LONG)(glyphCenterX * 2.f);
        bool textDrawn = false;
        TravelBandUseIconFont(fontSize, [&](HFONT iconFont) {
            HGDIOBJ oldFont = SelectObject(cd->hdc, iconFont);
            if (!oldFont || oldFont == HGDI_ERROR)
                return;
            int oldBkMode = SetBkMode(cd->hdc, TRANSPARENT);
            COLORREF oldTextClr = SetTextColor(cd->hdc, textClr);
            DrawTextW(cd->hdc, glyphStr, 1, &glyphRc,
                DT_CENTER | DT_VCENTER | DT_SINGLELINE | DT_NOCLIP);
            SetTextColor(cd->hdc, oldTextClr);
            SetBkMode(cd->hdc, oldBkMode);
            SelectObject(cd->hdc, oldFont);
            textDrawn = true;
        });
        if (!textDrawn)
            return;

        if (needsChevron) {
            HPEN pen = CreatePen(PS_SOLID, 1, textClr);
            if (pen) {
                HGDIOBJ oldPen = SelectObject(cd->hdc, pen);
                const int cx = rc.left + (int)(w * 0.5f + pairOffset);
                const int cy = rc.top + (int)centerY;
                const int dx = std::max(2, (int)(w * 0.095f + 0.5f));
                const int dy = std::max(1, (int)(h * 0.06f + 0.5f));
                MoveToEx(cd->hdc, cx - dx, cy - dy, nullptr);
                LineTo(cd->hdc, cx, cy + dy);
                LineTo(cd->hdc, cx + dx, cy - dy);
                SelectObject(cd->hdc, oldPen);
                DeleteObject(pen);
            }
        }
    };

    if (!g_d2dFactory) {
        drawGdiFallback();
        return;
    }

    FPUGuard fpu;
    Microsoft::WRL::ComPtr<ID2D1DCRenderTarget> pRT;
    if (FAILED(CreateBoundD2DRenderTarget(cd->hdc, &rc, g_d2dFactory, &pRT))) {
        drawGdiFallback();
        return;
    }
    auto fmt = TravelBandEnsureDWFormat(fontSize);
    if (!fmt) {
        drawGdiFallback();
        return;
    }
    Microsoft::WRL::ComPtr<ID2D1SolidColorBrush> brush;
    pRT->CreateSolidColorBrush(D2D1::ColorF(0.f, 0.f, 0.f, 0.f), &brush);
    if (!brush) {
        drawGdiFallback();
        return;
    }

    pRT->BeginDraw();

    if (showFill) {
        const float alpha = dark ? (pressed ? 0.14f : 0.20f) : (pressed ? 0.06f : 0.09f);
        brush->SetColor(dark ? D2D1::ColorF(1.f, 1.f, 1.f, alpha)
                             : D2D1::ColorF(0.f, 0.f, 0.f, alpha));
        const float inset = 1.2f * dpiScale;
        const float radius = std::min(w, h) * 0.16f; // less rounded than the first pass (was 0.30)
        pRT->FillRoundedRectangle(
            D2D1::RoundedRect(D2D1::RectF(inset, inset, w - inset, h - inset), radius, radius),
            brush.Get());
    }

    brush->SetColor(D2D1::ColorF(GetRValue(textClr) / 255.f,
                                  GetGValue(textClr) / 255.f,
                                  GetBValue(textClr) / 255.f, 1.f));

    // Exibir reserves room for its chevron: glyph and chevron sit
    // symmetrically to either side of the button's true center on the same
    // vertical line, instead of the glyph sitting dead-center with the
    // chevron squeezed into a corner. Everything else keeps the plain
    // dead-center layout (pairOffset 0).
    // Pivot the scale around the glyph's own (possibly off-center) position
    // so the hover pop scales around the icon itself, not the button's
    // geometric center -- both the fill above and this glyph share the same
    // local coordinate space CreateBoundD2DRenderTarget binds around rc.
    D2D1_POINT_2F center = D2D1::Point2F(glyphCenterX, centerY);
    pRT->SetTransform(D2D1::Matrix3x2F::Scale(D2D1::SizeF(scale, scale), center));
    pRT->DrawTextW(glyphStr, 1, fmt.Get(), D2D1::RectF(0.f, 0.f, glyphCenterX * 2.f, h), brush.Get());

    // Fixed chevron-down, mirrored to the right of center at the glyph's own
    // vertical center -- same hand-drawn two-line technique as
    // DrawSplitButtonChevronGlyph, sized proportional to the button instead
    // of DPI-scaled absolute pixels. Drawn INSIDE the same transform as the
    // glyph above (pivoted at the glyph's center) so it pops/settles as one
    // coherent unit with the icon instead of staying visually static.
    if (needsChevron) {
        const float cx = w * 0.5f + pairOffset;
        const float cy = centerY;
        const float dx = std::max(1.7f, w * 0.095f);
        const float dy = std::max(1.1f, h * 0.06f);
        const float stroke = std::max(1.0f, std::min(w, h) * 0.05f);
        pRT->DrawLine(D2D1::Point2F(cx - dx, cy - dy), D2D1::Point2F(cx, cy + dy), brush.Get(), stroke);
        pRT->DrawLine(D2D1::Point2F(cx + dx, cy - dy), D2D1::Point2F(cx, cy + dy), brush.Get(), stroke);
    }

    pRT->SetTransform(D2D1::Matrix3x2F::Identity());

    if (FAILED(pRT->EndDraw()))
        drawGdiFallback();
}

// Same style match as IsClassicPlacesBarToolbar, minus the kPropertyDialogDarkModeMarker
// requirement -- lets ClassicDlgToolbarSubclassProc (installed unconditionally,
// works in light mode too) recognize the places bar even when PropertyDialogSubclassProc
// (installed later, dark mode only, via ApplyPropertyDialogDarkMode) never ran at all.
// Whichever of the two subclasses is first in the chain for a given
// NM_CUSTOMDRAW answers it directly (both call the same PaintClassicPlacesBarItem,
// so which one wins doesn't change the result) -- deliberately not relying on a
// specific subclass-chain order here, since SetWindowSubclass's ordering isn't
// something this code needs to get right to behave correctly either way.
static bool IsClassicPlacesBarToolbarAnyMode(HWND hwndFrom)
{
    if (!hwndFrom)
        return false;
    wchar_t cls[32] = {};
    if (!GetClassNameW(hwndFrom, cls, ARRAYSIZE(cls)) || _wcsicmp(cls, L"ToolbarWindow32") != 0)
        return false;
    constexpr LONG_PTR kNeeded =
        WS_CHILD | WS_VISIBLE | WS_TABSTOP |
        TBSTYLE_TOOLTIPS | TBSTYLE_WRAPABLE | TBSTYLE_FLAT |
        TBSTYLE_CUSTOMERASE | TBSTYLE_TRANSPARENT |
        CCS_TOP | CCS_NORESIZE | CCS_NOPARENTALIGN | CCS_NODIVIDER;
    LONG_PTR style = GetWindowLongPtrW(hwndFrom, GWL_STYLE);
    if ((style & kNeeded) != kNeeded)
        return false;
    HWND root = GetAncestor(hwndFrom, GA_ROOT);
    wchar_t rootCls[32] = {};
    return root && GetClassNameW(root, rootCls, ARRAYSIZE(rootCls)) &&
           _wcsicmp(rootCls, L"#32770") == 0;
}

// Per-(toolbar HWND, command) state -- mirrors g_buttonPopAnims's keying
// (not the Explorer nav pane's single global slot) so multiple dialogs/
// windows animating their places bar at once never fight over one slot.
// CHECKED is mutually exclusive across the 5 buttons (confirmed via the
// diagnostic probe), so one checked command + one in-flight wipe per
// toolbar is enough -- no per-command map needed here.
struct PlacesBarState {
    bool     everObserved   = false;
    UINT_PTR checkedCommand = 0; // 0 = none checked
    UINT_PTR animCommand    = 0; // command mid-wipe, 0 = none
    DOUBLE   animStart      = 0.0;
    DOUBLE   animDuration   = 0.0;
};
static std::unordered_map<HWND, PlacesBarState> g_placesBarState;
static std::mutex g_placesBarStateMutex;
static void PlacesBarDWriteCacheClear();

static constexpr UINT     kPlacesBarAnimTimerId = 0x5A4E06;

static LRESULT CALLBACK PlacesBarAnimSubclassProc(HWND hwnd, UINT msg, WPARAM wp, LPARAM lp,
    DWORD_PTR)
{
    if (msg == WM_TIMER && wp == kPlacesBarAnimTimerId) {
        bool stillActive = false;
        UINT_PTR animCommand = 0;
        {
            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(g_placesBarStateMutex);
            auto it = g_placesBarState.find(hwnd);
            if (it != g_placesBarState.end() && it->second.animCommand != 0) {
                animCommand = it->second.animCommand;
                DOUBLE elapsed = TimerGetSeconds() - it->second.animStart;
                bool finished = elapsed >= it->second.animDuration;
                if (finished) it->second.animCommand = 0;
                else stillActive = true;
            }
        }
        if (animCommand != 0) {
            int idx = (int)SendMessageW(hwnd, TB_COMMANDTOINDEX, animCommand, 0);
            RECT rc = {};
            if (idx >= 0 && SendMessageW(hwnd, TB_GETITEMRECT, idx, (LPARAM)&rc)) {
                RedrawWindow(hwnd, &rc, nullptr,
                    RDW_INVALIDATE | RDW_NOERASE | RDW_NOCHILDREN | RDW_UPDATENOW);
            }
        }
        if (!stillActive) KillTimer(hwnd, kPlacesBarAnimTimerId);
        return 0;
    }
    if (msg == WM_NCDESTROY) {
        KillTimer(hwnd, kPlacesBarAnimTimerId);
        bool empty = false;
        {
            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(g_placesBarStateMutex);
            g_placesBarState.erase(hwnd);
            empty = g_placesBarState.empty();
        }
        if (empty)
            PlacesBarDWriteCacheClear();
        RemovePropW(hwnd, kPropGlyphEraseWarm);
        WindhawkUtils::RemoveWindowSubclassFromAnyThread(
            hwnd, PlacesBarAnimSubclassProc);
    }
    return DefSubclassProc(hwnd, msg, wp, lp);
}

// Detects a genuine checked-item change (this button just became the
// "current location" indicator) and starts its bespoke wipe-to-Filled
// animation, same trigger shape as the nav pane's isNewSelection check --
// the very first observation (dialog just opened, already on a shortcut
// location) sets state directly with no animation, only later transitions
// animate. Always (re)installs the subclass, even when nothing animates
// this call, so WM_NCDESTROY cleanup of g_placesBarState is guaranteed for
// every places bar ever painted, not just ones that happened to animate --
// SetWindowSubclass is a no-op/update when already installed, so this is
// cheap to call every item-paint.
static void PlacesBarTrigger(HWND hwnd, UINT_PTR command, bool checked, wchar_t glyphCh)
{
    if (g_pillUnloading.load(std::memory_order_acquire) ||
        !WindhawkUtils::SetWindowSubclassFromAnyThread(
            hwnd, PlacesBarAnimSubclassProc, 0)) {
        return;
    }

    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(g_placesBarStateMutex);
    auto& st = g_placesBarState[hwnd];
    if (checked && st.checkedCommand != command) {
        bool skipAnim = !st.everObserved;
        st.everObserved   = true;
        st.checkedCommand = command;
        if (!skipAnim && SysAnimationsEnabled()) {
            DOUBLE dur = PlacesBarWipeDuration(glyphCh);
            if (dur > 0.0) {
                st.animCommand  = command;
                st.animStart    = TimerGetSeconds();
                st.animDuration = dur;
                SetTimer(hwnd, kPlacesBarAnimTimerId, 16, nullptr);
            }
        }
    } else if (!checked && st.checkedCommand == command) {
        st.checkedCommand = 0;
        st.everObserved   = true;
    }
}

static void PlacesBarCleanup()
{
    std::vector<HWND> owners;
    {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(g_placesBarStateMutex);
        owners.reserve(g_placesBarState.size());
        for (const auto& [hwnd, state] : g_placesBarState) {
            (void)state;
            owners.push_back(hwnd);
        }
        g_placesBarState.clear();
    }
    for (HWND hwnd : owners) {
        if (IsWindow(hwnd)) {
            KillTimer(hwnd, kPlacesBarAnimTimerId);
            WindhawkUtils::RemoveWindowSubclassFromAnyThread(
                hwnd, PlacesBarAnimSubclassProc);
        }
    }
    PlacesBarDWriteCacheClear();
}

// Dedicated word-wrapped, center-aligned DirectWrite format for the
// places bar's button labels (Inicio/Area de Trabalho/...) -- distinct from
// TravelBandEnsureDWFormat, which is single-char/no-wrap and hardcoded to
// the Segoe icon font, not a real UI font.
static Microsoft::WRL::ComPtr<IDWriteFactory>    g_placesBarDwFactory;
static Microsoft::WRL::ComPtr<IDWriteTextFormat> g_placesBarLabelFmt;
static int  g_placesBarLabelFmtSize = 0;
static UINT g_placesBarLabelFmtDpi  = 0;
static std::mutex g_placesBarDwMutex;

static Microsoft::WRL::ComPtr<IDWriteTextFormat> PlacesBarEnsureLabelFormat(int size, UINT dpi)
{
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(g_placesBarDwMutex);
    if (g_placesBarLabelFmt && g_placesBarLabelFmtSize == size &&
        g_placesBarLabelFmtDpi == dpi)
        return g_placesBarLabelFmt;
    if (!g_placesBarDwFactory) {
        IDWriteFactory* raw = nullptr;
        if (FAILED(DWriteCreateFactory(DWRITE_FACTORY_TYPE_SHARED, __uuidof(IDWriteFactory),
                reinterpret_cast<IUnknown**>(&raw))) || !raw)
            return {};
        g_placesBarDwFactory.Attach(raw);
    }
    const wchar_t* fonts[] = {
        L"Segoe UI Variable Display",
        L"Segoe UI",
    };
    Microsoft::WRL::ComPtr<IDWriteTextFormat> fmt = CreateSegoeVariableAwareTextFormat(
        g_placesBarDwFactory.Get(), fonts, ARRAYSIZE(fonts), DWRITE_FONT_WEIGHT_NORMAL,
        (float)size, dpi);
    if (!fmt)
        return {};
    fmt->SetTextAlignment(DWRITE_TEXT_ALIGNMENT_CENTER);
    fmt->SetParagraphAlignment(DWRITE_PARAGRAPH_ALIGNMENT_NEAR);
    fmt->SetWordWrapping(DWRITE_WORD_WRAPPING_WRAP);
    g_placesBarLabelFmt = fmt;
    g_placesBarLabelFmtSize = size;
    g_placesBarLabelFmtDpi = dpi;
    return fmt;
}

static void PlacesBarDWriteCacheClear()
{
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(g_placesBarDwMutex);
    g_placesBarLabelFmt.Reset();
    g_placesBarDwFactory.Reset();
    g_placesBarLabelFmtSize = 0;
    g_placesBarLabelFmtDpi = 0;
}

// Natural wrapped height of `label` at `fmt`'s size within `maxWidth` --
// used to center the icon+text pair as a single group (see PaintClassic
// PlacesBarItem) instead of splitting the button into fixed icon/text
// bands regardless of how many lines the label actually wraps to.
static float PlacesBarMeasureTextHeight(const wchar_t* label, IDWriteTextFormat* fmt, float maxWidth)
{
    if (!fmt || !label || !label[0])
        return 0.0f;
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(g_placesBarDwMutex);
    if (!g_placesBarDwFactory)
        return 0.0f;
    Microsoft::WRL::ComPtr<IDWriteTextLayout> layout;
    if (FAILED(g_placesBarDwFactory->CreateTextLayout(label, (UINT32)wcslen(label), fmt,
            maxWidth, 1000.0f, &layout)) || !layout)
        return 0.0f;
    DWRITE_TEXT_METRICS metrics = {};
    if (FAILED(layout->GetMetrics(&metrics)))
        return 0.0f;
    return metrics.height;
}

static float PlacesBarMeasureTextHeightGdi(HDC hdc, const wchar_t* label,
    float maxWidth)
{
    if (!hdc || !label || !label[0] || maxWidth <= 0.f)
        return 0.f;
    RECT measure = { 0, 0, (LONG)maxWidth, 0 };
    return DrawTextW(hdc, label, -1, &measure,
        DT_CALCRECT | DT_CENTER | DT_WORDBREAK | DT_NOPREFIX)
        ? (float)(measure.bottom - measure.top) : 0.f;
}

// Buttons are big (102x93 in the observed layout), rendered in one of two
// layouts: "paired" (icon+label centered together as one group -- the rest
// state for any shortcut that isn't the current location) and "settled"
// (label gone, icon alone dead-center -- the current-location state, same
// idea as the Microsoft Store/Settings nav collapse). `settleT` interpolates
// between them: 0 = fully paired, 1 = fully settled. On the click that makes
// an item the current location, settleT animates over a short, fixed
// kSettleDur -- independent of (and faster than) the bespoke SVG content
// wipe below, so the layout snaps into place quickly while the icon's own
// shape transformation keeps playing in its final, centered spot. Returns
// false (drawing nothing) for an unrecognized command so the caller can
// fall back to the control's own default draw instead of leaving the
// button blank.
static bool PaintClassicPlacesBarItem(HWND toolbarHwnd, const NMCUSTOMDRAW* cd)
{
    if (!cd || !cd->hdc)
        return false;
    const wchar_t* glyphStr = PlacesBarGlyphForCommand((UINT_PTR)cd->dwItemSpec);
    if (!glyphStr)
        return false;

    RECT rc = cd->rc;
    if (rc.right <= rc.left || rc.bottom <= rc.top)
        return false;
    const float w = (float)(rc.right - rc.left);
    const float h = (float)(rc.bottom - rc.top);
    const float scale = (float)DpiForPaintHdc(cd->hdc) / 96.f;

    const bool hot       = (cd->uItemState & CDIS_HOT) != 0;
    const bool pressed   = (cd->uItemState & CDIS_SELECTED) != 0;
    const bool disabled  = (cd->uItemState & CDIS_DISABLED) != 0;
    const bool checkedNow = (cd->uItemState & CDIS_CHECKED) != 0;

    PlacesBarTrigger(toolbarHwnd, (UINT_PTR)cd->dwItemSpec, checkedNow, glyphStr[0]);

    bool filled = false, wiping = false;
    float wipeElapsedSec = 0.0f;
    {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(g_placesBarStateMutex);
        auto it = g_placesBarState.find(toolbarHwnd);
        if (it != g_placesBarState.end()) {
            filled = (it->second.checkedCommand == (UINT_PTR)cd->dwItemSpec);
            if (it->second.animCommand == (UINT_PTR)cd->dwItemSpec) {
                DOUBLE elapsed = TimerGetSeconds() - it->second.animStart;
                if (elapsed < it->second.animDuration) {
                    wiping = true;
                    wipeElapsedSec = (float)elapsed;
                }
            }
        }
    }

    HWND ctxHwnd = g_tlsPaintHwnd ? g_tlsPaintHwnd : WindowFromDC(cd->hdc);
    const bool dark = IsDarkForExcludedAwarePaint(ctxHwnd);
    COLORREF neutralClr = disabled
        ? (dark ? RGB(120, 120, 120) : RGB(160, 160, 160))
        : (dark ? RGB(255, 255, 255) : RGB(25, 26, 26));
    // Checked (current-location) item gets the same accent-color treatment
    // as the Explorer nav pane's selected item, on top of the Normal->Filled
    // shape change -- applies to both icon and label.
    COLORREF itemClr = (filled && !disabled) ? GetAccentIndicator() : neutralClr;

    // EaseInOutCubic's gentle start avoids the instant-max-velocity snap
    // EaseOutCubic has at t=0, reading as smoother despite the short duration.
    static constexpr float kSettleDur = 0.15f; // fast layout snap, independent of the slower SVG wipe below
    float settleT = filled ? 1.0f : 0.0f;
    if (wiping)
        settleT = EaseInOutCubic(std::min(1.0f, wipeElapsedSec / kSettleDur));

    const float iconSize = std::min(w * 0.5f, h * 0.46f);
    const float gap = h * 0.05f;

    wchar_t label[128] = {};
    SendMessageW(toolbarHwnd, TB_GETBUTTONTEXTW, cd->dwItemSpec, (LPARAM)label);
    // Label size kept proportional to the icon so it doesn't read as too
    // small next to it.
    int labelSize = std::max(9, (int)(h * 0.16f));
    auto fmt = label[0] ? PlacesBarEnsureLabelFormat(labelSize, DpiForPaintHdc(cd->hdc)) :
                          Microsoft::WRL::ComPtr<IDWriteTextFormat>{};

    // Only needed while the label might still be visible -- skip the
    // DirectWrite measurement once fully settled (label gone).
    float textH = 0.f;
    if (label[0] && settleT < 0.999f) {
        if (fmt)
            textH = PlacesBarMeasureTextHeight(label, fmt.Get(), w - 4.0f);
        if (textH <= 0.f)
            textH = PlacesBarMeasureTextHeightGdi(cd->hdc, label, w - 4.0f);
    }

    // Paired layout: icon+label centered together as one group. Settled
    // layout: icon alone, dead-center of the square. Both share the same
    // horizontal centering (iconSize is constant), so only the icon's Y
    // and the label's opacity need to change between them.
    const float groupH = iconSize + (textH > 0.0f ? gap + textH : 0.0f);
    const float pairedIconTop  = rc.top + (h - groupH) / 2.0f;
    const float settledIconTop = rc.top + (h - iconSize) / 2.0f;
    const float iconTop  = pairedIconTop + (settledIconTop - pairedIconTop) * settleT;
    const float iconLeft = rc.left + (w - iconSize) / 2.0f;
    RECT iconRc = {
        (LONG)iconLeft, (LONG)iconTop,
        (LONG)(iconLeft + iconSize), (LONG)(iconTop + iconSize)
    };
    // Label stays at its paired position (doesn't track the moving icon)
    // and just fades out -- simpler and avoids the (already-invisible-by-
    // then) text drifting past the settled icon's bounds.
    const float textTop = pairedIconTop - rc.top + iconSize + gap;
    const float textAlpha = 1.0f - settleT;
    bool labelDrawn = false;

    FPUGuard fpu;

    // Pass 1: hover/pressed fill + text label share one render target --
    // both are plain 2D fills/text over the full button rect.
    {
        Microsoft::WRL::ComPtr<ID2D1DCRenderTarget> pRT;
        if (SUCCEEDED(CreateBoundD2DRenderTarget(cd->hdc, &rc, g_d2dFactory, &pRT))) {
            Microsoft::WRL::ComPtr<ID2D1SolidColorBrush> brush;
            pRT->CreateSolidColorBrush(D2D1::ColorF(0.f, 0.f, 0.f, 0.f), &brush);
            if (brush) {
                pRT->BeginDraw();
                pRT->SetTextAntialiasMode(D2D1_TEXT_ANTIALIAS_MODE_GRAYSCALE);
                // Active (checked) item keeps its rounded background even at
                // rest, not just on hover/press. Every tier (hover, press,
                // active-at-rest) uses the same accent/neutral choice as the
                // Explorer nav pane's own selection+hover background
                // (DrawRoundedItemBg / g_settings.NeutralSelection) -- only
                // the alpha differs between them.
                if (!disabled && (hot || pressed || filled)) {
                    const float hoverAlpha = dark ? (pressed ? 0.14f : 0.20f) : (pressed ? 0.06f : 0.09f);
                    const float restActiveAlpha = dark ? 0.16f : 0.08f;
                    const float a = (hot || pressed) ? hoverAlpha : restActiveAlpha;
                    D2D1_COLOR_F fillColor;
                    if (g_settings.NeutralSelection) {
                        const float base = dark ? 1.f : 0.f;
                        fillColor = D2D1::ColorF(base, base, base, a);
                    } else {
                        const COLORREF ac = GetAccentIndicator();
                        fillColor = D2D1::ColorF(GetRValue(ac) / 255.f, GetGValue(ac) / 255.f,
                                                  GetBValue(ac) / 255.f, a);
                    }
                    brush->SetColor(fillColor);
                    const float inset = 1.2f * scale;
                    const float radius = std::min(w, h) * 0.10f;
                    pRT->FillRoundedRectangle(
                        D2D1::RoundedRect(D2D1::RectF(inset, inset, w - inset, h - inset), radius, radius),
                        brush.Get());
                }
                bool attemptedLabel = false;
                if (fmt && textAlpha > 0.01f) {
                    brush->SetColor(D2D1::ColorF(GetRValue(itemClr) / 255.f,
                                                  GetGValue(itemClr) / 255.f,
                                                  GetBValue(itemClr) / 255.f, textAlpha));
                    pRT->DrawTextW(label, (UINT32)wcslen(label), fmt.Get(),
                        D2D1::RectF(1.6f * scale, textTop, w - 1.6f * scale, h - 1.6f * scale), brush.Get());
                    attemptedLabel = true;
                }
                // Accent pill at the left edge -- ported from the regedit
                // treeview's own selection pill (same PILL_H_FRAC constant
                // and EaseOutBackGentle expand curve). Only for the active
                // item; its scale-in reuses the wipe's own elapsed clock as
                // a fast, independent sub-animation (same idea as settleT
                // above), so it pops in alongside the icon settle instead
                // of needing separate trigger/state tracking.
                if (!disabled && filled) {
                    static constexpr float kPlacesBarPillExpandDur = 0.20f;
                    float pillScale = wiping
                        ? EaseOutBackGentle(std::min(
                            1.0f, wipeElapsedSec / kPlacesBarPillExpandDur))
                        : 1.0f;
                    if (pillScale > 0.001f) {
                        const UINT dpi = GetDpiForWindow(toolbarHwnd);
                        const float pillW = (float)MulDiv(3, (int)dpi, 96);
                        const float pillHalf = (h * PILL_H_FRAC / 2.0f) * pillScale;
                        const float cy = h * 0.5f;
                        const float pTop = cy - pillHalf;
                        const float pBot = cy + pillHalf;
                        if (pBot > pTop + 0.5f) {
                            const float pillLeft = 1.2f * scale; // same inset as the rounded bg fill
                            const D2D1_RECT_F pillRect = D2D1::RectF(pillLeft, pTop, pillLeft + pillW, pBot);
                            const COLORREF ac = GetAccentIndicator();
                            if (g_settings.AccentGradients) {
                                COLORREF baseC = GetAccentFromPalette(12);
                                D2D1_GRADIENT_STOP stops[2] = {
                                    { 0.f, D2D1::ColorF(GetRValue(ac) / 255.f, GetGValue(ac) / 255.f, GetBValue(ac) / 255.f) },
                                    { 1.f, D2D1::ColorF(GetRValue(baseC) / 255.f, GetGValue(baseC) / 255.f, GetBValue(baseC) / 255.f) }
                                };
                                Microsoft::WRL::ComPtr<ID2D1GradientStopCollection> sc;
                                Microsoft::WRL::ComPtr<ID2D1LinearGradientBrush> gb;
                                if (SUCCEEDED(pRT->CreateGradientStopCollection(stops, 2, &sc)) &&
                                    SUCCEEDED(pRT->CreateLinearGradientBrush(
                                        D2D1::LinearGradientBrushProperties(
                                            D2D1::Point2F(pillLeft, pTop), D2D1::Point2F(pillLeft, pBot)),
                                        sc.Get(), &gb)))
                                    pRT->FillRoundedRectangle(
                                        D2D1::RoundedRect(pillRect, pillW * 0.5f, pillW * 0.5f), gb.Get());
                            } else {
                                brush->SetColor(D2D1::ColorF(GetRValue(ac) / 255.f, GetGValue(ac) / 255.f,
                                                              GetBValue(ac) / 255.f, 1.f));
                                pRT->FillRoundedRectangle(
